Add 2000ml of water to the steamer, heat it until the water surface continues to bubble (100°C) 10. Place the bowl with the ingredients into the steamer, and cover the pot with the lid. 11. Keep steaming over medium heat for 60 Minutes (the heat is kept at a sustainable boiling level, about 600W heating power) 12. After the time is up, insert a chopstick into the center of the meat. If it can penetrate easily without obvious resistance, it means it is steamed. 13. If this state is not reached, continue to heat for 10 - 15 minutes until the meat is soft and the fat oozes out. 14. Take it out on a plate and serve.

Additional content: - If you want to make your own rice noodles, put 150g of rice into a pot, stir-fry over medium-low heat until slightly yellow (about 8 minutes), then add 1g of dried chili peppers, 1g of Sichuan peppercorns, and 0.5g of star anise. Stir-fry until fragrant and crush into pieces with a food processor, sieve and set aside. - During steaming, if the water level is 1cm lower than the height of the bottom of the pot, add 500ml of hot water (above 90°C) immediately to maintain sufficient steam.

Cut the pork belly into half-centimeter-thick slices. If it is too thin, it will be steamed dry. If it is too thick, it will not be easy to taste. Drain the water before mixing it with the rice noodles.
You can add a small amount of water to moisten the steamed meat rice noodles and let it sit for five minutes. It will not become dry and hard after steaming.
Put potatoes or pumpkin on the bottom of the bowl, place the meat slices on top, and steam over medium heat for 60 to 90 minutes. Chopsticks can be inserted easily.

Case: It was the birthday of an elderly person in the family. She cut the pork belly into thick slices and mixed it with rice noodles in advance. She put potatoes on the bottom of the bowl and steamed it in a pot. When it was out of the pot, it was inverted and sprinkled with chopped green onions. The meat was soft and glutinous but not greasy, and the potatoes absorbed oil and fragrant. The elderly said it was more homely than the ones in restaurants outside.

items.title: Sweet and Sour Pork Ribs
items.core: Sweet and sour pork ribs is a popular traditional dish that is sweet and sour, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. Spare ribs are rich in high-quality protein and calcium and have a good nourishing effect. This dish involves multiple steps such as blanching, frying, frying the sugar and collecting the juice. It has certain requirements for heat and seasoning. It is not particularly suitable for novices, but the success rate is higher if you follow the optimized process. Estimated production time is approximately 45 minutes.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Spare ribs - White sugar - Cooking oil - Light soy sauce - Oyster sauce - Dark soy sauce - Chicken essence - Ginger slices - Sesame seeds - Tomato paste - Balsamic vinegar - Five-spice powder

Calculation: per serving: - 300 g of ribs - 30 g of white sugar - 300–350 ml of cooking oil (the amount of oil needs to be adjusted according to the size of the pot, if used for deep frying, it should be enough to cover 2/3 of the ribs) - 5 ml of light soy sauce - 5 ml of oyster sauce - 5 ml of dark soy sauce - 2 g of chicken essence - 2 slices of ginger - 2 g of sesame seeds - Tomato sauce 10 g - Balsamic vinegar 5 ml - Five-spice powder 0.5 g

Operation: 1. Put the ribs and ginger slices into cold water, heat over high heat until the water boils and a lot of foam appears, then turn to medium heat. When the water continues to boil, turn to low heat and blanch for 2-3 minutes, remove and set aside. 2. Wash the ribs 2-3 times with boiling water to ensure the blood foam is completely removed. 3. Pour enough cooking oil into the pot for deep frying (the amount of oil depends on the size of the pot, it is recommended to be about 300 ml for general household use). After the oil temperature rises to about 170°C, fry the ribs for 3-5 minutes until the surface turns slightly golden. Remove and control the oil. 4. Take another clean pot, heat 50 ml of hot water over low heat, add 30 g of white sugar, and stir gently until the sugar is completely dissolved and turns slightly light yellow. The point of this step is to observe the dissolution of the sugar without relying too much on the color change. 5. Pour the fried pork ribs into the pot with the sugar water and stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds. Add 5 ml of balsamic vinegar, 5 ml of light soy sauce, 5 ml of oyster sauce, 2 g of chicken essence, 10 g of tomato sauce, and 0.5 g of five-spice powder. Stir-fry again for 30 seconds to evenly coat the ribs with the seasoning. Then add boiling water until the ribs are just covered. 6. After boiling the liquid in the pot over high heat, add 5 ml of dark soy sauce to color and reduce the juice quickly. If the ribs are large, you can turn to low heat and simmer for 5-10 minutes to better absorb the flavor. Do not simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes to avoid damaging the taste. 7. Remove from the pot, put on a plate, sprinkle with 2 g of sesame seeds, and enjoy.

Additional content: - When frying the ribs, you can lightly sprinkle a small amount of dry starch on the surface of the ribs according to the actual situation to enhance the crispy texture. - Pay attention to the change in heat when blanching: After putting the cold water in the pot, first use high heat until the water boils and the foam is rich, then turn to medium heat, and finally turn to low heat to blanch the water; wash with boiling water after blanching to avoid the meat becoming woody due to excessive temperature difference. - The key to step four is to ensure that the sugar is completely dissolved. There is no need to rely too much on color changes. - When the sauce is reduced, stir-fry quickly to coat the ribs evenly with the seasoning to avoid loss of taste caused by long-term stewing.
Blanch the pork ribs in a pot under cold water. After the water boils, skim the foam and cook for two minutes. Remove and rinse with warm water.
Use low heat to stir-fry the sugar color. When the sugar liquid turns amber, remove the ribs immediately. If the color is too dark, it will become bitter.
Sweet and sour sauce can be mixed with light soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a ratio of 1:2:2. When collecting the juice, stir frequently until the juice is thickened.

Case: Before having a dinner with friends, he blanched the ribs and fried them until slightly brown. When frying the sugar, he kept an eye on the color of the pot. He poured vinegar and sugar to reduce the juice. The finished product was bright red, sweet and sour, and not fishy when bitten. Everyone mixed the last bit of soup with the rice and ate it cleanly.

items.title: Sweet and Sour Pork
items.core: Sweet and sour pork is sweet and sour, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. It is a popular home-cooked flavor and is common in many regional cuisines. The pork tenderloin provides high-quality protein, but the breading, frying, and sweet-and-sour sauce make the overall caloric high. When making it, you need to master the heat of marinating, re-frying and seasoning, which is a bit challenging for novices. It is recommended to prepare the ingredients in advance and cook it in one go. It takes about 45 minutes to an hour from prep to serving.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Tenderloin - Vinegar - White sugar - Starch - Eggs - Light soy sauce - Cooking wine - Oyster sauce - Tomato sauce - White pepper - Salt

Calculation: per serving: - Tenderloin 500g - Vinegar 10g - White sugar 30g - Starch 50g - Eggs 50g - Light soy sauce 10ml - Cooking wine 20g - Oyster sauce 10g - Tomato sauce 30ml - White pepper 5g - Salt 10g

Operation: 1. Marinate the meat: Cut the pork tenderloin into thick slices first, pat it with the back of the knife to loosen the meat. Cut into strips as thick as a finger, add cooking wine, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, salt, white pepper, and an egg, rub the meat evenly with your hands, and marinate for more than 20 minutes. 2. Make the sauce: ketchup + 10g vinegar + 30g sugar + 150ml water, stir until the sugar melts, set aside. 3. Coat in flour: Coat all the flour before frying, so that you won’t be in a hurry when frying. Prepare a large bowl, put starch in it, and coat each strip of meat fully with starch. 4. Fry: Fry the tenderloin at 160 degrees Celsius. You can put a dry chopstick in the oil to test it. If there are small bubbles around it, you can put it in the fryer. 5. Fry until the surface turns slightly yellow and can be taken out. Keep the heat on medium throughout. Then wait until the oil temperature rises to 200 degrees Celsius, pour the tenderloin in and fry it again. It only takes 40 seconds. The skin will be very crispy and you can take it out immediately. 6. Coat the sauce: Take another pot, put some base oil in the pot, pour the prepared sauce into it, cook until it bubbles, put the fried tenderloin in, and stir-fry so that each one is coated with the sauce. 7. Add the fried tenderloin, stir-fry, turn off the heat and serve.

Additional content: - Fry the tenderloin several times and pay attention to the heat, otherwise you will not achieve the effect of being charred on the outside and tender on the inside! - Go to the kitchen - Baidu Encyclopedia
Cut the tenderloin into finger-thick strips, add salt, cooking wine, and egg white, mix well, and marinate for fifteen minutes. It will become more tender after frying.
Fry in 60% oil for the first time until it is set, take it out and raise the oil temperature and fry again for 20 seconds to make the shell crispier.
The sweet and sour sauce is prepared in advance and the starch water is added. After the tenderloin is put into the pot, turn the heat quickly and the sauce will be out of the pot in ten seconds.

Case: For her child’s birthday dinner, she cut the tenderloin into strips, marinated them, rolled them in flour, fried them first and then fried them again. Finally, she poured in the sweet and sour sauce that had been prepared in advance and quickly stirred them in. The skin was crispy, and the sweet and sour sauce hung in the sauce. It was eaten up quickly after it was served.

items.title: Braised pig's trotters
items.core: Braised pig's trotters is a classic home-cooked dish with rich soup and soft and glutinous meat. It is salty and sweet and goes well with rice. Pig trotters are rich in collagen and protein and are rich in nutrients. This dish is challenging for novices, but the process can be simplified with the help of a pressure cooker, making it easier to get started if you have a certain cooking foundation. It takes approximately 1 hour from prep to completion.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Pig trotters - Bay leaves - Ginger - Green onion - Dark soy sauce - Cinnamon - Rock sugar - Cooking wine - Light soy sauce - Salt - Star anise - Edible oil

Calculation: One serving is just enough for 3-4 people. - Pig's trotters: 2~3 - Edible oil: 30ml - 2 bay leaves - 5 slices of ginger - Half green onion - 1 piece of cinnamon - 7-8 pieces of rock sugar - 30 ml of cooking wine - 20 ml of light soy sauce - 20 ml of dark soy sauce - 8 grams of salt - 4 star anise

Operation: Start making: 1. Put the pork trotters chopped by the enthusiastic stall owner into a pot of cold water, add 20 ml of cooking wine and green onion and ginger, and cook for 15 minutes to remove the blood. 2. Heat the cold oil in the pot, pour in 30ml of cooking oil, add 7-8 rock sugar, turn on low heat, and boil until it turns into sugar color. Use a spatula to crush the rock sugar and cook for about 2 minutes. 3. After it turns into sugar color, add the blanched pig's trotters, continue to stir-fry the pig's trotters over low heat until both sides of the pig's trotters are slightly yellow. 4. Add 2 bay leaves, 1 piece of cinnamon bark, 4 star anise, 20 ml of light soy sauce, 20 ml of dark soy sauce, 10 ml of cooking wine, 3 slices of ginger, and 8 grams of salt. Turn to medium heat and continue to stir-fry for 1 minute. 5. Add boiling or cold water, the water needs to cover the pig's trotters, cover the pot, and bring to a boil over high heat. After boiling, turn off the heat. 6. Pour all the ingredients in the pot into the pressure cooker. It will take 15 minutes to cook in the pressure cooker (if you don't have a pressure cooker, you can put it in the pot and cook it from high to low heat). 7. After 15 minutes, pour the ingredients from the pressure cooker into the wok, turn on high heat to reduce the juice. You can use chopsticks to taste the taste. If it is light, you can add 2~3g of salt. 8. The duration of the high fire to reduce the juice is calculated based on the water in the pot. Generally, 30 seconds is enough. It doesn’t matter if you leave a little more. The braised pig’s trotters soup is also very delicious
Additional Content
Blanch the pig's trotters and pluck the hair with tweezers. Boil the ginger slices with cooking wine to effectively remove the fishy smell and impurities.
After the pressure cooker is steamed, press it for 20 to 25 minutes until the chopsticks can penetrate it, then return it to the pot to collect the juice.
When the juice is collected, the soup should cover half of the pig's trotters. Stir frequently over medium-low heat to prevent the sugar-colored paste from becoming bitter.

Case: On the day of cooling down, he wanted to eat soft and rotten pig's trotters. He first used a pressure cooker to cook it for 20 minutes, then returned it to the wok and added light and dark soy sauce to reduce the juice. The pig's trotters were sticky to the mouth and had a rich sauce. It was served with rice and hot soup. It was a very satisfying meal.

items.title: Southern Style Braised Pork
items.core: This braised pork dish has a bright red color, the fat melts in your mouth, the lean meat is crispy and not burnt, and it is salty and sweet. It is a typical southern sweet flavor. Pork belly provides high-quality protein and rich collagen, and the spices can also remove fishy smell and warm the stomach. Although the preparation requires boiling the sugar and simmering, each step is clearly broken down and easy to understand, and even a novice can succeed by following the operation. The whole process can be served on the table in about 1.5 hours.
body: Necessary raw materials and tools: * Note: If possible, please try to sharpen the knife. * Tools: pot (casserole is suitable, aluminum pot is second, pressure cooker is also acceptable, it is best not to use iron pot or copper pot) * Main ingredient: pork belly * Accessory ingredients: oil, rock sugar, dark soy sauce, cooking wine, bay leaf, star anise, ginger, salt, green onion, boiling water, cold water, garlic, pepper

Calculation: One serving is just enough for 2-3 people (it is recommended to halve all doses for 1 person). - Pork belly: 1000g (about 2 pounds). Note: Raw meat shrinks and defatts severely after cooking. The final amount of meat produced is about enough for 2-3 people. If only 1 person is consuming it, it is recommended to halve the dosage of all ingredients. - Oil: 100-150ml, salad oil, lard, peanut oil can be used - Ginger: 6 slices - Shallot: about 30g (3-4 stalks), cut into white pieces and set aside - Garlic: about 25g (5-6 cloves), cut in the middle and set aside - Rock sugar: 50g (15 pieces of broken single crystal rock sugar about the size of your thumbnail). If 50g has been used to stir-fry the sugar color in the previous step, the 50g here is used for secondary seasoning during stewing. It can be adjusted to 30g according to the acceptance of "Southern sweetness". - White sugar: 30g - Dark soy sauce: 15ml - Cooking wine: total amount 30ml (20ml is used for blanching in the early stage to remove the fishy smell, and 10ml is used for stewing in the later stage to enhance the freshness) - Cold water: enough to cover the ingredients, depending on the size of the pot - Boiled water: enough to cover the ingredients, depending on the size of the pot - Bay leaves: 4 pieces - Star anise: 3 - Salt: 2-3g - Sichuan peppercorns: 10g

Operation: It is recommended to check the tutorial for stir-frying sugar color before this. 1. Do not cut the pork belly into small pieces, but cut it into large pieces (about 5-6cm wide) that can be put into the pot. 2. Slice the ginger (about 3mm thick per slice) 3. Bring boiling water to a boil 4. Just cold tap water 5. Cut the white part of the shallot into small pieces (scallions are best, green onions are also acceptable) 6. Cut the garlic in the middle and do not flatten it, otherwise it will be difficult to remove and the taste will be affected when the juice is finally collected. 7. Please divide the auxiliary ingredients into two "preparatory packages": - Package A (for removing fishy smell): 2 slices of ginger, 2 slices of green onion. - Bun B (for stewing): Put the remaining 4 slices of ginger, scallions, garlic cloves, peppercorns, star anise, and bay leaves into a small bowl and set aside. 8. Place large pieces of pork belly in a pot of cold water, add 20ml of cooking wine and package A (2 slices of ginger, 2 slices of green onion), cook for 15 minutes to remove the blood, take it out and wash it clean; 9. Take out the blanched pork belly, let it cool slightly (just don’t scald your hands), and cut into sides of about 3cm × 3cm × 3cm Cube pieces (the meat tightens after blanching, making it easier to cut into pieces than raw meat and the size of the finished product is more uniform. The final product is about 2.5cm when cut into 3cm pieces, which is the most suitable size for the mouth and easy to burn through) 10. Stir-fry the sugar color in a separate pot. Note: In this recipe, please use the "Operation 2" mentioned in it to make it, that is, when the sugar liquid bubbles densely, quickly add it to the Pour package B (ginger, scallions, garlic, peppercorns, star anise, bay leaves) into the pot and saute until fragrant. 11. After the aroma explodes (within about 5-10 seconds), do not add boiling water first, but immediately pour the blanched pork belly into the pot and stir-fry over high heat, so that the meat is evenly coated with sugar color and the fat is stir-fried. After the meat smells fragrant, pour boiling water until all the meat is covered, cover the pot, turn to medium-low heat and simmer for 50-60 minutes (40 minutes for a pressure cooker); 12. Add 10ml of cooking wine; 13. Cover the pot and cook until it boils, then open the lid every 25 minutes to remove the oil and foam floating on the surface; 14. When the height of the water is reduced to 3/5 of the highest height of the meat and the height of the bottom of the pot , turn to medium heat, remove all the ingredients except the meat and water, and start to reduce the juice; 15. Open the lid of the pot, and when the soup is almost gone, take it out of the pot and it becomes sticky (remember not to dry it out);
Additional Content
Cut the pork belly into three-centimeter cubes, blanch it in cold water, dry it, and fry until it is slightly brown on all sides, then stew it for more flavor.
When you see fine bubbles and maroon color in the fried sugar, eat the meat immediately. The heat will make it bitter.
Stew meat. Heat water to cover the meat surface. Add onions, ginger, star anise and a small amount of rice wine. Simmer over low heat for 60 minutes.

Case: When I returned home during the Qingming Festival, my mother fried the pork belly with rock sugar until it turned into jujube brown sugar color, stewed the pork belly until it was trembling, and finally cooked it over a high fire until it was bright and juicy.

items.title: Simple Braised Pork
items.core: This delicious home-cooked dish is red and shiny in color, soft and waxy in texture, fat but not greasy, and has a rich sauce flavor. It is particularly enjoyable when paired with rice. Pork belly provides high-quality protein and essential fatty acids, and with quail eggs or bean curds, the nutrition is more comprehensive. The recipe is quite beginner-friendly, and it takes about 1.5 hours from preparation to cooking.
body: Necessary materials and tools: - Note: If possible, please try to sharpen the knife. - Main ingredients: meat, eggs (optional), tofu skin (optional) - Accessories: ginger, rock sugar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, cooking wine, bay leaves, star anise, salt, water, green onions (remember to boil water)

Calculation: Before each production, you need to determine how many servings to make. One serving is just enough for 2-3 people. If only 1 person is serving, consider halving the ingredients. - Pork belly: about 3~4 pounds - Ginger: 6 pieces - Rock sugar: 15 grams (about 7 pieces) - Light soy sauce: 10ml - Dark soy sauce: 15ml - Cooking wine: 5ml - Boiled water: enough to cover the ingredients, 600ml-900ml is needed - Bay leaves: 3 pieces - Star anise: 2 pieces - Quail eggs (optional, if you don’t have quail eggs, you can use eggs of the same weight instead): 0-2 - Bean curd (optional): 0-80g - Salt: 2-3g

Operation: Raw material preparation: 1. Cut pork belly into large pieces (about 4.5cm, freeze for half an hour to an hour for better cutting) 2. Cut bean curd into 2cm width 3. Slice ginger (each slice is about 3mm thick) ) 4. Boil the water 5. Boil the quail eggs and prick them with a fork/toothpick (try to use as many as possible for the flavor) 6. The white part of the scallions will be white. Start making: 1. Put the chopped pork belly in a cold water pot, add cooking wine and scallions and ginger, cook for 15 minutes to remove the blood 2. Add two slices of ginger to the pot to enhance the flavor 3. Turn on medium-low heat and add the pork belly directly. No cooking oil is needed. Fry all six sides of each piece of pork belly until oil comes out. 4. Pour out the fried oil and set aside, push the pork belly to one side, add 15g of rock sugar, and stir-fry until the rock sugar melts; 5. After melting, stir-fry the pork belly and rock sugar until they are combined and colored, add - 10ml of light soy sauce - 15ml of dark soy sauce - 5ml of cooking wine - Stir-fry until browned; 6. Add boiled water and simmer for 40 minutes (those with poor knife skills may cut too large, please extend the stewing time), and add - 2 pieces of ginger - 3 pieces of bay leaves - 2 star anise 7. Cover the pot and cook until boiling, add the cooked quail eggs and bean skins with holes, turn on medium-low heat and wait for 40 minutes. (Stir appropriately in the middle to prevent sticking to the pot); 8. Open the lid of the pot, and when the soup is almost gone, turn on high heat to reduce the juice (remember not to let it dry); 9. Add 2-3g of salt, stir-fry, and it is ready to serve.
Additional Content
Cut the pork belly into small pieces and add it directly to the cold pan. Slowly stir-fry the oil over low heat until the surface turns slightly brown before seasoning.
The amount of rock sugar used is about half of that of light soy sauce. Melt it first and then stir-fry. This will make the meat more colorful and shiny.
Quail eggs can be boiled and shelled in advance. After the meat is tender, put it in and simmer for ten minutes to make it more delicious.

Case: He wanted to save trouble on a weekday night, so he stir-fried the pork belly in a non-stick pan, added soy sauce, rock sugar and quail eggs and simmered it together. After more than an hour, the meat became soft and glutinous, and the eggs soaked up the sauce. Even the children took the initiative to add half a bowl of rice.

items.title: Braised chicken wings
items.core: Braised chicken wings are a home-cooked dish. They are salty and sweet, bright red in color, and the meat is tender and easy to fall off the bones. Chicken wings are rich in high-quality protein and collagen, and their nutrients are easy to absorb. The preparation difficulty is moderate, and novices can master it smoothly by following the steps. It takes about 40 minutes from preparing the ingredients to taking it out of the pan.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Fresh chicken wings (recommended to choose chicken wings, the meat is more tender) - Ginger slices (ginger is recommended, the fishy removal effect is better) - Onion segments (the white part of green onions is recommended, the fragrance is stronger) - Garlic - Bay leaves - Star anise - Dried chili pepper (optional, if you don't like spicy food, you can omit it) - Rock sugar - Rice wine or cooking wine (choose one of the two, rice wine has a more mellow flavor) - Light soy sauce - Dark soy sauce - Salt - White sugar - Pepper (white pepper is recommended, the spiciness is mild) - White sesame seeds (cooked) - Green onions (for garnishing)

Calculation: Before each production, you need to determine how many servings to make. One serving is enough for 3-4 people. Each serving: - 500g fresh chicken wings (about 8-10 pieces, a single chicken wing is about 50-60g) - 4-5 slices of ginger (about 10g, slice thickness is about 2mm) - 2-3 green onion sections (about 15g, each section is about 3cm long) - 3-4 cloves of garlic (about 15g) - 1 bay leaf - 1 star anise - 2 dried chili peppers (optional, about 5g, omit if you don’t like spicy food) - 15g rock sugar (granular rock sugar) - 35ml rice wine or cooking wine - 15ml light soy sauce - 5ml dark soy sauce - salt 3g - white sugar 2g - pepper 1g - white sesame seeds 3g - chopped green onion 5g - cooking oil 10-15ml

Operation: 1. Wash the chicken wings. Use a knife to make three cuts in the thick part of the chicken wings and prick the back once to facilitate the flavoring. 2. If the chicken wings are not fresh, soak them in ginger water for 10-20 minutes after cutting. 3. Prepare 10g ginger slices (3-4 slices) and 15g green onion segments (2-3 segments); break up 3-4 cloves of garlic (about 15g) with a knife (no need to chop); prepare 1 bay leaf, 1 star anise, and 2 dried chili peppers (optional) for later use. 4. Turn the pot over high heat, add water to cover all the chicken wings, put the cooked chicken wings under cold water, add 20ml of rice wine or cooking wine, and 2 slices of ginger (about 5g), turn up the heat and bring to a boil. After boiling, keep the heat on and continue to cook for 2-3 minutes, and skim off the foam. 5. After cooking, take out the chicken wings, wash them twice with warm water, thoroughly remove the blood foam, drain the water and set aside. 6. Take another pot, heat it up and add 10-15ml cooking oil. 7. When the oil temperature reaches 50%, add 15g of rock sugar, turn up the heat and simmer the rock sugar until it is completely melted. After the rock sugar melts and changes color, turn to low heat and continue frying until the rock sugar turns maroon red. Immediately add the chicken wings that have been dried and stir-fry quickly for 1-2 minutes, so that each chicken wing is evenly coated in sugar color. 8. Add the prepared 1 bay leaf, 1 star anise, 2 dried chili peppers (optional), the remaining 2 ginger slices (about 5g), 15g scallions, and chopped garlic, and continue to stir-fry for 30 seconds until the aroma of the spices is completely released. 9. Pour 15ml cooking wine or rice wine and 15ml light soy sauce along the edge of the pot and stir-fry quickly for 10 seconds. 10. Add warm water (water temperature is about 50-60℃), enough water to slightly cover all the chicken wings. 11. Add 5ml dark soy sauce, 3g salt, 2g sugar, 1g pepper, and stir gently with a frying spoon. 12. Cover the pot and cook over medium heat for 7-8 minutes. 13. Open the lid of the pot, use chopsticks to pick out the bay leaves, star anise, ginger slices, green onions and garlic in the pot and discard them. 14. Turn up the heat and stir-fry continuously until the soup becomes thick (about 1-2 minutes). 15. Turn off the heat, put the chicken wings on a plate, and pour over the remaining thick soup in the pot. 16. Finally, sprinkle 3g white sesame seeds and 5g chopped green onion to complete the preparation.
Additional content:- If it smells fishy, ​​you can double the amount of spices.
Score the chicken wings twice on each side, blanch them and dry them. This will prevent oil from splattering when frying and make them more flavorful.
Fry until both sides are golden brown and then add water to simmer. The soup only needs to cover two-thirds of the chicken wings to reduce the juice faster.
Cola itself contains sugar, so the amount of light soy sauce and dark soy sauce should be reduced until the juice is thick enough to hang the chicken wings.

Case: There were only chicken wings, green onion and ginger left from dinner. She blanched the chicken wings until both sides were golden brown, added light soy sauce and cola and simmered until the juice was reduced. The chicken wings were red and boneless, salty and sweet, and the child even mixed the soup at the bottom of the plate with the rice.

items.title: Braised Lamb Chop Noodles
items.core: Braised Lamb Chop Noodles is a northern home-cooked dish with rich meat flavor and chewy noodles. The lamb chops are soft and rotten, and the wide noodles soak up the soup, making every bite satisfying. This dish contains meat, noodles and vegetables. One meal can provide the protein, carbohydrates and fats needed by the human body, making it comprehensively nutritious. When making it, you need to stew the lamb chops first and then simmer the noodles. There are a few steps, and it is more suitable for friends with some cooking experience. The whole process is expected to take about one and a half hours.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Lamb chops with skin - Green pepper - Bell pepper - Green pepper - Green onion - Sichuan pepper - Dried chili pepper - Ginger - White sugar - Dark soy sauce
Calculation: 1 person * 2 meals = 2 people - Lamb chops with skin 500g - Green pepper, bell pepper 2 each

Operation: 1. Blanch the mutton in a pot with cold water. After the water boils, skim off the blood foam and take out the mutton. 2. Cut ginger (4 slices), add dried chili pepper and Sichuan peppercorns in a bowl and set aside. 3. Add oil to the wok. (A little more is okay) 4. After the oil is hot, add sugar and fry the mutton until it turns caramel color. 5. After the mutton is fried, add salt, dark soy sauce, and prepared seasonings. 6. Add water to cover the mutton, bring to a boil over high heat, let it continue to cook for 10 minutes, then simmer over low heat for 30 minutes. 7. During this period, you can make noodles. The amount of dough and the operation method are explained in the additional content* (Note 1). 8. Add green pepper, bell pepper, scallions, and dough and stir-fry. 9. After stir-frying evenly, take it out of the pan. *Note 1: You can use supermarket noodles instead, but try to choose wide noodles.

Additional content: (Ingredients in the Dough Mixing Guide) - 300 g all-purpose flour - Salt 3 g - Water 180 ml (Operations in the Dough Making Guide) - Mix the ingredients evenly first, add water while stirring, and then knead the dough until it is smooth - Let the dough rise (10 minutes) - Knead the dough again until it is smooth - Let the dough rise (5 minutes) - Knead the dough into strips and cut it into 6 to 8 small pieces - Apply oil and wait for 5 minutes - Roll out the dough into a dough - Put it in a pot and simmer for 4 minutes (operate one piece at a time)
Put the lamb chops in a pot under cold water, add ginger slices, cooking wine and peppercorns and blanch them, which can effectively remove the smell and blood foam.
Add enough water to stew the lamb chops at one time. The soup will be slightly salty, and the noodles will be more flavorful when braised later.
Spread the noodles on the soup surface, cover and simmer over medium-low heat for eight to ten minutes. After opening the cover, shake them with chopsticks to prevent them from sticking.

Case study: When a friend came to his house in winter, he first blanched the lamb chops and stewed them until soft, then spread them on the hand-rolled wide noodles and simmered them until the soup was fully absorbed. Then he took them out of the pot and stirred in the beans and minced garlic. The noodles were chewy and the lamb chops were not sour. Everyone gathered around the pot and ate steaming hot.

items.title: Lao Ma's hoof flower
items.core: Lao Ma's hoof flower soup is milky white in color, the pig's trotters are soft and fall off the bones, and has a delicate texture. It is very appetizing when paired with hot and sour dipping sauce. It is a classic Sichuan-style home-cooked dish. Pig's trotters are rich in collagen, and white kidney beans add a dense texture and are rich in nutrients. The operation requires a pressure cooker and soaking in advance, which is a challenge for novices, but it is not difficult to master by following the steps. Including soaking and pressure cooking, the entire process takes about 2 hours (not including soaking the white kidney beans the night before).
body: Necessary raw materials and tools: - Pork trotters (try to choose the front trotters: more meat, more tendons and less bones) - Onions - Ginger - Cooking wine - Light soy sauce - Angelica dahurica - Angelica sinensis (optional) - Chicken essence - Salt - Garlic - Millet pepper - White pepper - Light soy sauce - Balsamic vinegar - Pepper oil - Spicy pepper (optional) - White kidney beans (no kelp available)

Calculation: - Pig trotters: 3 - White kidney beans: 200g - Angelica sinensis: 2g - White pepper: 5g - Ginger slices: 30g - Angelica sinensis: 2g - Minced garlic: 8g - Chicken essence: 2g - Light soy sauce: 25g - Chopped green onion: 10g

Operation: Start making: 1. Soak 200g white kidney beans in water one night in advance and set aside. 2. Prepare the pig's front trotters. When buying vegetables, ask the chef to split them in the middle, use a flamethrower to remove the hair follicles, and take it home to clean. 3. Add the pig's trotters, green onion segments, ginger slices, and cooking wine to a cold water pot, blanch for ten minutes, skim off the foam, remove, wash and set aside. 4. Put pig's trotters, angelica root, angelica root, white pepper powder, and ginger slices into the pressure cooker. Put the steam on and press for thirty minutes. Add the white kidney beans and press for another ten minutes. At this time, if the soup base is milky white, then congratulations are correct (if you need to add water halfway, you can only heat the water) 5. After uncovering, add salt, chicken essence, and chopped green onion to taste. 6. Prepare the soul juice: add onion, garlic, millet pepper, white pepper, light soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, oily chili pepper, Sichuan peppercorn oil, pig trotter stock 7. Soul juice, pour
Additional Content
Soak white kidney beans overnight in advance until the bean skin wrinkles, which makes them more likely to become soft and sandy when pressure-cooked.
Blanch the pig's trotters first and then press them with ginger slices for 25 minutes to make the soup clearer and less fishy.
Mix minced garlic, light soy sauce, balsamic vinegar and chili oil into the dipping sauce. Dip the pig trotters in to make it more appetizing.

Case: On weekends, she soaked the white kidney beans one night in advance, pressed the pig's trotters until they fell off the bones the next day, and served them with garlic and chili sauce. The soup was milky white and the beans were soft. Each member of the family had a bowl, and even those who were usually afraid of greasiness drank it all.

items.id: 老式锅包肉-老式锅包肉
items.title: old-fashioned pot-wrapped pork
items.core: pot-wrapped pork is a classic Northeastern dish, originated from Daotai Prefecture in Harbin. White vinegar is used to bring out the bright sour aroma, the shell is crispy, the meat slices are smooth, sweet and sour. Pork provides high-quality protein, and is paired with onions, ginger and other vegetables to appetize and relieve fatigue. This dish requires mastering the battering, oil temperature and re-frying skills. The cooking difficulty is medium to high, and novices need to practice patiently. From marinating the meat, mixing the batter to frying it, the preparation time is estimated to be about 90 minutes.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Pork ribs - Green onions - Ginger - Garlic - Carrots (optional) - Coriander - White vinegar (it is recommended to use 9 degree vinegar, so that it will have a more prominent vinegar aroma unique to old-fashioned pot-wrapped pork) - White sugar - Cooking wine - Salt - MSG - Potato starch - All-purpose flour - Baking soda - White cooked sesame seeds (optional) - Edible oil

Calculation: per serving (about 2 Serve): - 300g pork tenderloin - 5ml cooking wine - 50g green onions - 30g ginger - 3-4 cloves garlic - 10g carrots (optional) - 10g coriander - 5g baking soda (optional) - 5g salt - 4g light soy sauce - 55g white vinegar - 65g sugar - corn starch 1.5g (can be replaced by potato starch) - Method 1: 170g potato starch - Method 2: 210g potato starch and 70g all-purpose flour - 1000ml edible oil (for frying) - 5g white cooked sesame seeds (optional)

Operation: 1. Process the pork: - Cut the pork tenderloin into uniform slices with a thickness of 8mm, and remove the white fascia. - Rinse the meat slices with clean water to remove blood. - Optional: Add 5g of baking soda, mix well, and let sit for 5 minutes. - Rinse 1-2 times with clean water to remove excess baking soda. 2. Marinate the meat slices: - Add 3g of salt and 5ml of cooking wine to the meat slices, mix well, and marinate for 15 minutes. 3. Hanging slurry: - Method 1 (recommended): - Add 170g of potato starch to excess water, mix well, and let stand for 60 minutes, waiting for the starch to settle and stratify. - Pour out all the water in the upper layer, leaving the bottom starch slurry (like a non-Newtonian fluid). - Add the meat slices, 5ml of water, 3ml of cooking oil, and stir evenly. - Method 2: - Mix 210g potato starch and 70g all-purpose flour. - Add water in small amounts and several times, stir until it becomes yogurt-like, can be drawn when lifted, and the paste can accumulate in the basin. - Add 10ml cooking oil and 1g baking soda, stir evenly. - Add the marinated meat slices into the paste and mix well to coat each piece of meat evenly with the paste. 4. Prepare sweet and sour sauce: - Mix 65g white sugar, 55g white vinegar, 4g light soy sauce, and 2g salt, stir well and set aside. - Optional: 4g water, 1.5g cornstarch, for thicker sweet and sour sauce. 5. Prepare side dishes: - Shred green onions, ginger, and carrots, cut coriander into sections, and slice garlic. 6. Fry the meat slices: - First frying: - Add cooking oil to the pot and heat to 170°C (60% hot). - Put the meat slices into the oil one by one, fry until the surface is set, the surface is slurry and does not stick to chopsticks, the meat floats to the surface, and the color is light yellow, about 30 seconds (depending on the size of the meat slices), remove and set aside. - Second frying: - Oil temperature rises to 200°C (70% hot). - Put all the meat slices in oil and fry until the shell is golden and crispy, about 30 seconds, remove and set aside. - Third frying (optional): - Oil temperature rises to 220°C (80% hot). - Fry the meat slices again quickly until you can see the meat slices are yellow and red inside, about 30 seconds (depending on the ability of the oil to maintain temperature) to enhance the crispiness, remove and drain. 7. Stir-fry: - Leave 20ml of base oil in the pot, pour in the prepared sweet and sour sauce, heat over high heat until boiling, and simmer until the soup is thick, about 30-60 seconds. - Optional: Pour out 1/2 of the sweet and sour sauce to make it easier to stir-fry later - Add the fried meat slices, shredded green onions, garlic slices, carrot shreds, and coriander segments, top with the sweet and sour sauce poured out earlier, and stir-fry 3 times quickly to make the soup evenly coat the meat slices. 8. Remove from the pot and serve on a plate: - Place the pot-roasted meat on a plate, sprinkle with white cooked sesame seeds (optional), and serve.

Additional content: - Notes: 1. The thickness of the meat slices should be 8mm. Too thick or too thin will affect the taste. 2. It is very important to control the oil temperature when frying to avoid the shell being too dark or not crispy. 3. When boiling the sweet and sour sauce, be careful to boil it until it is thick but not lumpy to avoid turning into syrup. - References: - Old rice bone version - Old Northeast cuisine version - Village donkey version
Choose pork tenderloin and cut into 3mm thin slices, fluff it with the back of a knife, then add salt and cooking wine and marinate for 10 minutes to improve tenderness.
Make the paste according to the ratio of starch to water of 1:2, add a little oil and mix well. When making the paste, let the meat slices be evenly coated with the paste.
The oil temperature for initial frying is 60% and heat is set. After taking it out, increase the oil temperature to 80% and fry again for 20 seconds to ensure that the shell is crispy.

Case: I tried to replicate Northeastern cuisine over the weekend. During the first frying, the oil temperature was insufficient and the batter fell off. I adjusted the oil temperature to 60% hot and then fried again. The finished product was crispy, sweet and sour, and my family praised it for having a texture similar to that of a restaurant.

items.title: Meatloaf Stewed Eggs
items.core: Meatloaf Stewed Eggs is a salty, fresh and tender traditional home-cooked dish. The meatloaf absorbs the sauce, and the eggs lie in it. It tastes soft and goes well with rice. It is rich in high-quality protein and a variety of amino acids, which can replenish physical strength well. The recipe is very simple and friendly to kitchen novices, and it only takes about 20 minutes from preparation to serving.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Minced pork - Eggs - Cooking wine - Light soy sauce - White pepper - Sesame sesame oil
Calculation: - 300g minced pork - 2 eggs - Cooking wine 10ml - Light soy sauce 20ml - White pepper 5g - Sesame sesame oil 10-15ml

Operation: 1. Add minced pork, cooking wine, light soy sauce, white pepper, eggs and sesame oil to a bowl and stir evenly. 2. Spread the seasoned minced pork on a plate, use a spoon to make a hole in the middle, and break an egg into the hole. 3. Add water to the pot to 1/4 height. After the water boils, put the plate into the pot, cover the pot and steam for 15 minutes.
Additional content: - When taking out the meatloaf and stewed eggs, please note that the plate is very hot, please operate with caution.
Add the meat filling, onion, ginger water and light soy sauce and stir well clockwise. Let it rest for 5 minutes to make the meatloaf firmer.
Place the meat patties flat on the bottom of the bowl and use the back of a spoon to make indentations, then break in the eggs to avoid losing the egg liquid.
After the water boils, put it in the pot, steam over medium heat for 12 minutes, turn off the heat and simmer for 2 minutes to ensure that the eggs are cooked through.

Case: In order to make dinner in a hurry after get off work, I spread the meatloaf on the bottom of a bowl and directly poured in eggs to steam it. As a result, the eggs sank into the meatloaf. I adjusted to the method of steaming the meatloaf first and then adding the eggs. The finished product is tender and delicious.

items.title: Fermented bean curd pork
items.core: This is a classic Jiangnan home-cooked dish. Pork belly and red fermented bean curd are stewed together. The color is as red as amber. The meat is so crispy that it melts in the mouth. The salty and sweet aroma of wine and bean spreads on the tip of the tongue. Rich in high-quality protein and B vitamins, it is easier to digest after simmering. The production process requires patience to control the heat and collect the juice, which is a challenge for novices. The production is expected to take about 1 hour.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Pork belly with skin - Red bean curd (Xianheng brand rose bean curd is recommended) - Rock sugar - Dark soy sauce - Cooking wine - Chives (optional) - Ginger - Water - Edible oil

Calculation: You need to determine how many portions to make before each production. One serving is about enough for 2 people. Each portion: - 400 g pork belly with skin - 30 g red bean curd (about 2 pieces) - 15 ml fermented bean curd juice - 25 g rock sugar - 5 ml dark soy sauce - 15 ml cooking wine - 15 g green onion - 5 g chopped green onion - 10 g ginger - 500 ml water - 10 ml cooking oil

Operation: 1. Cut the pork belly into small pieces with a width of 2.5 cm. 2. Add cooking wine and ginger slices to cold water. Put the pork belly over high heat and slowly add it until the water boils. Remove it. 3. Grind the rose bean curd cubes and bean curd juice into a puree. Add rock sugar and dark soy sauce to make a sauce. 4. Sauté the onions and ginger with cold oil in a hot pot, and stir-fry the meat cubes until golden. 5. Pour in the bean curd sauce, stir well, and simmer in heated water. 6. Simmer over low heat for 40 minutes. 7. Reduce the juice over high heat. Turn off the heat when you see thick fish-eye bubbles in the soup

Additional content: - It is recommended to use single crystal rock sugar - Fermented bean curd comes with its own saltiness, no need to add additional salt - Keep shaking the pot while reducing the juice over high heat to avoid sticking to the bottom - References: [Step-by-step diagram] How to make fermented bean curd meat_How to make fermented bean curd meat_Recipe_Go to the kitchen
Choose skin-on pork belly and cut into mahjong pieces, blanch it in cold water and add ginger slices to remove the smell, remove and rinse with warm water.
Crush the red fermented bean curd and add a little fermented bean curd juice and mix thoroughly. Stir-fry the meat until the oil is released, then pour it in and stir-fry until it colors.
Add boiling water to cover the ingredients, add rock sugar and green onions, simmer over low heat for 1 hour, and finally reduce the sauce over high heat until thick.

Case: This dish was prepared in advance for a family dinner. When it was first simmered, the fermented bean curd was put directly into the pot, resulting in an overly salty taste. The adjustment was to stir-fry the meat pieces first and then add the fermented bean curd. After simmering over low heat, the meat became crispy and the aroma of wine and beans blended together.

items.id: 芥末罗氏虾-芥末罗氏虾
items.title: Mustard Roche Shrimp
items.core: This dish is fresh and slightly spicy, with rich mustard flavor and firm and tender shrimp meat. It is a quick home-cooked seafood dish. The shrimp itself is rich in high-quality protein and calcium, and has low fat content. It can be paired with mustard to make it appetizing and relieve fatigue. The level of difficulty is medium. As long as you follow the steps to prepare the bowl of juice and control the heat, novices can get started quickly. The whole process takes about 30 minutes.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Shrimp Roche - Garlic - Green mustard - Light soy sauce - Cornstarch - Pepper - White sugar - Oyster sauce - Salt - Chili millet (if you don't like spicy food, you can omit it or replace it with red pepper) - Butter - Cooking oil

Calculation: per serving (about 2 people): - 250g Shrimp Roche - 1-2 pieces of garlic - Green mustard 20g, for bowl juice - Cornstarch 10g, for bowl juice - Light soy sauce 30g, for bowl juice - Pepper 5g, for bowl juice - White sugar 3g, for bowl juice - Oyster sauce 15g, for bowl juice - Salt 3g, for bowl juice - 1-2 spicy millets - Butter 20g - Edible oil 80ml

Operation: 1. Process the shrimp: - Cut the shrimp from the back, remove the shrimp line and sandbags, or cut it from the abdomen. It will swell when fried, and the finished dish will be more beautiful - wash it with clean water, control the water and pat it with cornstarch, or not. 2. Garlic and bowl juice processing: - Cut 2 garlic into minced garlic - Prepare bowl juice, add light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, pepper, salt, squeeze in mustard according to personal taste, add water to dilute, then add cornstarch to dissolve 3. Stir-frying process: - Heat the pot and pour in cooking oil that can cover the bottom of the pot - Add the dried Roche shrimp and fry slowly - After the shrimp is fried (shown as a lot of bubbles in the pot), add the prepared minced garlic and millet - After smelling the aroma of the minced garlic, add butter - Stir the butter evenly after melting, and add the prepared bowl sauce - Cover the pot and simmer for 2 minutes until the soup thickens, then remove from the pot
Additional content: - Notes: 1. Do not fry the butter for too long after adding it to the pot. Melt and stir evenly before cooking into the bowl of sauce
Cut off the whiskers and legs of the shrimps, open the back and remove the lines, and use kitchen paper to absorb the moisture on the surface to prevent frying splashes.
Make the bowl of juice according to mustard paste: light soy sauce: oyster sauce = 1:2:1, add a little sugar to make it fresh, stir well and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Heat the pan and add cold oil to the shrimp, fry over medium heat until both sides turn red, pour in the sauce in the bowl and stir-fry quickly over high heat until evenly distributed.

Case: Friends wanted to make quick seafood for a dinner party. For the first time, they stir-fried the shrimp raw, which caused the water to turn fishy. I adjusted it to frying the shrimp until it changed color, then poured in the bowl of juice, and stir-fried for 1 minute over high heat. The shrimp meat was tender and had a rich mustard flavor.

items.title: Stir-fried Pork with Wild Wild Rice
items.core: Stir-fried Pork with Wild Wild Rice is a home-cooked quick-cooking dish. It is tender and crispy, salty and delicious, and is a typical home-cooked flavor in the south of the Yangtze River. Wild rice is rich in dietary fiber and multiple vitamins. It provides high-quality protein when paired with lean meat, and has balanced nutrition with meat and vegetables. The cooking difficulty is medium and can be mastered by novices with a little practice. It should take about 20 minutes to prepare.
body: Necessary raw materials and tools: * Wild rice * Lean meat * Starch * Edible oil * Chicken essence * Ginger * Garlic * Cooking wine * Salt
Calculation: per serving: * 2 wild rice stems * 100 g lean meat * 15 g starch * 30 ml cooking oil * 5 g chicken essence * 1 slice ginger * 1 garlic * cooking wine 5 ml * salt 2 g

Operation: Preparation: 1. Slice wild rice into slices, each slice is 0.5 cm thick. 2. Cut lean meat into strips, with a thickness of 0.3-0.5 cm. Add cooking wine, cornstarch, salt and water and stir. 3. Slice ginger and mince garlic. Production: 1. Bring water to a boil, add wild rice, cook for 60-90 seconds, take out and drain. 2. Remove from the pot and pour 15 ml. oil, add lean meat, stir-fry repeatedly for 60 seconds, take out. 3. Take out the pan, pour 15 ml of oil, add ginger and garlic, stir-fry for 30 seconds, add wild rice, stir-fry for 30 seconds. 4. Continue to add lean meat, stir-fry for 60 seconds, add 20 ml of water, add salt and chicken essence, stir-fry for 60 seconds, and remove from the pan.
Additional content: * In the last step, you can consider adding oyster sauce and light soy sauce instead of salt for coloring
Peel off the outer shell of the wild rice and cut it into cubes or thin slices. Blanch it in boiling water for 30 seconds to remove the oxalic acid. Drain it into supercooled water to keep it crispy.
Cut the lean meat into thin slices, add light soy sauce and starch, mix well and marinate for 10 minutes. When frying, the oil will be 40% hot and spread quickly.
First fry the meat slices until they change color and serve, then add wild rice and stir-fry over high heat for 1 minute. Mix the meat slices and add salt to taste.

Case study: I ​​wanted to have meat and vegetables for my weeknight dinner. The first time I cut the wild rice slices too thick and they became soft after frying, I cut them into 3 mm thin slices and blanch them in advance. After frying them with the meat slices, they tasted crispy and my family reported that it was refreshing and not greasy.

items.title: Lychee meat
items.core: Lychee meat is a traditional Fujian dish in Fuzhou that is sour, sweet and crispy. The meat is charred on the outside and tender on the inside, wrapped in a bright red sauce, and paired with fruits to add a refreshing fruity aroma. Lean pork is rich in high-quality protein, and pineapples contain dietary fiber and vitamins, which can help appetite and relieve fatigue. The production process requires cutting the meat, battering and frying twice. It is slightly challenging but the steps are clear. It is suitable for food lovers with a certain cooking foundation to try. It can be served to the table in about 45 minutes.
body: Necessary raw materials and tools: * Lean meat * Pineapple * Egg * Cooking oil * White sugar * Starch * Light soy sauce * Chicken essence * Minced ginger * Sesame seeds * Tomato paste * Balsamic vinegar

Calculation: per serving: * 2 fresh shiitake mushrooms * 30 g crab-flavored mushrooms * 150 g lean meat * 100 g pineapple * 1 egg * 500 ml cooking oil * 5 g sugar * 100 g starch * 5 ml light soy sauce * 5 g chicken essence * 5 g minced ginger * 2 g sesame seeds * 20 g tomato paste * balsamic vinegar 2 ml

Operation: 1. Cut the lean meat into pieces (each piece is 2-3 cm), put it into a large bowl, add 1 egg, 50 g cornstarch, 3 ml light soy sauce, and 2 g chicken essence. 2. Stir thoroughly until the cornstarch coats the lean meat pieces (if it is too thin, continue to add cornstarch, if it is too dry, add water), then add 5 ml of oil, stir thoroughly and set aside. 3. Prepare a bowl, add tomato sauce, and 3 g of chicken essence. , 2 ml of light soy sauce, minced ginger, white sugar, 10 g of cornstarch, 200 ml of balsamic vinegar, cold water, stir thoroughly and set aside. 4. Cut a pineapple and prepare 6 (1.5-2 cm each) pineapple cubes. 5. Heat oil in a pan, pour 500 ml of oil, and continue to heat until you hear the sound of frying. 6. Put the lean meat into the pot one by one (remember not to pour the whole bowl), ensuring that each piece of meat does not stick to each other. 7. After putting all the lean meat, use a spoon to flip the lean meat pieces back and forth every 30 seconds until the surface of the lean meat pieces is golden. 8. Take out the lean meat, pour it into the oil pan after one minute and continue frying until the surface of the lean meat pieces turns brown, then take it out and put it in a large bowl for later use. 9. Take the pot, pour the soup, add the lean meat pieces and pineapple pieces after 30 seconds, and stir-fry thoroughly. Remove from the pan 10. Arrange sesame seeds

Additional content: * In more cases, Fuzhou locals will use water chestnuts (to relieve greasiness) and potatoes (to wash oil). Because they are not available during the epidemic, pineapples are chosen. * Fujian cuisine is mainly sweet. If you are not used to it, you can give up sugar. * You can use a spoon to hit the lean meat pieces and hear the sound to judge whether the lean meat is fried thoroughly.
Cut the lean pork into diamond-shaped pieces and marinate it with a little baking soda for 15 minutes to make the meat more tender and easy to taste.
Mix the sweet potato starch and water into a yogurt-like paste at a ratio of 1:1.5, and add a little salad oil to increase the crispiness.
After initial frying and setting, increase the oil temperature and fry again for 30 seconds. Finally, stir-fry quickly with pineapple pieces and tomato sauce evenly.

Case: When trying a traditional Fuzhou dish, the batter was too thick for the first time and the meat was greasy. I adjusted the ratio of starch to water to 1:1.5. After re-frying, the shell became crispy. I stir-fried it with pineapple chunks and the sweet and sour fruity flavor was well received.

items.id: 荷兰豆炒腊肠-荷兰豆炒腊肠
items.title: Fried sausage with snow peas
items.core: Stir-fried sausage with snow peas is a refreshing and savory home-style stir-fry. The fat of the sausage moistens the green snow peas, giving it a crispy and tender texture that is not greasy. Snow peas are rich in high-quality protein and multiple vitamins, which help enhance the body's disease resistance. The method is simple and requires almost no knife skills, and even beginners can get started quickly. It only takes about 15 minutes from preparation to cooking.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Snow peas - Sausage - Light soy sauce - Cooking oil
Calculation: The following is for one person. Per serving: - About 50 snow peas - About 100 g sausage - 10ml cooking oil - 10ml light soy sauce

Operation: 1. Remove the stems of the snow peas, and if you have time, you can remove the tail at the same time. 2. Before buying the sausage, you can ask the boss whether it is raw or cooked. If it is raw, it needs to be steamed in advance. If it is cooked, it can be used directly. 3. Wash the snow peas and blanch them in water for about 45 seconds. Blanch the snow peas until they change color. Remove and cool the water and set aside. 4. Heat the pot and put about 10ml of cooking oil in the pot. Wait 10 seconds for the oil temperature to rise. 5. Add the sausage and stir-fry until the sausage is slightly curled. Note that the fire must be kept low, not too low, otherwise it will be easy to burn. 6. Add the snow peas, turn to medium-high heat, and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add light soy sauce, and then stir-fry for another 20-30 seconds.

Additional content: - No salt is added during the production process because the sausage itself will have some flavor, and the light soy sauce will also have some saltiness. - Although sausage tastes good, it is not a healthy food, so it is recommended to eat less of it.
Wash the snow peas after removing the old tendons, blanch them in boiling water with a little salt for 20 seconds, remove them from the cold water to keep them green.
Cut the sausage into thin slices diagonally, place in a cold pan and stir-fry over low heat until the edges are slightly charred, remove the fat and set aside.
Use the oil in the pot to fry the snow peas over high heat, add a little salt to taste, add the sausage and stir-fry quickly to combine.

Case: Making a quick dish in a small pot in the dormitory, the sausage was stir-fried raw so that the fat did not separate. The adjustment was to stir-fry the sausage until the oil was released and then add the snow peas. Stir-fry for 1 minute on high heat. The finished product was crisp, tender and salty, and my roommate praised it for serving with rice.

items.title: Lamb chops stewed with radish
items.core: This soup is fresh and not greasy, the mutton is soft and tasty, and the radish is sweet and glutinous after absorbing the soup. It is a common home-cooked warm-up dish in the north in winter. Mutton is rich in high-quality protein and iron, while radish contains vitamins and dietary fiber. The two are combined to warm the spleen and stomach, dispel cold and aid digestion. Although it requires blanching to remove the fishy smell and stewing twice, the steps are clear and easy to follow, and novices can get started smoothly. The overall preparation takes about two hours, which can be shortened to about one hour if you use a pressure cooker.
body: Necessary raw materials and tools: - Lamb chops - White radish - Green onions - Sichuan peppercorns - Angelica dahurica (optional) - Ginger - Cooking wine or rice wine - Edible salt - Rock sugar - Water

Calculation: per portion: - 400g lamb chops - One white radish - One green onion - 10 Sichuan peppercorns - 10g ginger, usually buy a head of ginger and cut about 4 pieces from it - Cooking wine or rice wine 30ml-40ml - Edible salt 10g - Rock sugar 2-4 grains - Water: enough to cover the ingredients, 1000ml is required

Operation: 1. Peel the radish and cut into 3-5cm large pieces with a hob, set aside. 2. You can ask the seller to cut the lamb chops when you buy it, because it is generally difficult to cut with a household knife. Set aside. 3. Put the mutton in cold water, add half of the cooking wine, half of the onion and ginger, and cook Remove the blood for 10 minutes. (Optional) Use a spoon to scoop out the bloody foam that appears during the blanching process. 4. In another pot of cold water, add the chopped white radish and half of the rock sugar. Wait for the water to boil and cook for 5 minutes to remove the spiciness of the white radish. 5. Take out the blanched lamb chops and put them into a pressure cooker. Add water to cover all the ingredients and then add about 300ml of water. 6. Put the remaining onion and ginger cooking wine, Sichuan peppercorns, rock sugar, Angelica dahurica (optional), and salt into the pot, cover the pot and wait for the steam to start, then simmer over medium heat for about 15 minutes. - If you don’t have a pressure cooker, place in a regular pot and simmer for about 40 minutes to 1 hour. 7. Turn off the heat, wait for the pressure cooker to deflate, open the lid, add the previously blanched radish, season, add 3-10g of salt or water, and taste the soup. 8. Turn on the heat again, put the pressure cooker on medium heat and stew for another 10 minutes, and cover the ordinary pot for another 20 minutes. 9. Turn off the heat, put on a plate
Additional content: - During operation, you need to pay attention to the boiling water level, if it is found to be lower than 2/3 The ingredients should be heated until the water is submerged.

Cut the lamb chops into pieces and put them in a pot under cold water. Add ginger slices and cooking wine and blanch them in water to remove the blood foam. Take them out and wash them with warm water.
Fry the sugar until the color is maroon, then add the lamb chops and stir-fry until browned. Add boiling water, green onions and star anise, and simmer over low heat for 1 hour.
Cut the white radish into hob pieces and add to the pot, continue to simmer for 30 minutes until transparent, add salt and white pepper to taste.

Case: I stewed the soup for my family to ward off the cold in winter. The first time I stewed the lamb chops directly had a strong fishy smell. After adjusting, blanch it and then stir-fry the sugar color. I added white radish and simmered it for 1.5 hours. The soup was clear and tender, and the meat was soft. The warming effect was obvious.

items.title: Roasted Chicken Legs with Green Onions
items.core: Roasted Chicken Legs with Green Onions is a home-cooked dish that can be completed with only two core ingredients: chicken legs and green onions. The chicken thighs are charred on the outside and tender on the inside, and the green onions are fragrant. The method is simple, and the whole process can be done in one pot, so even novices can succeed in one go. It's rich in protein and goes great with rice, making it a quick weekday dinner.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - 2 chicken legs (about 500g) - 1 green onion - 3-4 shallots - Light soy sauce (Haitian Gold Label recommended) - Dark soy sauce (for coloring, optional) - Oyster sauce (optional) - White sugar - Cooking wine or Huadiao wine - Salt - White pepper - Edible oil - 3-4 slices of ginger (optional, mainly used to remove fishiness and enhance flavor) - 10 Sichuan peppercorns (about 1g, optional, to enhance the aroma)

Calculation: Before each production, you need to determine how many servings you plan to make. One serving is just enough for 2 people. Each portion: - 2 chicken legs (about 350g of clean meat after bone removal) - 1 green onion (about 100g) - 3-4 spring onions (about 30g) - 15ml of light soy sauce - 5ml of dark soy sauce (for coloring, you can use light soy sauce if not available) - 10ml of oyster sauce (optional, add 5ml of light soy sauce if you don't have it) - 5g of white sugar - Cooking wine 10ml - Salt 2-3g - White pepper 1g - Edible oil 15-20ml

Operation: 1. Debone the chicken legs: Use scissors to insert from the big end of the chicken legs, cut the meat close to the bones, then cut twice along the bones to separate the bones and meat, and finally pull out the whole bone. Safer than using a knife to remove bones. 2. Cut the boneless chicken legs into 2-3cm cubes. 3. Cut green onions into thick slices (about 0.5cm thick), and cut green onions into 1cm long sections. 4. Add 10ml cooking wine, 5ml light soy sauce, 2g salt, 1g white pepper to the diced chicken legs, stir well and marinate for 10 minutes. 5. Take a small bowl and mix the sauce: 10ml light soy sauce + 5ml dark soy sauce + 10ml oyster sauce + 5g sugar, mix well and set aside. 6. Heat the pot and put 15-20ml cooking oil in the pot. 7. Add the ginger slices and Sichuan peppercorns and fry over low heat until the ginger slices are slightly browned and the Sichuan peppercorns become darker in color. 8. Use a slotted spoon to remove the ginger slices and Sichuan peppercorns and discard them, leaving the base oil. 9. Maintain medium-high heat, place the marinated diced chicken legs in the pan flatly, and do not flip them in a hurry. 10. Wait 2-3 minutes for the bottom of the diced chicken legs to brown, then stir-fry until all sides change color and the chicken is completely cooked. 11. Add the green onion slices and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 1 minute until the onion becomes fragrant. 12. Pour in the prepared sauce, stir-fry evenly and cover the pot. 13. Wait 2 minutes for the sauce and green onion aroma to fully blend into the chicken. 14. Open the lid, add scallions and 2g cooked white sesame seeds (optional), stir-fry for 5-10 seconds, then turn off the heat and serve.

Additional content: Tips for deboning chicken legs (scissor method): 1. Wash the chicken legs and use kitchen paper to absorb the surface moisture. 2. Find the end of the bone from the thicker end of the chicken leg. 3. Use the tip of the scissors to cut the outer skin and meat against the bone, and cut along one side of the bone to the bottom. 4. Turn the chicken leg over and continue cutting along the other side of the bone. 5. Use your fingers to peel away the joints between the meat and the bones. 6. Find the joint of the bone and cut it, and pull out the whole bone. The whole process does not require the use of a knife, which is much safer than the traditional "slicing and deboning" method, and even novices can succeed in the first attempt. About "Only green onions and chicken legs": The core of this dish is green onions and chicken legs, but relying on these two alone will lack layers. The ginger, Sichuan peppercorns, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and white sesame used in the video are all to make the onion and chicken aroma more three-dimensional. - Minimalist version: It can also be made using only green onions + chicken legs + salt + light soy sauce + sugar, but the green onions will be more monotonous. - Recommended version: Add ginger, Sichuan peppercorns, and oyster sauce to make the flavor richer. - Perfect version: Add a little dark soy sauce for color + cooked white sesame seeds to garnish, and the appearance and taste will be improved to a new level. Storage and reheating: 1. Refrigerated storage: seal and refrigerate for 2 days. 2. Frozen storage: Let cool and then freeze in portions. It can be stored for 1 month. 3. Reheating method: microwave for 2 minutes on medium heat, or return to the pot and add a little water and stir-fry.
Debone the chicken legs, place them skin side down in a cold pan, fry over medium-low heat until golden and crispy, then turn over.
Cut the scallions into sections and spread them on the chicken legs. Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and a little sugar. Pour in half a bowl of water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Open the lid and reduce the sauce over high heat until it thickens, allowing the onion aroma to penetrate into the chicken. Slice and serve on a plate, then pour over the soup from the pot.

Case: After get off work, I used a pot to finish dinner. The chicken legs were fried directly, causing the outside to be burnt and the inside to be raw. I adjusted it to fry the chicken skin first and then simmered it in water until the juice was reduced. The onion was rich and tender, and it was satisfying to eat with rice.

items.title: Stir-fried minced pork with garlic moss
items.core: Stir-fried minced pork with garlic moss is a home-cooked dish in the north. It is salty, crispy and tender, and has a rich garlic aroma. Garlic moss is rich in dietary fiber and vitamins, while pork belly provides protein, with a balanced mix of meat and vegetables. The method is simple, the ingredients are easy to prepare, and even novices can get started quickly. It only takes about 10 minutes from cutting to serving.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Pork belly slices - Garlic moss - Edible salt - Light soy sauce - Edible oil - Garlic cloves

Calculation: 1 person version - 1 bunch of garlic moss (each bunch of garlic moss is about 190g) - 4 slices of pork belly slices (about 20g) - 10ml cooking oil - 2 garlic cloves - 15ml light soy sauce - Salt 2g

Operation: 1. Cut the garlic into 5cm pieces, set aside. 2. Cut the pork belly into 5mm * 5cm strips, set aside. 3. Crush the garlic cloves and mince, set aside. 4. Heat the pot and put 10ml cooking oil in the pot. Wait 10 seconds for the oil temperature to rise. 5. Add minced garlic and stir-fry over medium heat for 10 seconds. Stir-fry the minced garlic until fragrant. 6. Add pork belly and 5ml light soy sauce and stir-fry over medium heat for 30 seconds. Stir-fry the meat until it is cooked and colored. 7. Put the garlic into the pot and add 10ml light soy sauce and stir-fry for 30 seconds. 8. Add 20g water to the pot and stir-fry over medium heat for 5 minutes. Fry the garlic until it softens slightly. 9. Finally add 2g of salt, stir-fry over medium heat for 30 seconds, and serve on a plate.

Additional content: - You can taste the saltiness before adding the salt and decide whether to increase or decrease the salt. - Thinly sliced pork belly is chosen because it is easy to cut and can be flavored without marinating
Cut the garlic into 1cm pieces, blanch in boiling water for 20 seconds and then rinse in cold water to keep it crispy and tender and shorten the frying time.
Combine the minced meat with a little light soy sauce and starch. Stir-fry the minced meat in a hot pan with cold oil until it changes color. Add bean paste and stir-fry until red oil appears.
Pour in the garlic moss and stir-fry over high heat for 1 minute, add a little salt to taste, and sprinkle with minced garlic to add flavor before serving.

Case: Adding vegetables temporarily and rushing for time, stir-frying the garlic sprouts directly caused the water to soften. The adjustment was to blanch the garlic sprouts first and then stir-fry the minced meat quickly. Add bean paste for seasoning to make it salty, crispy and tender. It was completed in 10 minutes and was approved by the family.

items.title: Tiger Skin Elbows
items.core: The finished dish is bright red in color, with attractive tiger skin texture on the elbow skin. It tastes soft and tasty, fat but not greasy, and the lean meat is soft. It is a traditional Chinese banquet dish. Pork knuckle is rich in collagen and high-quality protein, which is easier to absorb after long-term stewing and has a certain nourishing effect on the skin and joints. The production process includes multiple steps such as roasting the skin, frying, browning the sugar and stewing under high pressure. It is quite challenging for novices. It is recommended to have a certain cooking foundation before trying it. Expect it to take about 2.5 hours total from prep to serving.
body: Necessary raw materials and tools: - Pork elbow - Edible vegetable oil - Rock sugar - Salt - Dark soy sauce - Light soy sauce - White vinegar - Bay leaves - Cinnamon bark - Cardamom - Zanthoxylum bungeanum - Aniseed - Starch - Onion - Ginger - Garlic - Water - Cooking wine

Calculation: - 1 tablespoon = 15ml - 1 teaspoon = 5ml |Raw materials |Quantity |Unit| |:---:|:---:|:---:| |Pork front knuckle|1|pcs| |Edible vegetable oil|can submerge more than 3/5 of the pork knuckle|measured by the height of the pig's knuckle| |rock sugar|200|ml| |Cardamom|3|pcs| |Peppercorn|8-12|pcs| |Aniseed|2-4|pcs| |Starch|1|tbsp| |Onion|2|trees| |Ginger|6|g| |Garlic|6|pcs| |Cooking wine|2|tbsp

|Operation: Pretreatment: 1. Soak the pork knuckle for 1 hour to remove the blood after thawing. 2. If you have a flame spray gun, use the flame spray gun to burn the surface of the pig elbow skin until it is brown and black to remove the pig hair and destroy the sweat glands. Be careful not to grill the same spot for a long time to avoid burning. Stop burning when the pork knuckle skin is almost completely brown and black. 3. If there is no flame gun, heat the iron pot to above 200, put the pork knuckle directly into the pot, and use a spatula or chopsticks to fully contact the surface of the iron pot with the pork knuckle skin. When the contact point between the pork knuckle skin and the iron pot turns brown, change the position and continue scalding the pork knuckle skin until the entire pork knuckle is fully scalded. Pay attention to the temperature of the iron pot during the reheating process and do not make the iron pot red hot. 4. Use a cleaning ball to scrub the pork knuckle in water to remove the burnt part on the surface. After the brushing, the pork knuckle once again appeared in the same state as before it was burned. 5. Place the pork knuckle in the iron pot and add as much cold water as possible, depending on the depth of the iron pot and the size of the pig's knuckle. It is best if more than 3/4 of the pork knuckle can be submerged while ensuring that the iron pot and its contents can be handled. Remove the fishy smell: 1. Take the white part of 1 green onion, divide it into 3 sections, and put it into the pot. 2. Take 3 pieces of garlic, flatten them with the blade of a knife, and put them into the pot. 3. Take 3 grams of ginger and put it into the pot. 4. Add 2 tablespoons cooking wine to the pot. 5. After the water in the pot boils, wait for five minutes, then take out the pork knuckle, pick out all the ingredients in the pot, replace the container and keep all the broth for later use. Frying: 1. Add cold oil to the pan. Dosage calculation table: Use the previous water volume as a reference, it is better if it can submerge more than 3/5 of the pork knuckle. Turn on medium heat. 2. When the oil temperature reaches 50%, turn to low heat and fry the pork knuckles. 3. Cooks should pay attention to personal safety during the frying process. 4. During the frying process, use a spatula or other high-temperature resistant kitchen utensils to evenly pour the oil in the pot onto the unimmersed parts of the pork knuckle. If conditions permit, turn the pork knuckle over at 3-minute intervals to allow it to fry evenly. 5. The frying process lasts for about 20 minutes. When it is observed that the pork knuckle skin has turned light brown and the lean meat has been slightly burnt, remove it and set aside. 6. The oil after frying can be used to make other fried foods, but be careful not to use it too many times. Stir-fried sugar color: 1. Take 200 ml of rock sugar from the calculation table, stir-fry the sugar color and set aside. Stew: 1. Add the pork knuckle to the pressure cooker, add all the broth, sugar, bay leaves, cinnamon bark, cardamom, Sichuan peppercorns, aniseed, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, and white vinegar. If you like it sweeter, you can add an additional 2-3 grams of rock sugar. 2. Take the white part of 1 green onion, divide it into 3 sections, and put it into the pot. 3. Take 3 pieces of garlic, flatten them with the blade of a knife, and put them into the pot. 4. Take 3 grams of ginger and put it into the pot. 5. Cover the pot and simmer on pressure for 40 minutes. To reduce the juice: 1. Prepare water starch during stewing. Take a bowl, add 1 tablespoon of starch and 100ml of water, stir until it becomes a white suspension. 2. After the stewing time is over, open the lid of the pressure cooker and pick out all the ingredients in the pot, except for the pork knuckle. 3. Transfer the remaining broth in the pressure cooker to the iron pot, and transfer the pork knuckle to a plate or basin. 4. Place the iron pot on the stove and turn on high heat. During the juice collection process, you can use the head of a chopstick to dip the soup in the pot to judge whether it is salty or not, and add salt according to taste. Note that when there is more soup, the taste will be lighter than when there is less soup. You need to consider this when adding salt. 5. When the broth boils, pay attention to the remaining broth. 6. When the remaining broth is less than 1/2 of the original broth volume, stir the previously prepared water starch again and add half of it. 7. Wait for the broth to boil and add the remaining half. 8. Wait for the broth to boil. After boiling, wait 1-2 minutes and turn off the heat. At this time, the broth in the pot will be reddish brown and sticky. 9. Use a spoon to scoop up the broth and pour it evenly over the pork knuckle, trying to cover every part of the pork knuckle with the soup. If the soup has been used up before the pork knuckle is completely poured, it can be served directly. Otherwise, the remaining soup does not need to be poured again and can be served directly.
Additional content: - Reference: Bilibili’s video tutorial
Wash the pork knuckle and grill it until the skin is browned, then scrape it clean with warm water to remove any remaining hair roots.
Cook until chopsticks can be inserted, apply white vinegar on the skin, fry in oil until golden brown and bubbling to form tiger skin patterns.
Soak the fried elbows in cold water for 10 minutes, add sugar and spices and simmer under high pressure for 40 minutes to reduce the juice.

Case: I tried a feast for New Year’s Eve dinner. The skin was not completely cooked for the first time, which caused the finished product to have a frizzy feel. After adjustments, it was roasted and fried together, and then simmered under high pressure. The elbow skin showed tiger skin patterns, was soft and tasty, and won praises.

items.title: Ants on the tree
items.core: Ants on the tree is a classic Sichuan home-cooked dish, salty and slightly spicy, the vermicelli is soft and absorbs the juice, and the minced meat is tender and fragrant. Using sweet potato vermicelli and minced meat as the main ingredients, it is rich in carbohydrates and protein and can quickly replenish energy. The production difficulty is medium, the steps are clear, and it is friendly to novices. The whole process takes about 20 minutes to complete.
body: Essential ingredients and tools: - Sweet potato vermicelli - Minced pork (or minced beef) - Pixian bean paste - Light soy sauce - Dark soy sauce - Edible oil - Minced garlic, minced ginger - Green onion (optional)

Calculation: Before each production, you need to determine how many servings you plan to make. One serving is just enough for 2 people. Each portion: - 80g sweet potato vermicelli (dry weight) - 150g minced pork - 15g Pixian bean paste - 10ml light soy sauce - 5ml dark soy sauce - 10ml cooking oil - 10g minced garlic - 5g minced ginger - 300ml water (used to cook vermicelli)
