body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - 1 oven is required (the one with upper and lower heat functions is best, but not required) - 1 pair of insulated gloves - 1 box of egg tart liquid and 1 box of egg tart crust purchased online (nearby large supermarkets are also available, such as Carrefour, Wal-Mart, etc.)
Calculation: Each portion: - 1 egg tart shell - about 10ml of egg tart liquid, reaching 4/5 of the tart shell.

Operation: 1. Preheat the oven at 200 degrees for 10 minutes. 2. Place the egg tart shell on the baking sheet, and pour about 10ml of egg tart liquid into the egg tart shell. The specific amount depends on the size of the tart shell, usually 4/5 is enough. 3. Place the baking sheet in the oven, heat up and down to 190 degrees, and bake for 10 - 20 minutes. If you want to bake out the brown spots on the egg tart liquid quickly, you need to turn on the heat at a higher temperature, usually 200-210 degrees. 4. When the egg tart liquid is baked with brown spots, the egg tart skin is completely fluffy and oily.

Additional content: - During operation, you can adjust the time appropriately according to the size of the brown spots. If necessary - you can add 10g of shredded cheese to the egg tart to make a cheese egg tart~

The egg tart shell does not need to be defrosted for too long. Pour the egg tart liquid into it as soon as possible after placing it on the plate to avoid moisture affecting the crispiness of the bottom.
Pour the egg tart liquid until it is 80% full. It will expand when baking. If it is too full, it will easily overflow and stain the baking pan.
Bake until the surface is swollen and have caramel spots. Take it out of the oven and let it sit for a few minutes before unmoulding. The filling will be more stable.

Case study: After the egg tart shell softens at room temperature, pour in the egg tart liquid until it is 70% full. Bake at 200 degrees for 18 minutes until burnt spots appear on the surface. After cooling for five minutes, the mold will be more complete.

items.title: French fries
items.core: Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, golden and salty, French fries are a popular fast food snack. Potatoes provide carbohydrates and dietary fiber, but are higher in calories when fried or air-fried. Using semi-finished French fries and an air fryer, the operation is simple and even novices can get started. It takes about 25 minutes from preheating to serving.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - 1 bag of semi-finished French fries (recommended brand McCann) - 1 air fryer (if you like crispy food, avoid small brands) Note that different cooking tools may have different methods of frying French fries. Here we only introduce the method of using an "air fryer".

Calculation: - As a staple food, 1 person per meal 400g (subject to semi-finished products) - As a snack, 1 person per meal 1/4 staple food quality +-50g Using the above conditions, calculate the amount of materials according to the demand (including but not limited to daily food intake, mood and pre-meal exercise).

Operation: Unsealing French fries: 1. When opening large quantities of semi-finished French fries, make sure the opening is small, which can effectively reduce frost on the surface of French fries during long-term storage. Preheat the air fryer: 1. Plug in the power and preheat at 200℃ for 5 minutes. 2. The purpose of preheating is to ensure that the temperature inside the pot is at the required cooking temperature when ingredients are added. 3. Note that you should take out the fries after preheating and do not wait for the fries to soften before frying. French fries: 1. Take out the fries and put them in the air fryer at 200℃ for 20 minutes. 2. When taking out the fries, please note that the semi-finished fries are already oily, so you need to use a clamping tool if you want to cut the fries asynchronously. 3. After 5 to 10 minutes, you can take out the pot and shake it to heat the fries evenly and prevent them from sticking. Crisping (optional): 1. After 10 to 15 minutes, take out the pot and spray a layer of oil on the surface of the dried fries with an area of ​​2/3 of the surface area of ​​the fries. Take out & plate: 1. If you like crispy fries, take it out and dance with the pot to let the air pass through the surface of the fries before putting it on a plate; if you like soft fries, put it on a plate directly. Best served with dipping sauce or topped with sauce.
Extras: - Ketchup, mayonnaise, honey mustard, garlic soy sauce... The path to French fries lies in the exploration of sauces and sauce combinations.
Try to lay the French fries in a single layer, not pile them thickly, so that the hot air can circulate and the finished product will be more even and crispy.
Just spray a small amount of oil. Too much oil will make the fries greasy, while too little oil will make the surface not golden and crispy enough.
Pull out the frying basket and flip it half way through to prevent one side from becoming soft. The best taste is to eat it immediately after taking it out of the pan.

Case: A friend came to watch football at home. Akai spread the semi-finished French fries into the air fryer, sprayed them with oil and baked them at 200 degrees Celsius for 20 minutes, turning them over halfway through. When it's hot, dip it in tomato sauce. It's crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. It's eaten up quickly.

items.title: Butter hotpot base
items.core: This Chongqing hot pot base is based on a large amount of butter, mixed with glutinous rice cake peppers and various spices. The base is spicy and mellow with a strong aroma. It is the soul of scalding tripe, duck intestines and other ingredients. Butter and lard provide abundant energy. Chili and Sichuan pepper can warm the body, dispel cold and stimulate appetite. However, they have high fat content and should be eaten in moderation. The production process requires precise control of oil temperature and stir-frying heat, which is a challenge for novices. It takes about 1 hour from preparation to completion.
body: Necessary raw materials and tools: Raw materials: - Butter 4500 g - (Salad oil or rapeseed oil) 1000 ml - Pure lard 500 g - Douban (Pixian County) 1000 g - Rice cake pepper 3000 g - Ginger (sliced) 250 g - Green onion (cut into sections) 100 g - Onion (shredded) 100 g - Garlic (sliced) 200 g - Dougu (chopped) (Yongchuan) 10 g - Bean mother and son 140 g - Red pepper 150 g - Old oil? Granulated spices 100 g: Shaped spices 150 g - Malt powder (meaty) 12.5 g - White wine (52%VOL) 150 ml - Old oil ?? Dried chili noodles 15 g Spices: - Kaempferia 5 g - Star anise 10 g - Grass fruit 10 g - Cinnamon 10 g - Clove 5 g - Cumin 10 g - Angelica dahurica 10 g - Piper 5 g - Vanilla 10 g - Spicy fruit 10 g - Hawthorn 10 g - Tangerine peel 5 g - Lemongrass 10 g - Amomum villosum 10 g - 10 g of white cardamom - 10 g of bay leaf. Granulated spices: Place the above ingredients into a grinder and crush into approximately 4 mm particles for later use. Plastic spices: Wash the above ingredients and set aside. Tools: - Crusher
Calculation: - Each ingredient can make 7.5 kg of hot pot base/hot pot oil

Operation: 1. Set the pot over high heat (high fire), add butter and heat until it is 80% hot (240±10°C). Add ginger, scallions, onions and garlic (100g each), fry until dry (to absorb the odor (butter smell)), then remove and throw away. 2. Add (salad oil || rapeseed oil) and pure lard. When the oil temperature in the pot drops to 50% hot (150±10°C), add glutinous rice cake pepper and continue to stir-fry for 5-8 minutes. 3. Add the douban and stir-fry until scattered, then turn to medium-low heat and stir-fry until the residue is slightly white and sandy (makes a rustling sound). 4. When the oil turns cherry red, add ginger slices (150g) and garlic (100g) and stir-fry until fragrant, about 15 seconds. 5. Add bean drum, bean mother and son and stir-fry until fragrant, add red peppercorns and cumin and stir-fry until fragrant. 6. (Old oil) At this moment, add granulated spices. 7. Add malt powder and stir-fry. Add white wine and stir-fry. As a base: 1. Put the pot into a container and let it stand in a low temperature environment (10-20) for the best effect before using it for 5 days. As old oil: 1. Put the pot into a container, add dried chili noodles, mix well and let it sit for 24 hours, waiting to make the old oil. 2. Pour the base ingredients into the pot, add 3/5 of the boiling water and bring to a boil over high heat (base ingredients: 2/5, boiling water: 3/5). 3. After boiling, foam will appear on the surface. Skim off the foam. 4. Switch to medium-low heat and simmer slowly to release the flavor (about 25-30 minutes), then filter to remove residue. 5. After waiting for the oil and water in the container to separate, skim off the oil on the surface (punch out the oil) and put it into another container. 6. Pour the oil skimmed out in the previous step back into the clean pot until the water in the oil is dried out and put into a container to become the old hot pot oil.
Extras: - WARNING: Wipe your hands dry during operation! To prevent water from entering the oil pan and causing an explosion! Cause severe burns!
Simmer the butter over low heat first, add ginger and green onion to remove the smell, wait until the water evaporates and then add the spices to make it more stable.
The glutinous rice cake peppers and watercress should be stir-fried over low heat. Add the peppercorns when the color becomes darker and the oil becomes bright red.
Add the Sichuan peppercorns in two batches, stir-fry the first time to get the base flavor, add a small amount before serving to enhance the numbing aroma.

Case: For a winter dinner, the chef first boils the butter, then slowly stir-fries the glutinous rice cake with chili pepper, watercress and Sichuan peppercorns. The kitchen is spicy and fragrant. The base ingredients are mixed with soup and then the duck intestines are rinsed. Everyone said that the taste is mellow, slightly spicy and fragrant.

items.title: Air Fryer Lamb Chops
items.core: This dish is super lazy to make. Using the air fryer can force out excess fat. The finished product is charred on the outside and tender on the inside, with a strong garlic aroma. The flavor mainly depends on the quality of the lamb chop itself. Mutton is rich in high-quality protein and trace elements such as iron and zinc, which helps warm and replenish qi and blood and enhance physical fitness. The cooking difficulty is moderate, and it can be easily started by novices. The actual hands-on operation only takes 10 minutes, and the total time of marinating is taken into account and it can be served on the table in about 40 minutes.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Necessary: Lamb chops (recommend JD to buy the Lamb French shoulder chops imported from New Zealand from Hacienda, 500g/bag, three slices in total, 42 yuan if JD discounts) - Necessary: black pepper mixed with steak seasoning (lazy) - Necessary: garlic sauce (recommend Sichuan Wazi, also because of laziness) - Necessary: kitchen paper - Optional: butter (JD buys small boxes, one piece per box) - Optional: barbecue seasoning - Optional: chopped basil - Optional: air fryer grill (using a grill requires less oil, and the bottom is easier to cook, and it is troublesome to wash. If not used, it will taste better. It depends on personal choice)
Calculation: - 1 piece of lamb chop, about 160g - 5g of black pepper steak seasoning - 20g of garlic sauce - 1 small box of butter, 10g or 20g of barbecue seasoning

Operation: 1. Place the lamb chops in a bowl and wash away the blood. 2. Use kitchen paper to absorb the water from the lamb chops. Spread the black pepper seasoning and garlic sauce on both sides and let it marinate for 20 minutes. 3. Place the tin foil bowl on the grill, place the lamb chops on the grill, sprinkle with chopped basil, put butter or barbecue ingredients on the lamb chops, and air fry the pan at 180° for 10 minutes. 4. Turn the lamb chops over, sprinkle with chopped basil, butter (scooped from the tin foil bowl) or barbecue ingredients on the lamb chops, air fryer at 180° for 5 minutes (you can add a little more time according to personal preference, the time written here is the time that will not burn)
Additional content: - It is recommended to buy an air fryer with better temperature control, otherwise it may burn
Use kitchen paper to absorb the surface moisture of the lamb chops in advance. This will make them more flavorful when marinated and easier to color after grilling.
Add minced garlic, cumin and a small amount of light soy sauce to the marinade to remove the mutton smell without covering up the delicious flavor of the mutton itself.
Turn over once halfway through baking, adjust the time according to the thickness of the lamb chops, take it out and let it rest until the edges are slightly charred.

Case: For weekend dinner, Xiao Zhao marinated the lamb chops with minced garlic, cumin and light soy sauce for half an hour, then put it in the air fryer and grilled it until the edges were slightly charred. After it comes out of the oven, the fat is much less, and it is still juicy when you bite into it. My family said that the smell is light.

items.id: 空气炸锅鸡翅中-空气炸锅鸡翅中
items.title: Air fryer chicken wings
items.core: This is a convenient and hassle-free home-cooked dish. The chicken wings are crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. They have their own aroma of oil and are more appetizing than those in fast food restaurants. Chicken wings are rich in high-quality protein and fat and have sufficient energy. It is very friendly to novices, the actual operation only takes a few minutes, and the whole process can be eaten in about forty minutes.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Necessary: ​​Chicken wings (it is recommended to buy Tyson's Orleans chicken wings, if JD discounts, a bag of 454g is about 12 pieces for 30 more. I have also bought the ones from Shangxian and Shengnong, which are not as convenient. Tyson's are marinated, if you have time, you can buy unmarinated ones and marinate them yourself.) - Optional: chopped basil (sprinkled purely for appearance) - Optional: Yunnan Shanshan dipped in water (instead of barbecue ingredients)
Calculation: - 6 chicken wings (Tyson Orleans chicken wings, other brands such as Saint-Non Dudu wings may be larger, please consider according to your appetite)

Operation: 1. Take the chicken wings out of the refrigerator, place the chicken wings side down on a tin foil baking pan, sprinkle with chopped basil, cover with plastic wrap and defrost naturally for 20 minutes. 2. Sprinkle with chopped basil, and air fry at 200°C for 10 minutes. 3. Turn over, sprinkle with chopped basil, and air fry at 200°C for 7 minutes.
Additional content: - It is recommended to buy an air fryer with better temperature control, otherwise it may burn
Score both sides of the chicken wings so that the marinade can penetrate into the meat faster, and the grilling will be more flavorful and even.
Marinate for at least twenty minutes. If you are pressed for time, you can add a small amount of yogurt or lemon juice to help tenderize.
Wipe off excess marinade on the surface before grilling to reduce water leakage and make the chicken skin more crispy.

Case study: Cut the chicken wings in two, add light soy sauce, cooking wine and ginger slices and marinate them for 20 minutes. Bake them in an air fryer at 200 degrees for 12 minutes. Turn them over halfway through to make the skin more even.

items.title: Quick frozen dumplings
items.core: This is a home-cooked noodle dish originating from China. It is made from commercially available frozen dumplings. It has thin skin, rich fillings and a delicious taste. Served with vinegar, ginger, garlic and other dipping sauces, the taste will be more layered. As a meal, it provides sufficient protein and carbohydrates and is nutritious and satiating. There is no difficulty in making it, and novices can easily get started, and it only takes about a quarter of an hour.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: * A bag of unexpired frozen dumplings

Calculation: * Generally one person can eat 7 to 10 dumplings * One dumpling requires about twice its own volume of water (when the dumplings are poured into the pot, the height of the water should be one to two times the height of the dumplings, that is, the height of the dumplings is 1 and the height of the water is 1 to 2) Using the above conditions, calculate the proportion of raw materials planned to be used.

Operation: 1. On medium heat, pour water into the pot and wait for the water to boil. 2. Pour the dumplings into the pot. 3. You can rinse it with water before pouring it into the pot. 4. After pouring the dumplings, you can use a cooking spoon or shovel to stir the water, but be careful not to shovel the dumplings to avoid sticking to the pan, tearing the skin or sticking to each other, causing the adhesions to get caught. 5. The frequency does not need to be too high. Shake for 3 seconds every 30 seconds on average. There is no need to do this step again after the dumplings float. 6. After the dumplings float and the water boils again, use a cooking spoon to pick up a dumpling and observe. If the dough is uncooked, use a cooking spoon to scoop in 80ml of cold water, cool down the water, and continue to boil until it boils. Repeat this observation and stirring operation. Add water twice at most to fully cook. 7. After all the dumplings have floated (about 8 minutes after placing the dumplings), use a spatula or slotted spoon to scoop the dumplings into a plate or bowl. Place on the plate and serve. 8. After eating the dumplings, wait for the water temperature in the pot to drop, pour out the water and clean the pot promptly with dish soap, otherwise the flour cooked in the pot will form sticky material on the wall of the pot over time.

Additional content: There are some supplementary methods for this dish, including but not limited to: Add the following additional ingredients: * 10ml black vinegar * 50g small piece of ginger * 2 drops sesame oil * 3 cloves/person of garlic/garlic paste * Consider eating with black vinegar. Recommended dosage: 10-20ml. * Consider cutting the ginger into shreds, add 20ml of black vinegar and shredded ginger in a small bowl and stir as a dipping sauce for a richer flavor. * Consider adding 1~3 drops of sesame oil when paired with black vinegar, stir it as a dipping sauce. * Consider adding minced garlic when paired with black vinegar and stir to use as a dipping sauce. (The smell of garlic will remain in your mouth. If you need to talk face-to-face with others after a meal, it is recommended to give up or clean your mouth)
Put the frozen dumplings in after the water boils. Push them gently after putting them in the pot to prevent the dumplings from sticking to the bottom or sticking to each other.
Drink a small amount of cold water twice halfway to make the dumpling skins cooked and not easy to break. Just wait until you see them bulge and float.
Mix vinegar, minced ginger and minced garlic for the dipping sauce to make it fresh and relieve greasiness. You can also add a little chili oil.

Case: On a weekday night, Xiao He took out the quick-frozen dumplings from the refrigerator. After the water boiled, he put it in the pot. He ordered cold water twice. The dumplings floated and swelled before taking them out. Served on a plate with ginger, garlic and vinegar, it takes fifteen minutes to finish, it is hot and filling.

items.title: Quick frozen glutinous rice balls
items.core: Quick-frozen glutinous rice balls are a quick and convenient microwave dessert with soft and waxy outer skin and sweet filling. They are traditional Chinese snacks. Mainly provides carbohydrates, which can quickly replenish energy. The recipe is very easy to follow and even a novice can complete it. It only takes about 6 minutes from preparation to serving.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: - Quick-frozen glutinous rice balls - Microwave oven

Calculation: Per serving: - Quick frozen glutinous rice balls: 11 pieces. Quantity depends on bowl size. Make sure that the height of the glutinous rice balls placed does not exceed the height of the bowl - 5mm.

Operation: 1. Take out the quick-frozen glutinous rice balls and put them into a bowl. 2. Pour in boiling water until the glutinous rice balls are submerged. 3. Microwave on high for 4 minutes. 4. If the glutinous rice balls have absorbed water and swelled, they are ready. 5. If not done, reheat for 1 minute.

Additional content: - Be careful to add the glutinous rice balls first and then the hot water. Do not turn them upside down, otherwise the hot water may splash out and burn you. and the inability to control the height of the water surface for possible overflow. - If the bowl is too hot to remove from the microwave, you can use a towel, or some microwave ovens can remove it with the tray.

The water in the bowl should completely cover the glutinous rice balls, and stir once halfway through heating to avoid adhesion and damage to the outer skin, and to prevent uneven heating and sandwiching.

Control the total microwave heating time to 5-6 minutes, and fine-tune it according to the number of glutinous rice balls. It is more reliable to reheat for 30 seconds after all the glutinous rice balls float.
Be careful of the high temperature of the bowl when taking it out. Add a small amount of osmanthus or wolfberry to enhance the flavor. Sugar can be added according to personal taste.

Case: Xiao Zhou, who came home late from work overtime, didn’t want to complicate the process of turning on the fire. He took the quick-frozen glutinous rice balls and water and put them in the microwave, heated them over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirred and heated for another 2 minutes. The soft and glutinous glutinous rice balls came out of the pot, and the warm and sweet soup quickly dispelled fatigue. It was a simple midnight snack in ten minutes.

items.title: Quick-frozen wontons
items.core: Quick-frozen wontons have thin skin and tender fillings, and the soup is clear and delicious. They are a convenient home-cooked pasta. Mainly provides carbohydrates and protein for quick energy replenishment. The recipe is simple and very friendly to novices. It can be done using a rice cooker and it takes about 55 minutes from boiling water to cooking.
body: Necessary ingredients and tools: * A bag of unexpired quick-frozen wontons (it is better to bring your own seasoning pack) * Rice cooker (recommended brand Xiaomi smart rice cooker) * Salt (when there is no seasoning pack for quick-frozen wontons) * Chicken essence (when there is no seasoning pack for quick-frozen wontons) * Pepper (when there is no seasoning pack for quick-frozen wontons) * Sesame oil (when there is no seasoning package for quick-frozen wontons) * 1 coriander (optional) Note that different cooking tools may be used to make quick-frozen wontons in different ways. Here we only introduce the method of using a "rice cooker".

Calculation: * Generally, one person can eat 12 to 20 wontons in one meal * When all the wontons are put into the rice cooker, the amount of water that can just cover all the wontons is multiplied by 2 to 3 times the amount of water (a wonton for one person requires about 600ml of water)

Operation: Boil water: 1. Pour the water into the rice cooker and run it in stew or boil mode 35 minutes. At this time, when you open the rice cooker, you should see that the water is boiling. To prepare the wontons: 1. Carefully put the frozen wontons into the water, being careful not to burn them. 2. You can rinse it with water before putting it into the rice cooker. 3. If the wontons have seasoning packets, you can add them to the water at this time. To cook wontons: 1. Cover the rice cooker and run it in the same stew or boil mode for 20 minutes. To serve the wontons: 1. Put all the wontons into a bowl together with enough water to cover them all. 2. If you have not added the seasoning packet before, you can add salt, chicken essence, pepper, and sesame oil to season according to your own taste. 3. You can also sprinkle with 5~8 coriander leaves for flavor (only suitable for people who are not sensitive to the taste of coriander).
Additional content: * You can also add boiled poached eggs (sunny eggs) after cooking.
Put the wontons in after the water boils. Avoid adding cold water to the pot, which may cause the dough to boil. Stir gently during cooking to prevent them from sticking to the bottom of the pot.
Do not shorten the cooking time of the rice cooker arbitrarily, make sure the meat filling is completely cooked, and add a little salt and white pepper to season before serving.
You can put dried shrimps and light soy sauce at the bottom of the bowl in advance, ladle in the hot soup and stir it up, then add the wontons, the soup base will have a richer flavor.

Case: Xiao Lin, who lives alone in a rented house, wants to drink hot wontons. He adds water to the rice cooker and boils it, then puts in the quick-frozen wontons and simmers them for 50 minutes. Then he takes them out of the pot and sprinkles them with green onion and seaweed. The skin is thin and the filling is tender and the soup is delicious. There is no need to watch the stove, and it is easy to complete a simple dinner.

items.title: Kitchen Preparation
items.core: Before reading and referring to the recipe, imagine that you have already prepared the following items in your kitchen. These items are not mentioned in the Raw Materials and Tools section. Gas stoves, drinking water, woks, steamers, cooking pots, rice cookers, cooking oil, sinks, plates, bowls, chopsticks, spoons, soup spoons, colanders, detergents, rags, steel wool, kitchen knives, raw food chopping boards, deli chopping boards, paring knives, hot water kettles. Detergents, rags, steel wool, etc. are bowl cleaning supplies. For the complete dishwashing process, see How to Wash Dishes. The following materials may be used at high frequency. It is recommended to purchase food for the kitchen in advance and always ensure that there is fresh food available. Green onions, shallots, ginger, garlic, Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, cinnamon, bay leaves, dried chilies, millet peppers, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, cooking wine (yellow wine, optional), black vinegar (balsamic vinegar, mature vinegar), white vinegar, bean paste, rock sugar, marshmallow, salt, MSG/chicken essence, black pepper, white pepper, allspice, corn starch, sweet potato starch. If you need to deal with emergencies or long-term home needs, it is recommended to purchase the following: Refrigerator, microwave oven, plastic wrap, plastic bags Eggs, green peppers, carrots, cucumbers, tomatoes, fungus, tenderloin, eggplant, rice, noodles or instant noodles If you really want to pursue formality, standardization and ritual, and want to have a unique and interesting kitchen, then purchase the following items as well: Electronic scales (or balances), vernier calipers, measuring cylinders, stopwatches, beakers, thermometer guns, pipettes. If you want to save time, you can buy semi-finished products and simply process them before eating: Pre-fried fried chicken nuggets, frozen hand pancakes, wrapped dumplings, packaged curry, various rice bowls, self-heating foods, mixed toppings, takeout bags, convenience foods. For other raw materials for each dish, please refer to the chapter on the required raw materials for the dish itself.
body: Purchasing oil: Before buying oil, you need to understand some basic knowledge of fatty acids. Classification of fatty acids: Fatty acids are divided into: * Saturated fatty acids (try to avoid) * Unsaturated fatty acids * Cis fatty acids * Trans fatty acids (especially pay attention to avoid) * Polyunsaturated fatty acids * Monounsaturated fatty acids Saturated fatty acids will be solid at room temperature, while unsaturated fatty acids will be liquid at room temperature. Fatty acids to avoid: Of these, saturated and trans fatty acids are generally considered unhealthy. Saturated fatty acids increase the risk of obesity, high cholesterol, and heart disease. Studies have shown that long-term excessive consumption of trans fatty acids produced by hydrogenation processing can cause abnormal blood lipid metabolism in humans, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease. There are also studies showing that it may increase the risk of chronic diseases such as diabetes and obesity. The World Health Organization recommends that in order to improve cardiovascular health, trans fatty acids in the diet should be controlled as much as possible, with the maximum intake not exceeding 1% of total energy. In other words, if the average daily energy intake of an adult is 2,000 kcal, the daily intake of trans fatty acids should not exceed 2.2 grams. GB 28050-2011 stipulates that when food ingredients contain or use hydrogenated and/or partially hydrogenated oils and fats during the production process, the content of trans fats (acids) should also be indicated in the nutrition facts table. Trans fatty acids in food: According to relevant surveys, the average content of trans fatty acids in baked goods (pastry, biscuits, bread, etc.), condiments, and fried foods is between 0.30~0.50 g/100g. So don't worry too much - trans fatty acids in everyday foods are not enough to harm your health. But just in case, when purchasing snacks, you may wish to pay attention to the trans fat (acid) content marked on the nutrition facts table. Trans fatty acids in cooking: According to a 2021 survey, the average trans fatty acid content of vegetable oils in China is 0.86 g/100g, so there is no need to worry too much. The source of trans fatty acids to pay extra attention to is the cooking process: Vegetable oils often contain a higher proportion of polyunsaturated fatty acids, which have poor thermal stability and are easily converted into trans fats at high temperatures. Therefore, in different scenarios, we need to choose the oil reasonably and reduce the heating time of the oil as much as possible. Vegetable oil selection: | Oil name | Saturated fatty acids (%) | Omega 3 (%) | Omega 6 (%) | Omega 9 (%) | | :----: | :----: | :----: | :----: | :----: | | Canola oil | 7% | 11% | 21% | 61% | 12% | 1% | 71% | 16% | | Corn oil | 13% | 1% | 57% | 29% | | Olive oil | 15% | 1% | 9% | 75% | | Soybean oil | 15% | 8% | 54% | | 27% | 0% | 54% | 19% | | Lard | 43% | 1% | 9% | 47% | | Palm oil | 51% | 0% | 10% | 39% | | Beef tallow | 68% | 1% | 3% | 28% | Peanut oil is rich in monounsaturated fat. But it is only recommended to choose high quality ones. When processing, be careful not to heat it for too long to avoid producing trans fatty acids. * Olive oil is rich in monounsaturated fat, which has only one unsaturated bond. Olive oil has low saturated fatty acid content. * Cold/low-temperature cooking: It is recommended to choose extra virgin olive oil (Extra Virgin), which retains more polyphenols and other antioxidant substances, but its smoke point is low (about 160-190℃) and is not suitable for high-temperature stir-frying. * Medium-high temperature stir-frying: It is recommended to choose refined olive oil (labeled Pure or Refined), which has a higher smoke point (above 230℃) and is more suitable for Chinese cooking. * Soybean oil contains about 15% saturated fatty acids and contains linoleic acid and vitamins. …
Place spices in zones according to frequency of use. Light soy sauce, salt, onions, ginger, and garlic are placed next to the stove. Dry spices are stored in sealed jars to prevent moisture.
Strictly separate raw and cooked chopping boards, place detergents and rags separately, return kitchen utensils promptly after each meal, and develop storage habits.

Onions, ginger, garlic, and eggs that are easily consumable are always on hand, and semi-finished ingredients are stored in separate sections. There is no need to purchase them temporarily when there is an unexpected need for cooking.

Case: Ah Zhe, who had just moved to a new home, was cooking according to the recipe for the first time. He rummaged through the cabinets to find salt and light soy sauce. He mixed the kitchen knives and cutting boards but could not find the colander. He hurriedly smeared the pot. Afterwards, he prepared the tools and seasonings according to the list. The cooking efficiency will be greatly improved next time.

items.title: How to Wash Dishes
body: Dishwashing in the 21st Century: Dishwashing is one of the easiest-looking tasks in the kitchen. As modern kitchen tools become increasingly complex, "washing dishes" is no longer limited to its literal meaning. However, many people's understanding of dishwashing is still stuck in the "ancient method" of "wiping dishes with a towel". Some families even have hidden health risks (such as carcinogens) due to long-term unscientific dishwashing methods. In order to help everyone master scientific, efficient and modern dishwashing methods, this guide will introduce in detail the dishwashing process, precautions and avoidance of pitfalls.

The purpose of dishwashing: Whether you use traditional hand washing or a dishwasher, there is only one ultimate goal: to return the tableware to a state where it is safe to use again. Specifically, the following points need to be met at the same time: 1. Looks clean: no oil film, water stains, vegetable residues, or fingerprints on the surface. 2. It feels clean: Use your fingers to scratch the bottom of the bowl, the handle of the spoon, and the inside of the mouth of the cup. If there is no sticky feeling, it means it is clean. 3. Smells clean: no rancid oil smell, no pungent detergent smell. 4. Can be used dry: no obvious water accumulation after draining or wiping dry, and no moisture when stored. 5. No cross-contamination: tools used to handle raw meat do not contaminate washed tableware. Only when all the above 5 conditions are met can you be considered clean.

Tools to prepare: Modern kitchen tableware is made of various materials (non-stick coating, cast iron, enamel, wood, stainless steel...). Different materials require different cleaning tools. Choosing the wrong tool is a common pitfall. Washing-related tools already exist by default in kitchen preparation. It is recommended to ensure that the following items are available when washing dishes: hot water (priority), cold water, sink, dishwashing basin (optional), dishwashing sponge/scouring pad, detergent, steel wool (only stainless steel pots, non-stick pots/coatings are prohibited) Draining rack, clean rag or kitchen towel, gloves (optional) Dishwasher (optional, see below for details) Key points for using tools: - Sponge/scouring pad: the first choice for daily dishes. After use, squeeze it dry and let it air dry to prevent the sponge itself from becoming moldy and smelly. - Steel wire balls: only used on hard uncoated surfaces such as iron pots and stainless steel pots. It is forbidden to use on non-stick pans, ceramic coatings, and delicate porcelain, otherwise the coating will be damaged. - Rags: The rags used to dry tableware must be separated from the rags used to wipe the stove and the floor. Mixing them together means washing them in vain. - Dishwasher: If you have a dishwasher, you can skip the main process of hand washing, but you still need to complete the scraping preprocessing and post-wash storage. See the "Dishwasher" section below for details.

Overall process: Many people only have two steps to wash dishes: "add detergent → flush", which is far from enough. A scientific dishwashing process should include the following links: Collection and classification → Scraping and soaking → Cleaning and decontamination → Rinsing to remove detergent → Inspection → Drying → Storage Each step has an irreplaceable role, and skipping any step may leave hidden dangers. Step by step instructions below.

Detailed steps: 1. Collection and classification: After meals, collect the bowls, plates, chopsticks, spoons, pots, chopping boards, etc. scattered everywhere next to the sink, and sort them according to the degree of contamination. It is recommended to clean in the following order (from light to heavy): 1. Lightly soiled: glasses, cups, chopsticks, spoons 2. Medium soiled: serving plates, rice bowls 3. Heavy soiled: woks, frying pans, baking sheets, containers with egg liquid stuck on them 4. High risk: chopping boards and knives that have handled raw meat and fish (it is recommended to handle them separately last) Why we need to classify: wash lightly soiled items first, as the water and sponge are relatively clean and will not bring heavy oil stains to the cups; wash raw food utensils separately last to avoid bringing pathogens to the washed tableware. 2. Scraping and soaking: This step is skipped by many people, but it directly determines the difficulty of subsequent cleaning. Get rid of stubborn residue in advance, so you don’t have to brush repeatedly during the actual wash, which saves effort and water. Operation: 1. Use a napkin or spatula to scrape off large pieces of residue and pour it into the kitchen waste bin. Do not flush directly into the sewer, as it may become clogged. 2. Soaking is required in the following situations: - Dried rice grains and starch paste - Protein coagulation (egg liquid, milk residue) - Burnt pot and paste bottom 3. Soaking method: - Ordinary oil stains and rice grains: soak in hot water for 5–15 minutes - Burnt pot bottom: soak in hot water + a small amount of detergent, or add water to boil first and then turn off the heat and simmer for 10–20 minutes - Tea stains and scale on stainless steel: soak with a small amount of white vinegar and then scrub (do not mix with bleaching products) [!Warning] Do not pour cold water directly when the oil pan is not cooled. Thermal expansion and contraction may cause the pot to deform, and oil may splash and burn when exposed to cold water. Do not soak cast iron pots and carbon steel pots for a long time, otherwise they will easily rust. After washing, dry it immediately and apply a thin layer of oil. 3. Cleaning: Removal of oil and dirt: This is the core step of the entire process. The recommended water temperature is warm to hot water (about 40–50°C). Hot water can effectively reduce the viscosity of grease and greatly improve the decontamination efficiency. If you have an adjustable temperature faucet at home, it is recommended to adjust it directly to the appropriate temperature. Standard hand washing steps: 1. Turn on the faucet or prepare a basin of warm water in the sink. 2. Squeeze a small amount of detergent (about the size of a mung bean to a soybean, about 1–2ml) onto the sponge to create foam. 3. Wash in the order of "outside → inside, handle → head, edge → center": - Bowl: brush the outer wall first, then the inner wall, focusing on the inside of the bottom of the bowl - Plate: plate surface, plate rim, plate bottom - Chopsticks and spoons: chopstick heads and spoon heads are the key contaminated areas - Pot: pot bottom, pot wall, pot rim, don't forget the oil splashing on the outside of the pot 4. If you encounter stubborn stains, first use the rough surface of the sponge to scrub with local pressure. Do not apply steel wool as soon as you come up. 5. Chopping boards and knives: - Raw meat chopping boards: After scrubbing with detergent, they can be washed with hot water. Disinfect regularly when conditions permit. - Knives: Brush the blade away from you to avoid cuts. More detergent does not mean cleaner. Using too much will only increase the workload of rinsing later, and the residue on the dishes itself is not good. 4. Rinse: Remove detergent: After cleaning, the detergent and dissolved dirt need to be completely rinsed away with clean water. Operation: 1. Rinse each piece of tableware thoroughly under running water until the following conditions are met: - No foam - No greasy feeling to the touch - The water film on the surface is even (if the oil is not washed away, the water will gather into beads instead of spreading evenly) 2. Detergent is likely to remain in the mouth of the cup, the groove at the bottom of the bowl, and the seams of the pot handle, so rinse for a few more seconds. 3. If you use a sink for static rinsing, it is recommended to change the water at least once, and finally run it through running water again. 5. Inspection: Go through each piece of tableware: - Look: Hold it against the light to see if there is any oil film reflecting the light - Touch: Touch the inner wall lightly with your fingertips to see if it is sticky - Smell: Come closer and smell if there is a sour or detergent smell. If it fails, go back to step 3 and wash it partially again. Do not take an unwashed area directly to dry. 6. Drying: Cleaning does not mean it can be used directly - a humid environment is a breeding ground for bacteria. Many people feel that the task is completed after washing the dishes, but if they are stored before drying, the previous efforts may be in vain. Optional methods: | Methods | Specific operations | Applicable scenarios | | --- | --- | --- | | Drain | Invert on a drain rack and air dry naturally | Most commonly used in daily life, save effort | Batch processing...

Recommended cleaning order: If you wash the entire set at one time, it is recommended to follow the following order: 1. Glasses/cups 2. Chopsticks, spoons, forks 3. Plates, bowls 4. Cooking utensils such as spatulas and soup spoons 5. Wok/boiler (heavy oil) 6. Raw food cutting boards and knives (finally, wash the sink separately) 7. Rinse the sink and faucet handle (finishing) The principle is: the pollution advances from low to high to prevent the heavy oil pollution at the back from contaminating the things that have been washed before.

Handling tableware made of different materials: It is normal in modern kitchens to mix pots and tableware made of various materials, but the cleaning methods of different materials vary greatly. Using the wrong method may damage the appliance at first, or cause health risks at worst. Non-stick pans: - Use a soft sponge + neutral detergent and scrub gently. - It is prohibited to use steel balls or hard shovels to scrape the coating, otherwise the coating will be damaged and the pot will be useless. - Dry after washing to avoid water accumulation for a long time. Cast iron pot/carbon steel pot: - Use as little or no detergent as possible to protect the oil film on the surface of the pot. - Use hot water + brush to remove residue. - After washing, dry it, dry it on low heat, and then apply a thin layer of cooking oil to prevent rust. Wooden chopping board/wooden shovel: - Clean quickly and do not soak for a long time, otherwise the wood will crack and deform. - After washing, dry standing upright. - Regularly wipe cooking oil maintenance (chopping board). Chopsticks: - Focus on washing the end that comes into contact with food (chopstick head). - Bamboo chopsticks are prone to water accumulation and cracking, so be sure to dry them after washing. - Replace it directly if there is severe mold or cracking. Do not continue to use it reluctantly. Dishwasher: The dishwasher is one of the most efficient tools in the modern kitchen, but it is not a universal machine that "just throw the bowl in" and still requires manual cooperation to achieve the best results: 1. Scrape off large pieces of debris (bones, vegetable leaves, etc.) first, otherwise it will easily clog the filter and spray holes. 2. Place the tableware according to the dishwasher instructions, with the bowl mouth facing down and the plate on its side. Be careful not to block the rotation of the spray arm. 3. Choose the appropriate program—for heavy oil use, use the strong or high setting; for light soiling, use the quick wash or energy-saving setting for daily use. 4. After washing, open and inspect, focusing on the grooves at the bottom of the bowl and the inside of the cup mouth. If there are any that are not washed, wash them by hand. 5. Clean the dishwasher filter and sealing ring regularly to prevent odor and mildew. It is recommended to clean the filter every 1–2 weeks and empty-wash it once a month with a special detergent. Air fryer: The basket and chassis of the air fryer are the main cleaning objects. Many people just wipe them and put them back. Over time, the oil will carbonize, affecting the heating effect and food safety. - After each use, wait for the machine to cool down, take out the frying basket and bottom plate, and clean them with warm water + detergent + sponge. - It is easy for food residue to get stuck in the gaps between the basket grid. You can use an old toothbrush or a small brush to help clean it. - Do not use steel wool to brush the frying basket - most frying baskets have a non-stick coating. Brushing with steel wool will damage the coating, causing it to stick and peel off during subsequent use. - If there is oil splashing on the inner wall of the fuselage, just wipe it with a wet rag. Do not immerse the entire fuselage in water. - If the heating tube (top) is stained with oil, wipe it gently with a damp cloth after cooling. Oil stains that have not been cleaned for a long time will smoke or even produce harmful substances under high temperatures. Rice cooker: Most rice cooker inner pots have a non-stick coating, so you need to pay attention to protecting the coating when cleaning. Many people neglect cleaning the steam valve and the inside of the pot lid. - Use a soft sponge + detergent to clean the inner tank. Steel wool is prohibited. Once the coating is scratched and peeled off, the rice will stick to the pan, and the peeled off coating fragments will also get mixed into the food. - The inside of the pot lid, steam holes, and sealing rings are areas that are easily overlooked—starch steam will condense into sticky residue in these places, which will become sour and smelly over time. It is recommended to wipe the inside of the pot lid after each use and remove the sealing ring regularly for cleaning. - The outer shell of the pot can only be wiped with a damp cloth. Do not soak it in water to avoid damaging the circuit. High pressure cooker/electric pressure cooker: The focus of cleaning high pressure cookers is not the pot itself, but safety-related parts such as sealing rings, exhaust valves and pot lids. If these parts are not cleaned properly, it will not only affect hygiene, but also affect sealing performance, posing safety risks. - Seal: remove after each use and clean with warm water + detergent. Food residue and grease are easy to hide in the grooves of the sealing ring, so they need to be scrubbed carefully. Wash and dry before putting them back together. The sealing ring should be replaced in time after aging (hardening, deformation, cracks). - Exhaust valve/pressure limiting valve: rinse with clean water after removal to ensure that the valve hole is unobstructed and not blocked. If the valve hole is blocked by food residue, it may cause abnormal pressure relief the next time it is used. - Pot lid: The grooves on the inside and the edge of the pot lid are prone to accumulation of oil and food residues and need to be scrubbed clean. - Inner pot: The cleaning method is the same as that of ordinary stainless steel pots or non-stick pots. Select the tool according to the material of the inner pot. Oven: The baking pan, racks and interior walls of your oven need to be cleaned regularly. Many people only wash the grill pan and ignore the grill and inner wall. Over time, the grease will carbonize and produce a smoke smell, which may even affect the flavor of the food. - Baking pan: Clean it with detergent + sponge while it is still warm (be careful not to scald your hands). After cooling, the grease will solidify and become difficult to clean. There are stubborn...

Common problems and pitfalls: The following are the most common mistakes and misunderstandings in the dishwashing process, organized by type. Each one comes with specific consequences - only by knowing "why not do this" can you truly avoid these pitfalls. Cleaning habits: - Rinse without brushing: Just rinsing with water cannot remove the oil film. Grease is insoluble in water. It must be emulsified by the surfactant of detergent and then removed by physical friction with a sponge. The result of only rinsing without rinsing is that the surface of the bowl may look clean, but in fact there is still a thin film of oil on it, making it slippery to the touch. The next time you serve a meal, the food will be stained with the smell of spoiled grease. - Putting too much detergent: Too much foam does not mean clean washing. After the detergent exceeds a certain concentration, the decontamination effect will not continue to improve. The consequence of putting too much is that it is difficult to rinse out during the rinsing stage, and the residual detergent will be eaten together with the next meal. Although long-term ingestion of detergent residues will not cause immediate poisoning, it can irritate the gastrointestinal mucosa, so there is no need to take this risk. - Only wash the inner wall but not the outer wall and bottom: Many people only wash the inside of the bowl when washing dishes, ignoring the outer wall and bottom of the bowl. When the dishes are stacked, the bottom of the upper bowl directly contacts the inner wall of the lower bowl - if the bottom is dirty, it means that the lower bowl has been washed in vain. - Let it dry if it is not rinsed thoroughly: If there is still detergent foam left on the bowl, take it out and drain it. After drying, the detergent will form a dry film on the bowl surface, which will enter the body with the food the next time it is used. The judgment method is very simple: touch it with your fingers. If there is still a greasy feeling, it has not been rinsed off. - If left untreated overnight: starch and protein residues will dry out and become very solid if left at room temperature overnight, requiring several times the effort to brush them off the next day. What's more important is that in summer, food residues begin to multiply in large numbers within 2-4 hours at room temperature, and a dirty bowl left overnight is basically a petri dish. If there are meat residues in the bowl, it will also attract cockroaches and fruit flies. Tools used: - Steel wool brush for non-stick pans: Steel wool will scratch the non-stick coating (usually Teflon), and once the coating is damaged, it will continue to fall off. A damaged non-stick pan not only loses its non-stick function, but the peeling coating fragments can also get mixed into the food. After the coating is damaged, the pot body is directly exposed, and it is easy to stick to the pot. The correct way is to use only the soft side of a sponge to scrub non-stick pans. - Wipe dishes with dirty rags or smelly sponges: Sponges and rags that remain wet for a long time become a breeding ground for bacteria and mold. Using a smelly sponge to "wash" the dishes is equivalent to wiping away bacteria. The same goes for rags—wiping the dishes with a cloth that has just been used to clean the greasy stovetop just moves the dirt to another place. It is recommended that the sponge be squeezed dry and ventilated after each use, and the rags should be cleaned or replaced regularly at high temperatures. - Use hard tools to scrape enamel/ceramic coating: The surface of enamel pots and pots with ceramic coating is relatively brittle, and scraping hard with a metal spatula or steel wool ball will cause the porcelain to chip or scratch. After the enamel collapses, the underlying metal is exposed, which not only affects the uniformity of heating, but also makes the metal prone to rust when exposed. - Keep the faucet running when washing dishes: keep the faucet running the whole time, and you may waste dozens of liters of water in one wash. A better approach is: first turn off the water, wipe all the dishes with a sponge and detergent, and then rinse them in boiling water. Material damage categories: - Long-term immersion of cast iron pots/carbon steel pots: Cast iron and carbon steel do not have anti-rust coatings (or rely on a layer of oil film to prevent rust), and will rust quickly if soaked in water for a long time. Once rust occurs, it is not only unsightly, but if the rust is severe, the pot will need to be re-opened and maintained. The correct way is to dry it immediately after washing, dry it on low heat and then apply a thin layer of cooking oil. - Use a lot of detergent for cast iron pots/carbon steel pots: detergent will wash off the oil film that has been hard-earned on the surface of the pot, causing serious sticking to the pot the next time you use it. Daily cleaning of cast iron pots and carbon steel pots only requires hot water + a brush. If there are stubborn residues, you can rub them with coarse salt. - Directly pouring cold water into a hot pot: The temperature of the pot after cooking is very high. Directly pouring cold water into it will cause severe thermal expansion and contraction. Stainless steel pans may warp, and cast iron pans may even crack. If there is residual hot oil in the pot, pouring cold water will cause the oil and water to splash, which may cause burns. You should wait for the pot to cool down slightly before cleaning. - Wooden chopping boards/wood shovels soaked in water for a long time: The wood will expand after absorbing water, shrink after drying, and will crack and deform after repeated several times. When wooden chopping boards have cracks, food residues and bacteria can easily hide in the gaps, making them difficult to clean. The correct way is to wash and dry quickly and hang it upright. Hygiene hazards: - Put wet bowls directly into the cabinet: Putting them in a closed cabinet before drying is equivalent to providing an ideal warm and humid environment for bacteria and mold. After a few days, mold or an odor may appear on the bowl, and the entire cabinet of tableware may be affected. - No distinction is made between raw and cooked food: if the chopping boards and knives that have been used to cut raw meat or fish are placed directly in the dishwashing water and washed with other dishes and chopsticks, the raw meat may be carrying...

Summary: Cooking is to turn the ingredients into an edible state, and washing dishes is to restore the kitchen to a state where you can cook again. The two things form a complete circle - just cook and not wash the dishes, and the kitchen will soon become unusable. Mastering scientific dishwashing methods, making good use of modern kitchen tools, and understanding the correct ways to handle different materials can make dishwashing both efficient and safe. Develop the habit of "washing after use and putting away after washing" so that cooking can continue in the long term.

Case: After dinner, Xiao Tang piled up a sink of dishes. He scraped off the residue on the plates, scrubbed them with warm water and detergent, cleaned the burnt stains on the bottom of the pot with steel wool, rinsed away the foam with running water, wiped away the water stains with a rag, and put away all the stains. The kitchen countertop was restored to be clean and fresh.

sections.title: Tips·How to choose what to eat now

items.title: How to decide what to eat
items.core: How to decide what to eat is also a big problem for me before cooking. So it can only be described mathematically.
body: Calculation method: Calculate the number of meat and vegetable dishes: * Number of dishes = Number of people + 1. * There can be one more meat dish than vegetarian dish, or the same number. From this, you can get the number of meat dishes and vegetarian dishes, and then choose from the recipe in the previous step. Formal language description: When there are N people, let the number of vegetarian dishes be a and the number of meat dishes be b. N, a, b are all integers. At this time, there is the following set of inequalities: * a + b = N + 1 * a ≤ b ≤ a+1 The solution is const a = Math.floor((N+1)/2); const b = Math.ceil((N+1)/2); Choice of dishes: * If there are more than 8 people, consider adding fish and meat dishes to the meat dishes. * If you have children, consider adding sweet dishes. * Consider adding special dishes and specialty dishes. * Be careful not to use all the meat of the same animal when making meat dishes. The order of consideration is: pork, chicken, beef, mutton, duck, fish. * Don’t choose strange animals for meat dishes. If you're still not sure, use the What's For Today? tool to choose what to eat today.

Make a list of frequently eaten dishes in advance, filter them from the two dimensions of time consumption and the ingredients you have on hand, and first eliminate options that cannot be made immediately.
Set weights for taste preferences and cooking difficulty, simply score and sort, and the dish with the highest score will be directly selected as this time.
Set a deadline for decision-making. If the decision cannot be finalized after more than five minutes, always choose the standing semi-finished product to avoid excessive internal friction.

Case: Xiao Wu, who had difficulty choosing what to eat before dinner, listed weighted scores from three dimensions: time consumption, taste, and remaining ingredients. He compared the scores of tomato egg noodles and fried rice, and quickly finalized the plan. The menu was determined in less than ten minutes, and he no longer struggled with it.

items.title: Remove the fishy smell
items.core: Removing the fishy smell is a process in the cooking process. Removing fishy smell refers to removing the fishy smell from meat, aquatic products and other foods by means including but not limited to adding seasonings and blanching. The fishy smell is the source of the flavor of some foods. Excessive removal of fishy smell may cause the food to lose its flavor. There are many ways to remove fishy smell, and you should be flexible in your choice during cooking projects.
body: Method: Adding seasonings: Adding seasonings to ingredients is the simplest way to remove fishy smell. For example, for most dishes that use egg liquid (egg custard, scrambled eggs with tomatoes), you can add salt, cooking wine, vinegar and other seasonings to remove the smell during the process of making the egg liquid. When cooking certain meats, you can add peppercorns, star anise, bay leaves, cinnamon, cumin, chili pepper and other spices to the soup base to remove the fishy smell. The finished spicy hot pot base has an extremely rich aroma, which can be added in appropriate amounts during cooking, enough to cover the fishy smell of most meats. Dips: Some foods still smell fishy after cooking. Dips can be prepared to mask the fishy smell when eating. Common dipping ingredients include: vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, bean paste, sweet noodle sauce, sesame paste, peanut butter, fermented bean curd, salt, garlic, ginger, etc. The combination of various dipping sauces is a matter of opinion, so I won’t give an example here. Stir-fried pot: During the cooking process, you can use onions, ginger, garlic, dried chili and other spices to stir-fry the pot. The aromatic substances in spices evaporate under the action of high temperature, which can cover the fishy smell to a certain extent and increase the flavor of the finished dish. Blanching in a cold water pot: There is blood remaining in some animal raw materials, such as chicken, pig's trotters, ribs, etc. If the remaining blood is not removed, the finished dish will have a fishy smell. When the cold water is put in the pot, the remaining blood will be dispersed into the water; as the temperature rises, the proteins in the blood coagulate, and the blood originally dispersed in the water forms foam and floats on the water. At this time, just use a spoon to skim off the foam to complete the fishy removal, and the remaining clear soup can be used as a soup base for stews to continue cooking. Notes: - When blanching, some seasonings are often added to the pot, such as Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, cooking wine, green onions, etc. to further strengthen the removal of fishy smell. - Star anise has a strong fragrance and should be added in appropriate amounts. - Sichuan peppercorns and peppercorns are small in size and large in amount. After adding, they may remain in the pot or even remain in the finished dish. You can use gauze to wrap a seasoning bag or use a food-grade stainless steel seasoning box to facilitate picking out before serving.

Case study: Soak the meat in cold water for one hour, change the water twice in the middle, and then blanch it in water to skim off the foam. The fishy smell will be significantly reduced when used in soup.

items.title: Cold salad
body: What is Cold Salad: Cold Salad is a way of mixing main ingredients and auxiliary ingredients to form a dish. The form of Cold Salad: Cold Salad can be made into a form in which the ingredients and auxiliary materials are mixed in space. Cold Salad can be made into a form in which the ingredients and auxiliary materials are spatially separated, and the auxiliary materials are called dipping sauces. Why Cold Salad: * Some Cold Salads do not require a heat source when they are made into dishes * Some Cold Salads can reduce the process of washing the pot (no washing or just watering) * Cold salad can preserve the state of ingredients, especially vegetables and raw meat. Purpose of cold salad: * The purpose of cold salad is to add flavor to tasteless or bland ingredients, such as chicken ribs. What can be put in cold salad: Including but not limited to: * Main ingredients * Accessories * Marinade sauces * Seasonings. Notes: * Pay attention to the safety of ingredients when cold salad. If you are not sure whether the ingredients are safe, do not mix the corresponding ingredients. If you confirm that the ingredients are unsafe, you should not mix the corresponding ingredients * The contact area of staple food dishes should be maximized as much as possible, so it is recommended to cut, slice, beat or even stir the salad. * Cold dishes put forward basic requirements for the gastrointestinal tract. Please use cold dishes when you confirm that there will be no ejaculation or there is time for ejaculation. * The document was written during the COVID-19 epidemic. It is recommended that all ingredients be heated in an environment above 100 degrees Celsius for more than 15 seconds for psychological comfort. If you want to be safe, please avoid cold salads.

Utensils: You can use any container, from porcelain jars to food-grade plastic bags. Notes: * To prevent ingredients from spilling during mixing, it is more appropriate to use a hard container with a volume that is more than twice the volume of all ingredients. * To ensure food safety, please move the ingredients to a porcelain container or metal container as soon as possible after marinating in a plastic bag or bowl. * To ensure food safety, please handle raw food ingredients and accessories on a clean chopping board.

Process: Processing of main vegetable ingredients in slices (this process is optional) (single or multiple choices): Use examples: cabbage, lettuce, cabbage hearts, onions, etc. Tear the ingredients into 4cm 4cm pieces * Cut the ingredients into 0.5cm long strips * Cut off the unused parts of the ingredients and use them whole * Blanch the processed ingredients Notes: You don’t need to peel some ingredients, just cut along the axis and cut along the vertical axis. Those who are confident in the knife skills can cut directly along the vertical axis. Processing of main ingredients of block vegetables (this process is optional) (single or multiple choices): Use examples: potatoes, water chestnuts, cucumbers, potatoes, etc. Cut the ingredients into 0.5cm 0.5cm long strips with a cross-section. Cut the ingredients into 4cm 4cm slices with a thickness less than 0.5cm* Smash or crush the ingredients with a knife (also suitable for cucumbers) * Use the ingredients directly (also suitable for ingredients that are small pieces) * Blanch the processed ingredients. Notes: When smashing the ingredients, it may cause the ingredients to splash. You can wrap them in food-grade plastic bags and smash them. Processing of bulk fungi staple dishes (this process is optional) (single or multiple choices): Use examples: various types of mushrooms, various types of fungus, etc. * Soak the ingredients. Cut the ingredients into 0.5cm 0.5cm cross-section strips Cut the ingredients into 4cm 4cm slices with a thickness less than 0.5cm * Use the ingredients directly (it is also suitable for ingredients that are small pieces) * Blanch the processed ingredients Notes: All fungi need to be strictly confirmed for safety, as soon as they are laid on the board, there will be nothing. Processing of lump meat staple dishes (this process is optional) (single or multiple choices): Use cases: fish, jellyfish, cooked pork, cooked poultry, etc. * Cook the ingredients by steaming, cooking, roasting, frying, etc. * Soak the ingredients in cold water for a while (applicable to seafood) * Tear the ingredients into strips of meat * Cut the ingredients into thin slices (applies to cooked pork) Cut the ingredients into 0.8cm 0.8cm long strips * Some beef, fish, and seafood can be eaten raw after being confirmed to be safe. I am thinking that this is also a category of food processing (this process should be avoided as much as possible) (optional required): Use cases: noodles, rice, fruits, young leaves, etc. * Confirm the safety of the food * Process the food into an edible state * Process the food into a stirrable state Notes: * Please confirm that the food is safe. You can crush a small amount of food and rub it on the upper arm for 30 minutes to detect allergic reactions. If there is any abnormality, it must be discarded * Most leaves and grasses contain ingredients that can cause discomfort, even after cooking, please confirm safety * Most cereals are not conducive to digestion and absorption before being cooked, and may have adverse effects on the gastrointestinal tract Processing of auxiliary materials (this process is optional) (single or multiple choices): Use examples: chilli padi, garlic cloves, ginger, dried chilies, etc. * Remove the stems of chilli padi, wash and cut off the 0.5cm long part of the stem, then chop or cut into sections * Crush the garlic clove and peel it, cut off the 0.5cm long part of the stem and chop or cut it into sections * Peel the ginger and chop or shred or slice it * Crush the dried chili pepper * Put the prepared ingredients into a small bowl or a container that will be used for mixing * Add: various powders, seasonings or pickled sauces to the container, stir evenly Notes: * The types, processing, and methods of auxiliary materials are extremely broad, please do not limit your thinking, but please be careful to verify, use appropriate amounts, and remember safety Mixing ingredients (this process is optional) (single or multiple choices): * Squeeze out the water from meat ingredients with high water content and drain them * Put vegetable ingredients with high water content into a container, add about 200g: 5g of salt and stir, let it sit for 5 minutes, and drain the water * Add ingredients and accessories to the mixing container * Wash and stir with chopsticks, spoons or hands * Seal the container and shake evenly * Tilt the container to an angle where no material will spill out, and rotate the container around the axis. Notes: * Ingredients with high water content may precipitate too much water to dilute the seasoning after being added directly. * If you find that the amount of water is insufficient or the mixing is uneven during mixing, add an appropriate amount of boiled water. If you cannot determine the amount, 15mL each time is better. * It is not recommended to stir some ingredients with high water absorption rates, which may cause the pickled ingredients to taste too strong. Eating (required for this process): * Add the stirred...
Wash the cold vegetables and fully control the moisture, or blanch them lightly in cold water to prevent the finished product from becoming watery and making the taste crisper.
Use hot oil to stir up the fragrance of minced garlic and dried chili peppers, then pour in the ingredients, add seasonings in batches, season first and then add vinegar to prevent bitterness.

Cold vegetables are cooked and eaten immediately. If pickled in advance, they will easily become watery and spoil. They can be refrigerated in the summer, but they should not be stored for a long time.
Case: Crack the cucumbers and marinate them with salt for five minutes. Pour out the seeping water and add vinegar and minced garlic. The texture will be crisper and less likely to become watery.

items.title: Stir fry/fry
body: Utensils: Ordinary metal (iron/stainless steel/aluminum) frying/frying pans or non-stick pans can be used. It is not recommended to use aluminum containers. For details, please refer to the food safety section. Notes: * The method of using an ordinary pot to stir-fry vegetables without sticking: Scramble the eggs first: * Scramble an egg before frying any dish. Do not clean the pan after frying, and the next dish will be non-stick. Hot pot and cool oil method: * Remember to use hot pot with cold oil, heat the pot first * Put nothing in a clean pot, dry it, so that it is heated evenly, and heat it up * Put in the cold oil, rotate the pot, so that the oil covers the entire pot (you can rotate it back and forth to make it heat evenly) * When you see gas coming out of the pot, it means that the oil in the pot has been heated * Pour out the oil, do not brush the pot after pouring out * You can repeat the above steps 2-3 times to get a better non-stick effect * Note: If it is gas, it may spit fire, pay attention to safety. Hot pot double oil method: * First heat the pot * Put nothing in the clean pot, dry it, so that it is heated evenly, and it is hot * Add "a small amount of cold oil" and rotate the pot to make the oil cover the whole pot (you can rotate it back and forth to make it heat evenly) * When you see gas coming out of the pot, it means that the oil in the pot has been heated * Then continue to put in the cold oil and start cooking * Note: If it is gas, it may burst into flames, please pay attention to safety. Supplement: * The purpose is to make the oil cover the bottom of the pot. It is applicable to all household pots on the market. After the oil is added, it will become non-stick in seconds. * Use non-stick pans to fry food without sticking. The functionality of a non-stick pan comes from the coating on its inner wall. Metal spatulas can scratch the coating. Use a wooden or silicone spatula when using nonstick pans to avoid damaging the coating. Process: Turn on the fire - place the pan flat on the fire, heat it - pour the oil into the pan, heat it - add the dishes, stir-fry - remember to add seasonings before taking out the pan Notes: * When judging whether the pan/oil is hot, you can place your hand flat on top of the pan to feel the heat; add ingredients after the oil is hot. *Before pouring oil into the pot, make sure there is no residual water inside the pot. Water can cause hot oil to splash, causing a hazard. * Continuing from the previous article, the ingredients should be drained before being put into the oil pan (egg liquid is fine); similarly, unfrozen ingredients should not be put into the oil pan to avoid danger caused by freezing. * If the oil pan catches fire, do not pour water to extinguish the fire. Doing so will spread the fire. When the fire just starts, turn off the heat quickly and cover the pot.

When frying ingredients, heat the pan with cold oil. Do not flip the ingredients immediately after they are put into the pan. Wait for one side to set before flipping over to reduce the problem of sticking to the pan and breaking the skin.

Control the heat when cooking. Green leafy vegetables should be stir-fried quickly over high heat. For meat stir-fry, you can use starch to mix well in advance to lock in moisture and make the taste more tender.

Drain the surface moisture of the ingredients as much as possible to prevent the hot oil from splashing. Add the ingredients to the pot in batches to avoid lowering the oil temperature when there is a large amount of ingredients in the pot.

Case study: Xiao Zheng, a novice, fried chicken breast. He poured oil into a cold pan and heated it until it started to smoke slightly before adding the ingredients. Frequent flipping caused the meat to stick to the pan and breakage. Later, he switched to a hot pan with cold oil, put it in the pan and let it sit for a while before stir-frying. The chicken breast was completely non-stick and tasted fresh and tender.

items.title: Blanch
items.core: Blanching is a process in cooking, pronounced chāo shuǐ. Blanching refers to heating the preliminary processed raw materials in a boiling water pot until they are half-cooked or fully cooked, and then taking them out for further cooking or seasoning. Blanching is an indispensable process in cooking, especially cold dishes. It plays a key role in the color, aroma and taste of dishes, especially the color. Most vegetables and meats with a fishy smell need to be blanched.
body: Operation: Boiling water in a boiling pot: Blanching in a boiling water pot means heating the water in the pot and then adding the raw materials to the pot. After putting it in the pot, stir it in time. The time should be short and don't overdo it. This method is mostly used for plant-based raw materials, such as celery, spinach, lettuce, etc. Pay special attention to the heat when blanching. If the time is longer, the color will become lighter and it will not be crispy or tender. Therefore, after putting it in the pot, when the water is slightly boiling, you can take it out and let it cool. - Leafy vegetable raw materials should be blanched before slicing to avoid excessive loss of nutrients. - When blanching, the water should be wide and the heat strong, so that the pot can be opened in time after adding the raw materials; when blanching green leafy vegetables, they should be boiled slightly and taken out. - Vegetable raw materials should be cooled and dried immediately after blanching to prevent them from turning yellow and overcooked due to residual heat. - When blanching vegetables, you can add an appropriate amount of salad oil such as peanut oil, corn oil, and soybean oil to keep them green. Cold water pot blanch: Cold water pot blanch is to put the raw materials and cold water into the pot at the same time. The water should cover the raw materials and then boil. The purpose is to mature the raw materials for further processing. Potatoes, carrots, etc. are not easy to mature due to their large size, so they need to be cooked for a longer time. Some animal raw materials, such as white meat, beef belly, tripe collar, etc., are also heated and matured in a cold water pot before further processing. Some animal raw materials used to cook soup also need to be boiled in cold water. During the heating process, the nutrients will gradually overflow to make the soup delicious. If a hot water pot is used, the protein will coagulate. - The amount of water added to the pot should not be too much, so as to submerge the raw materials. - During the gradual heating process, the raw materials must be turned frequently to ensure that the raw materials are heated evenly and achieve the purpose of blanching.

Additional notes: - Blanching sometimes causes some unstable and soluble nutrients in the raw materials to overflow, especially the water-soluble vitamins in fresh vegetables that are more susceptible to loss - Animal raw materials and plant raw materials should be blanched separately; those with heavier color and flavor should be blanched separately from those with lighter color and flavor; large lumps should be blanched separately from small lumps to prevent mutual odors - After blanching animal raw materials, the soup can be used as fresh soup after skimming and clarification. Blanching of meat: - The meat raw materials can change color after being blanched in boiling water. Remove and drain the water before proceeding to the next step of cooking. - After blanching the meat, you need to wash off the blood foam stains attached to it. Remember to wash it with warm water, otherwise the heat expansion and contraction of the meat will absorb the stains, making it impossible to clean off the blood foam. Blanching of vegetables: - When washing vegetables, sprinkle some salt in the water to wash out the bugs in the vegetables - The vegetables after blanching should be immersed in cold water immediately to maintain the color and taste. If you don't soak the vegetables in cold water, the vegetables will no longer be crisp due to the residual heat of the boiling water, and will appear rotten.
Blanching green leafy vegetables with a small amount of salt and cooking oil can lock in chlorophyll, keep the ingredients bright in color, and avoid yellowing and wilting.
Blanch the meat in cold water and gradually heat it up to force out the blood inside; place the vegetables in boiling water and shorten the heating time to retain the crispiness.
The blanching time should not be too long. Remove the vegetables as soon as they are raw. Skim off any foam on the surface of the meat. Rinse the impurities with warm water after removing them.

Case: Xiao Zhou makes cold broccoli. Boil the water and add a little salt and cooking oil. Add the broccoli and blanch it for two minutes. Take it out immediately and immerse it in cold water. The cauliflower remains green and crisp. It has a bright color after being cold with seasonings and does not turn yellow or soft.

items.title: cook
body: Process: Pour water into the pot - turn on the heat, put the pot on the fire to heat - the water is boiling (the water is rolling and there are a lot of bubbles coming out) and then add the ingredients. Notes: * Covering the pot when heating can speed up the heating. But doing so runs the risk of overflowing the pot. After continuous heating, excessively churning fluid may come out of the pot, which is called overflow. * If the pot is about to overflow, immediately turn down the heat and open the lid. * If you want to speed up the heating and avoid overflowing of the pot, you can half-open the lid to leave a gas outlet; you can also turn down the heat later and pay attention to the situation in the pot at all times. * According to cooking needs, the ingredients can also be placed in cold water. However, it will take longer to boil the water.

Put porridge and grains into the pot under cold water and slowly raise the temperature to allow the ingredients to fully absorb the water. The cooked food will be soft and glutinous and less likely to be cooked.
Put the noodles and dumplings into the pot under boiling water, and add cold water twice in the middle to allow the dough to heat evenly to avoid overcooking and making the soup base turbid.

Pay attention to the amount of water during the cooking process. If the water evaporates quickly, add warm water in time. Do not add cold water directly to prevent the food from shrinking and hardening.

Case: My mother, Ms. Chen, cooked millet porridge, put the rice under cold water, brought to a boil over high heat, then turned to low heat and simmered slowly, stirring occasionally to prevent the bottom from burning.
