After 40 minutes, the porridge was dense and sticky, the rice grains bloomed, and the rice oil was rich. The family drank it to warm their stomachs and feel comfortable.

items.title: Learn to use a knife
items.core: This is a knife tutorial for beginners in the home kitchen. The goal is to cut stably, in the right size, clean and safe, and not to pursue speed. Read safety and knife holding before choosing the ingredients to be processed; when encountering hard bones, hard shells, or frozen solid foods, change tools or purchase pre-processed ingredients.
body: Before you start: Prepare the kitchen first: 1. Keep the countertop bright and clean, clear enough space; keep children and pets away from the operating area. Stop using the knife when you are tired, after drinking alcohol, or when you have difficulty concentrating. 2. Wash and dry your hands. Check whether the handle of the knife is loose and whether the blade is chipped. If any damage is found, stop using it. Greasy and slippery hands cannot hold the knife directly. 3. Choose a complete, flat wooden or food contact plastic cutting board. Place a non-slip mat or a wrung-out damp cloth under the cutting board and push it with your hand to make sure it won't slip. Do not cut on glass, stone, or porcelain plates. 4. Place the ingredients to be cut, finished product bowls and waste bowls, and do not let the front edge of the cutting board protrude from the countertop. When not in use, keep the knife flat on the board away from the edge, with the blade facing toward the untouched side. 5. Use separate knife boards for raw meat, raw fish, cooked food, and ready-to-eat fruits and vegetables; if there is only one set, cook the ready-to-eat food first. After handling the raw meat, wash it thoroughly and disinfect it according to the instructions of the cleaning product before changing tasks. 6. Cut only a small amount at a time. Take raw meat out of the refrigerator in batches, refrigerate or cook it immediately after cutting; do not leave it at room temperature for a long time for practice.

Safety habits that must be developed: - If the knife falls, step away, never reach out to catch it, and never use your foot to block it. Wait for the knife to fall firmly before picking it up. - Do not point at people with a knife, gesture, or turn around to speak; put down the knife first before removing food, answering the phone, or opening a cabinet door. - Do not hide knives under dishwater, foam, rags or ingredients. Don't leave knives scattered in a drawer. - Try to operate in a fixed position. When you must move, keep the tip of the knife downward and avoid yourself and others. Do not lift heavy objects with the other hand at the same time; do not squeeze through the crowd. - When passing the knife, place it on a stable surface first and wait for the other person to hold the knife handle before taking it away. Don't hand the tip of the knife to someone else. - No need for a kitchen knife to open cans, pry bottle caps, twist screws, peel hard shells or unpack. Stop exerting force when the knife is stuck, do not twist the knife, knock the back of the knife, or lift the food with the knife to hit the board. - A sharp knife can still hurt someone; "keep it sharp" is to reduce slippage and brute force, but it does not mean that you can relax your hand guard. - Cut-resistant gloves do not protect against all punctures and cuts; if used, choose products suitable for food contact and the right size, wash according to instructions, and still need to be held correctly.

Types of knives: Select by task: | Knives | What is suitable for | What is not suitable for | | --- | --- | --- | | Chinese sliced knives, mulberry knives | Slicing and shredding vegetables and boneless meat; wide blade for easy transfer of ingredients | Chopping bones, cutting hard frozen meat; wide appearance does not mean that it can chop bones | Prying shells, twisting and cutting hard bones, thin blades are especially vulnerable | | Santoku knife | Daily cutting of vegetables, fish, and boneless meat | Forced fulcrum of the knife tip to cut, vigorous chopping of bones | Chopping bones; the other hand should be kept away from the path when sawing with a long knife | | Deboning knife, fish filleting knife | Skilled people carve out meat and fillet fish along the bones; the degree of softness and hardness depends on the purpose | Novices hold the meat with bare hands and cut toward the palm | Cut hard bones beyond the rated purpose; cut cooked food without washing it after use | Beginners usually buy a stable main knife, a small knife and a stable cutting board; often eat bread and add a serrated knife. You don’t have to buy a whole set of knives to get started. Read the instructions first, and then check whether the length, weight, and handle fit your hands. A blade that is too long or too heavy will make it more difficult to control. Stainless steel knives can also rust; carbon steel knives need to be wiped dry in time. The normal oxidation and discoloration of the surface is different from the reddish-brown rust spots. Ceramic knives are hard and brittle and are not suitable for twisting, chopping garlic, cutting bones, or freezing food. Knife sharpening is usually left to professionals.

Understanding the knife and how to hold it: Knife hand: Stability first: The back of the knife is the thick edge opposite to the blade, the tip is at the front, and the heel is close to the handle. The heels of some knives are also very sharp and your fingers cannot go under the cutting edge. Whole-hand grip: wrap the handle of the knife with your fingers, and naturally stabilize your thumb to prevent your fingers from sliding forward to the blade. Suitable for those who are just starting to practice or those who are not suitable for pinch grip. Pinch grip method: Gently pinch the sides of the blade near the handle with your thumb and index finger, and wrap the other fingers around the handle; keep your fingertips away from the lower edge. It is suitable for use when the knife shape allows and the hand feels stable. Do not pinch the tip or edge of the knife or extend forward excessively. The grip strength should be as long as the knife does not rotate. Do not hold it until your wrist becomes stiff. Keep your wrists as natural as possible and your shoulders relaxed; if the food is too high or too hard, change the shape of the food first instead of raising your arms to add force. Auxiliary hand: The cat claw hand is not an armor: 1. Bend the fingertips toward the palm and hold the ingredients with the fingertips, with the knuckles facing the side of the knife. 2. Keep your thumb behind the food and do not extend it in front of the knife edge; do not open your little finger. 3. The side of the knife can be lightly bent by the joint of the finger as a position reference, but the cutting edge is always lower than the leading joint. Do not lift the knife high over the joint. 4. Every time you make a cut, let the knife stop first, and then move your auxiliary hand back a little; do not move your hand while chasing the knife. 5. Stop when there are very short pieces left, lay them flat and change directions, or keep them for other uses. No need to cut to the last millimeter. When encountering slippery meat, round ingredients, or small pieces that cannot be stably grasped by your fingers, first wipe off excess water on the surface, make a flat bottom, or change tools. Don't just rely on your "cat's claw" to forcefully cut.

Basic knife skills and size: The size is used to help understanding, not a unified standard; it is subject to the specific recipe and doneness requirements. The same ingredients in the same pot should be of the same size as much as possible to avoid being mushy on the outside and hard on the inside. | Knife techniques | Methods | Common uses and examples | --- | --- | --- | | Slicing | Use a flat-bottomed board, advance the knife steadily and withdraw gradually | Fried potato slices can be practiced starting from about 2-3 mm; the thickness can be adjusted according to the recipe | The diced side dishes can be practiced from about 1 cm; do not stack too many layers at the same time | | Cut into pieces | Divide into pieces of similar size | Stews are usually larger than those for stir-frying, please refer to the recipe | Ginger, garlic, herbs; do not put the assistant hand near the cutting edge | | Pull cutting, push cutting | The blade cuts in with horizontal movement, not vertical pressure all the time | Boneless meat, soft vegetables; the movement range cannot touch the other hand | A straight blade does not have to imitate the action of a curved chef's knife. Preferably use a scraper or hands to transfer ingredients. When using the cutting board, stop the knife first and keep the cutting edge away from your fingers to avoid dulling the cutting edge caused by scraping it across the cutting board. Do not rub your fingers along the blade to remove stuck food.

Cut vegetables: Start from a stable surface: potatoes, carrots, white radish: flat bottom first, then slice into dices: 1. Wash, peel as needed, and remove the inedible parts. Do not use potatoes that are green or obviously sprouted or spoiled for practice or consumption. 2. Cylindrical carrots can be cut into manageable segments first; cut off a thin slice to form a flat bottom, then cut with the flat bottom facing down. 3. Cut slices of similar thickness first. When shredding, only stack a small number of smooth slices. If there is any slippage, spread it out and cut one by one. 4. Cut into cubes first to obtain equal width strips, then cut crosswise. Do not chop down long radishes while they are standing upright. Onions: Beginners do not need to cut across the palm: 1. Remove the outer skin and dry top, and cut in half along the root direction; stabilize the onion when making the first cut, and cut out small planes if necessary. 2. Place half an onion cut side down and root end toward the back. Make several cuts along the direction from the top to the root, leaving a little connection near the root. 3. Turn and dice crosswise, taking advantage of the onion's own layers without adding a horizontal knife toward the palm of your hand. 4. Stop near the root end, and lay the ends that are difficult to fix alone or discard them. Don't cut onions with your eyes closed. When tears affect your vision, put down the knife and step away from the chopping board, and then continue after you recover. Green peppers, sweet peppers, and capsicums: Place the peppers firmly, cut them lengthwise, lay them flat, remove the seeds and white inner ribs, and then cut them into strips or dices. When the leather surface is slippery, turn the inside side up. Avoid touching your eyes after handling peppers; use food contact gloves, wash hands and clean knife blades afterward. Tomatoes, eggplants, and cucumbers: Use a sharp thin-edged knife to gently pull tomatoes, or lightly saw them with a serrated knife. Do not apply sudden force due to slippage. Remove the stems of cucumbers and eggplants first, then cut them lengthwise into stable bottoms or lay them flat in half. When making the hob block, cut a small amount and stop the knife rotation one after another to prevent the ingredients from rolling towards the knife edge. Leafy vegetables, onions and herbs: Wash and drain excess water first, and remove bad leaves. Stack a small amount of leafy vegetables, roll them lightly and then cut them into sections or shreds. Do not roll them into a high pile. Cut the scallions into short sections and align them. Reduce the quantity when the scallions are white and slippery. Gather the herbs first and then cut them. Do not reach out to pick up the loose leaves when the knife falls. Ginger, garlic and mushrooms: Cut the ginger into flat pieces, slice it first, shred it and then mince it. Garlic can be peeled and sliced, minced, or used a garlic press; it is not recommended for beginners to imitate slamming garlic with a knife, especially ceramic knives or thin crisp knives. Remove the unnecessary roots from the mushrooms, halve the large mushrooms and cut them side down; if the small mushrooms are difficult to fix, you can keep them whole and cook them according to the recipe. Harder ingredients such as pumpkin, winter melon, and corn: The most important thing for large pumpkins and hard-skinned melons is stability and tool matching. Beginners should give priority to buying cut pieces; do not hit the back of the knife, step on the knife, or hit the board with the knife in order to cut. When the knife gets stuck after entering, it stops without twisting the blade left and right. A special thresher can be used for corn kernels. When using a knife, first obtain a small, stable section that can be laid flat, fix it at a low position, keep the blade away from the hand holding the object, and cut off each side; if it cannot be stably fixed, buy ready-made corn kernels. Do not peel the whole corn on a smooth surface while standing it up.

Cut meat: Look at the texture and whether it is bone-free: boneless beef, pork: Slice against the grain: The long, parallel fibers on the meat are the texture. Cutting against the grain is to make the cuts across the fibers and shorten the long fibers in each bite of meat; it is not to cut in a certain direction of the body. 1. Thaw raw meat under refrigerated conditions; do not cut hard frozen meat, and do not leave it at room temperature for a long time to soften. 2. Wipe off excess juice on the surface, use a knife blade specially designed for raw meat, and put the cut meat into a container promptly. 3. Look at the direction of the fibers and place the meat in a position where it is easy to cross the fibers. If there is no flat bottom, first divide it into pieces that can be laid flat stably. 4. Use a steady force to cut into slices of similar thickness; the fried pork slices can be made from about 2-4 mm, and still adjust according to the recipe. Do not hold the meat in the air with your hands and pull it tightly before cutting it with your hands. 5. For shredding, you can slice it first and then cut it into strips; for stew, cut it into pieces of similar size. The fiber direction may change in different parts, turn the meat and observe again. "Cut the cow crosswise and the pig vertically" cannot replace observing the parts and recipes. Whether to go against the grain, how thick to cut, and whether the shape needs to be maintained must be combined with the requirements of the finished dish; for quick-fried boneless meat that needs to be tender, shortening the fiber is usually easier to chew. Chicken breast, chicken leg and bone-in poultry: Lay the chicken breast flat, remove the obvious fascia and then slice or block it; beginners can buy thin-cut meat without pressing their palms on the meat to slice it horizontally. Prioritize buying boneless chicken legs, unfold them and cut them into pieces. Do not use a knife to cut joints, leg bones or frozen chicken pieces. Ask the merchant to cut them into pieces. Do not rinse raw chicken to avoid splashing and contaminating the surrounding area. After cutting raw poultry, wash your hands, knife board, countertop and handles that have been touched; plates that have been filled with raw meat should not be directly filled with cooked meat. Cutting meat thin does not mean it is cooked safely. Cooking still needs to follow recipes and food safety requirements. Fish, shrimp and seafood: For starters, boneless fish fillets are preferred. Wipe off excess water from the fish fillets, lay them flat, and gently pull and cut them to avoid crushing the meat. If you find fish bones, use special fish bone pliers to remove them and inspect them. Don't just rely on the "boneless" label to omit observation. Deboning and skinning whole fish and shelling shellfish involves sliding, prodding and special tools, allowing merchants to handle them. You can use kitchen scissors to trim the back of the shrimp, and then pick out the part that needs to be removed; do not hold it in the palm of your hand and stab it with a sharp knife. Oysters, coconuts, crab shells, etc. cannot be pried hard with an ordinary kitchen knife. Cooked meat and leftovers: Use a clean knife board that does not come into contact with raw meat to cut cooked meat, and slice according to the texture of the meat and the requirements of the recipe. Do not use your hands to press the hot meat that has just come out of the pan. Bring it to a suitable operating temperature before cutting it. Also avoid leaving it at room temperature for a long time. Refrigerate cut leftovers promptly and properly.

Fruit, bread, tofu and other ingredients: apples, pears, citrus: wash and cut on the board. Cut flat surfaces out of apples and pears first, then divide them into segments, lay them flat and remove the core; do not hold the fruit segments in the palm of your hand to peel the core. The citrus can be peeled by hand. When slicing is needed, cut out a stable base first. Avocados, mangoes and pitted fruits: Special tools can be used first for ripe avocados. When using a knife, stabilize the fruit on a cutting board, slowly cut around the core, stop the knife and separate the two halves with your hands, and then use a spoon to remove the core and pulp. Do not hold half a fruit in the palm of your hand, chop the core with a knife or pick the core with the tip of the knife. First form a stable bottom surface of the mango, and divide the pulp along both sides of the flat core; when cutting into small pieces, take the pulp from the skin to the board and then cut. Do not hold the peel to make grids, as the tip of the knife may pierce the skin and prick your hand. Cut the peaches, plums, etc. and separate them with your hands or take out the core with a spoon instead of prying them hard with a knife. Watermelon, pineapple and hard-shelled fruits: For large watermelons and pineapples, consider the weight and cutting board size first; if you can’t control it, buy in cut portions. When it can be operated stably, form a flat bottom first, then divide it into small pieces and then trim it. Do not chop hard sideways on large, rolling, intact fruits. Hard shells such as coconuts require specialized tools and operating conditions that ordinary kitchen knives are not suitable for. Bread, cakes, tofu and cheese: Use a serrated knife to lightly saw the bread, keeping the hand holding the bread away from the front and back of the knife; the force will be reduced as you go to the lower layer to avoid sudden penetration. Cut the cake smoothly with a long clean knife, and then wipe off any attachments after stopping the knife. Place the tofu lightly on the board and cut into pieces with a thin and sharp knife without squeezing with your hands; when the cheese sticks to the knife, reduce the thickness of the cut or use a suitable cheese knife and do not twist the knife to pry off the large pieces. Use special clamps to handle hard nut shells, and do not use a kitchen knife to chop ice cubes and hard candies.

Cleaning, drying and storage: 1. Dispose of the knife separately immediately after use, holding the knife handle and keeping the blade away from the body and the other hand. 2. Clean with warm water, mild detergent and a cleaning tool that will not easily scratch the blade surface. The cleaning direction should avoid the cutting edge. Do not wrap the blade with a sponge or rag and stroke it back and forth, nor wipe the cutting edge with bare hands. 3. The knife board contaminated by raw food should be decontaminated and cleaned first, and then operate according to the instructions of the applicable disinfection product; the concentration, contact time and whether to rinse are subject to the product requirements, and detergents cannot be mixed at will. 4. After rinsing, carefully dry the blade surface, handle joint and handle, avoiding the blade. Do not soak for a long time, and it is not recommended to put it in the dishwasher, especially knives with wooden handles, carbon steel, or knives that the manufacturer prohibits machine washing. 5. After it is completely dry, place the scabbard, knife holder or drawer with independent slots. The knife holder also needs to be clean and dry; the magnetic holder needs to be secure, out of the reach of children, and placed according to the manufacturer's instructions to avoid collision with the blade. Maintain the wooden handle according to the manufacturer's instructions and use maintenance products that are allowed to come into contact with food; do not apply industrial engine oil yourself. Wash and dry carbon steel knives as soon as possible after cutting acidic food. Whether to apply a thin layer of anti-rust oil for food contact during long-term storage depends on the instructions. Clean before use. If you find rust, cracks, loose handle, or obvious chipping, you should repair or replace it first.

Knife sharpening, trimming and judging sharpness: when maintenance is needed: The same ingredients require more effort, cutting tomatoes is always slippery, and crushing onion leaves instead of cutting them are all reminders that the blade may need maintenance. Also check whether you have chosen the wrong knife, the cutting board is slippery, or the ingredients do not have a flat bottom. Do not run the blade with your fingers, shave or cut paper on your hand for testing. You can use normal ingredients and normal cutting methods on the board to observe whether it is smooth; if there is a chip, do not continue to try cutting. The difference between a sharpening rod and a whetstone: Some steel sharpening rods mainly help to tidy up slightly offset edges; ceramic rods and diamond rods may also grind away metal. Different knife materials, hardness and blade shapes have different requirements for tools. Japanese thin-blade, single-edged knives or ceramic knives cannot copy the maintenance methods of other knives. A whetstone restores the edge by grinding away a small amount of material. There is no uniform number for angle that is suitable for all knives. Priority should be given to following the manufacturer's instructions for single-sided angle, blade type and grinding tool. Mistaking the double-sided angle for the single-sided angle will damage the blade. Maintenance process for beginners: 1. Check the tool description to confirm whether it can be sharpened by yourself, suitable grinding tools and angles. When in doubt, leave it to a professional knife sharpening service. 2. Fix the grinding stone or guide sharpener on the non-slip base. The table should be clean and well-lit. Follow the instructions on the grinding tool whether to soak, add water or use oil. Do not soak all the grinding stones in water. 3. Use a guide tool or use the learned steady motion to sharpen gently, keeping your fingers away from the path of the blade. Don’t hang the sharpening stick in the air to perform rapid swings. 4. Do not press hard or grind out an edge that is too thin for the sake of sharpness; leave serrated knives, single-edged knives and ceramic knives to people who are familiar with the corresponding knife types for maintenance. 5. After finishing, clean the metal grinding chips on the cutter and table, dry them and put them away. The feel of the sharpened knife will change. Start by cutting a small amount of food slowly. The frequency of knife sharpening depends on the intensity of use, knife material, cutting board and technique. It does not have to be a fixed number of days. Using a suitable cutting board, avoiding lateral scraping of the blade, and storing it separately are often more important than frequent sharpening.

Common troubleshooting: | Problem | Check first | More secure handling | | --- | --- | --- | | Ingredients rolling | No flat bottom, the board is too slippery | Stop the knife, make a flat bottom, and fix the cutting board | Reduce the quantity, stop once and start with thick slices | | Meat is crushed | Knife is dull, meat is too soft, keep pressing downwards | Keep it refrigerated to keep it strong, change to a sharp knife to cut smoothly | Ingredients stick to the knife | The cut surface is wet or starchy | Use a suitable tool to remove it after stopping the knife and do not wipe it along the blade

|Practice in stages: no time, no faster: 1. In the first stage, only practice setting the table, holding the knife, cat's claw hand and stopping the knife. Choose half a cucumber or a medium-hard vegetable that is easy to fix and cut into a small number of thick slices. 2. In the second stage, use flat-bottomed potatoes to make slices, strips, and cubes. Just check that the size is close to each other. Do not pursue thinness like hair. 3. In the third stage, practice diced onions, shredded peppers and leafy vegetables to feel the stabilization of different ingredients. 4. In the fourth stage, practice boneless meat slices on a separate meat cutting board. First identify the texture, then cut a small amount, and finally complete cleaning and disinfection. 5. Review at the end of each session: whether the chopping board moved, whether the thumb was exposed, whether the knife was pressed with force, whether the cutter stopped actively when cutting to the small end, and whether the knife was put away in time. At each stage, being able to move slowly slowly is the prerequisite for entering the next stage. Minors should be given face-to-face guidance by adults with operational capabilities and should choose appropriate tools and tasks based on their age and ability.

In case of accidental cut: Put down the knife immediately and stop touching the food. Small wounds can be stopped by continuous direct pressure with clean dressings or cloths; if there is something stuck in the wound and you do not remove it yourself or press it directly on the foreign object, you should apply pressure around it and seek medical attention. When the dressing is soaked, add a layer on top to avoid opening it repeatedly to look at it. After hemostasis, small and superficial wounds can be rinsed with clean running water, the surrounding skin cleaned, and then covered with sterile dressings. Discard food contaminated by wounds and clean contaminated surfaces. Do not add salt, coffee powder, or use food remedies to wounds. If you have uncontrollable bleeding, spurting bleeding, deep wounds, serious injuries to your palms, numbness, limited movement, or foreign objects, seek medical help immediately; dial 120 for emergencies in mainland China. If subsequent redness, swelling, pus discharge, fever, etc. occur, you should also seek medical attention, and medical staff will evaluate the need for infection and tetanus prevention. Text tutorials are not a substitute for on-site first aid training.

Data source and graphic description: The following information is used to check general safety, maintenance and first aid principles; the specific cutting methods of ingredients are original arrangements for home kitchens and are not verbatim translations. Viewed October 18, 2026. - UK Health and Safety Executive: Safe kitchen knives: suitable knives, stable cutting surface, safe carrying and storage, do not catch dropped knives. - UK Food Standards Agency: Avoid cross-contamination: the spread of contamination between food, tools and work surfaces. - Zwilling: Use and care of knives: hand wash, dry, avoid dishwasher damage and store independently; other brands still refer to their instructions. - NHS: Cuts and scrapes: stop bleeding, clean coverage and signs of urgent medical attention. The text of this article and the three schematic diagrams are the original content of this contribution and are provided under The Unlicense. External materials are only for reference links and do not include reproduced images; schematic diagrams are used to explain layout, cutting shape and fiber direction, and do not represent true proportions, nor do they replace live action demonstrations.

Case: Xiao Li, a newbie in the kitchen, cuts potatoes for the first time. He presses the fingers of his left hand against the ingredients, holds the kitchen knife firmly with his right hand and cuts vertically, slowly cutting into even thin slices without cutting his hand in the whole process. The cut potato slices are of the same thickness and are evenly heated in the pot without becoming mushy.

items.title: Marinate (meat)
body: Note: The marinating described here is the step of processing the ingredients before cooking, and is not the preparation of finished products such as bacon or pickled sausages

Marining: Marinating meat before cooking is a common method to pre-flavor the meat. Generally, the object of pickling is raw meat. According to the needs of the dishes, you can determine the size of the meat knife. For example, fried chicken popcorn, the chicken breast is cut into dice-sized pieces and then put into a bowl for marinating. For example, roasted whole lamb, leg of lamb, half fan or whole fan of lamb can be marinated with a large amount of seasonings on the surface without changing the knife. Depending on the dish, the seasonings and accessories selected for pickling can be of any type. Sometimes the auxiliary ingredients may also need to be pre-processed for different flavors.

Basic concept of pickling: What is introduced here is the normal pickling process. - Generally speaking, the larger the amount of meat (such as marinating 5kg chicken wings at one time), the larger the volume (such as a whole leg of lamb), and the stronger the taste, the more seasonings and accessories are needed - Generally speaking, the longer the marinating time is planned, the less seasonings and accessories are used - When marinating, the ingredients should be evenly covered on all surfaces. If it is sliced ​​meat or shredded meat, you should try to grasp and stir it evenly with your hands. If it is a whole leg of lamb, the surface should be brushed evenly with your hands or a brush - generally stir-fried and fried meat needs to be marinated in advance. Stir-fried meat should ensure a fresh and tender texture, and cooking often requires high heat and a short time. When cooking for a short time is not easy to taste, pickling in advance can make up for the lack of taste

Pickling techniques: - Thin shreds of meat, thin slices of meat: Because the meat is fragile, it needs to be as gentle as possible. Use your fingers in the shape of claw machine pliers to gently grasp the marinade evenly. Then stir gently in one direction until evenly mixed - shredded pork, sliced ​​meat, chunks of meat: the method is the same as above, but the force can be slightly stronger - chicken legs, chicken wings, etc.: first make a few cuts on the ingredients. The roots of chicken wings and drumsticks can be pierced with a knife. Then mix the marinade in a bowl first, then put the ingredients into the bowl and wrap them evenly - Lamb leg and other sizes: generally you can pierce the thicker part of the meat. Then mix the marinade and apply it evenly on the surface of the ingredients

Marinization container and time: - Choose a container that can hold the ingredients and marinade. Including bowls, plates, trays, etc. At this time, it is open pickling, which usually takes a short time, with a common pickling time of 0.5-2 hours. (Grilled) lamb legs, etc. can also be marinated in this way, but the time will be longer - you can choose a large enough food sealing bag for marinating. At this time, it is sealed and marinated, usually for a long time, such as overnight marinating, or marinating ribs that are not easy to taste. Common 4 hours-overnight. At this time, the ingredients used should be slightly reduced to prevent the finished dish from being too heavy and salty

Commonly used pickling ingredients: - Light soy sauce: to make the sauce fragrant and have a salty bottom taste. Can be used for almost all meats - dark soy sauce: not too salty, but easy to stain. Used to tone and enhance fragrance. Generally, it should not be used in large quantities to avoid producing a beany smell. Can be used for almost all red meats (less commonly used), pork liver, etc. You can add more - salt: salty but no sauce flavor after frying. Can be used for all meats - White (granulated) sugar: to sweeten the taste (large amounts), and also add tenderness to the meat (low amounts). It can be used on all poultry and livestock meats, but is less commonly used on fish and seafood. - Brown sugar: adds sweetness and unique taste to brown sugar, slightly heavier than white sugar. Can be used for almost all meats (generally darker meat or darker finished dishes) - Oyster sauce: adds fresh, salty and sweet taste. Typically used on red meat - white/rice vinegar: adds a sour taste. Rarely used - aged vinegar/balsamic vinegar: not only has a sour taste, but also adds flavor and color to dishes. Balsamic vinegar is more suitable for dark-colored fish (especially grilled fish) - cooking wine: removes fishy smell and adds flavor. Can be used on almost all meats. However, please note when using it: - The flavor of cooking wine itself is very strong and can easily cover up the aroma of the ingredients. For ingredients that do not have a strong fishy smell, you may consider not using cooking wine to remove the fishy smell. For example: beef, fish and chicken. - For chicken, white wine can be used instead of cooking wine. - For beef, you can use ginger and scallion water instead of cooking wine. - For white fish, you only need to clean the blood and mucous membranes so that there will be no fishy smell. It is recommended not to add cooking wine. - Rice wine: removes fishy smell and increases aroma. The effect is better than that of cooking wine, and the aroma is more complex than that of cooking wine. Generally used for white meats. Red meat can also be used, but the effect is equivalent to cooking wine. - Five-spice powder/Thirteen spices: It is the simplest compound spice to add flavor to meat. Five-spice powder only adds fragrance, while the fragrance of thirteen-spice powder is more unique and recognizable. The amount used for pickling with such spices should be controlled. Can be used on almost all meats, but less commonly on fish and seafood - Paprika: There are many types of paprika. Regardless of the type of chili pepper, there are chili powder/chili noodles, crushed chili peppers, etc. according to the grinding fineness. In addition to adding spiciness to meat, it can also add color to finished dishes. Dishes pickled with chili peppers should avoid excessive amounts of chili peppers. It can be used for almost all meats that require a spicy base, but the cooking time should be slightly controlled to prevent the pepper from becoming bitter or darkening in color - cumin powder and cumin powder: generally ground powder is used as a marinade instead of granules, which can make the meat easier to taste. Can be used on almost all red meat and chicken - X Paprika: Adds pungent, spicy, fragrant and choking taste to meat. It should be used in moderation to avoid overpowering other flavors - black pepper: spicy and spicy. Can be used on almost all red meats - White pepper: spicy and fragrant. Slightly weaker than black pepper, it highlights the aroma. Can be used for almost all meats - Sichuan peppercorns: spicy and choking taste. It has the special aroma of Sichuan peppercorns, which is more recognizable. Can be used for almost all meats - Doubanjiang: adds the sauce aroma, salty and spicy taste of beans to meat. Can be used in almost all red meats - onion, ginger, and garlic: onion and ginger remove fishiness and flavor, remove odor; garlic adds spicy flavor. Onions can be cut into sections or slices as needed; ginger is generally sliced, but in some cases it needs to be peeled; garlic can be sliced ​​or chopped. If you don’t want onion and ginger to appear in the finished dish, or if you need a lighter taste, you can put the onion and ginger pieces in a bowl with a very small amount of water to squeeze out the juice, and marinate the meat with the onion and ginger water. Garlic is generally not added directly. Can be used on all meats - seafood sauce, shrimp paste, etc.: adds fresh and salty flavor to meat. The seafood sauce tastes sweet, and the shrimp sauce tastes heavy. Can be used on almost all meats, but there are not many usage scenarios - Tempeh: Adds the aroma and salty taste of fermented beans to meat. Can be used in almost all red meats, but not many are used - Cornstarch: This is starch. Cornstarch is an important marinade for sizing. The thicker the sizing, or the smoother the taste, the more cornstarch is needed. Can be used on almost all meats. Cornstarch can be used as a simple fried coating (generally, flour, etc. need to be added as needed). At this time, it is generally not added during pickling. - Corn starch and potato starch: generally have the highest viscosity. - Sweet potato starch: slightly lower viscosity. - Oil: Add an appropriate amount of oil for sealing during pickling, which can lock in moisture and flavor. If you use an open container to marinate for a long time (such as in a bowl), the oil seal can greatly ensure that the meat does not dry out or become woody. Can be used on almost all meats. The base oil should be slightly reduced when frying after sealing, but there is no difference when frying.

Several common pickling formulas: - Beef: Use an appropriate amount of light soy sauce, a small amount of cooking wine, and a small amount of white sugar for pickling. According to taste, use salt (to add saltiness), oyster sauce and a very small amount of seafood sauce (beef in oyster sauce), five-spice powder/shisanxiang (fried beef with onions). Use onions and ginger with caution - Chicken (including chicken breasts and wings): Use an appropriate amount of light soy sauce, a smaller amount of white sugar, and a small amount of cooking wine to marinate. According to taste, use salt (to add saltiness), five-spice powder/sanxiang (fried chicken popcorn), and a very small amount of dark soy sauce (for pan-fried chicken wings) - White fish: use an appropriate amount of salt and a small amount of cooking wine/rice wine to marinate. According to taste, choose seafood sauce/seafood soy sauce/steamed fish soy sauce (fried hairtail), onion and ginger (water) (grilled fish with skin) - Red fish: Use an appropriate amount of light soy sauce and a small amount of cooking wine to marinate. According to taste, choose seafood soy sauce/a small amount of steamed fish soy sauce (fried salmon), brown sugar (Nordic grilled salmon) - Pork liver: use an appropriate amount of light soy sauce and an appropriate amount of cooking wine to marinate. Use cornstarch, appropriate amount of dark soy sauce (fried pork liver), a small amount of sugar, etc. according to taste

Practical examples of dishes: - Stir-fried beef with onions: Take 150g of beef for one person as an example. The beef should be sliced until it feels tender and needs to be stir-fried - 10ml of light soy sauce (about 2 tablespoons) - 5ml of cooking wine (about 1 tablespoon) - 2.5-10g of white sugar (about 1-4 teaspoons, depending on the sweetness of taste) - 5g of cumin powder (about 2 teaspoons) - 10-15g of cornstarch (about 1 small handful) - 10ml of oil (about 10ml of oil) 2 tablespoons) - (optional) Thirteen spices 1g (about 0.5 teaspoon) - (optional) black pepper 1g (about 0.5 teaspoon) - Beef in oyster sauce: Take 150g beef for one person as an example. The beef should be sliced until the finished dish feels tender and well-coated. This dish tastes sweet and needs to be fried - 5ml light soy sauce (about 1 tablespoon) - 5ml cooking wine (about 1 tablespoon) - 10-20ml oyster sauce (about 2-4 tablespoons, choose according to the saltiness of taste, oyster sauce is salty) - 5-15g white sugar (about 2-6 teaspoons, choose according to the sweetness of taste) - Cornstarch 25-35g (about 1 large handful) - Oil 10ml (about 2 tablespoons) - Five-spice salt crispy chicken: Take 150g chicken breast for one person as an example. The chicken should be cut into dice shapes and needs to be fried - 10ml light soy sauce (about 2 tablespoons) - 2.5ml cooking wine (about 0.5 tablespoons) - 5g allspice (about 2 teaspoons) or 2.5-5g thirteen spices (about 1-2 teaspoons) - (optional) cumin powder 1g (about 0.5 teaspoons) - (optional) white pepper 1g (approx. 0.5 teaspoon) - Grilled chicken wings with honey sauce: Take 250g of bone-in chicken wings for one person as an example. Several cuts should be made on the chicken wings. The finished dish is salty and sweet, but the sweetness needs to be roasted - 10ml light soy sauce (about 2 tablespoons) - 2.5ml cooking wine (about 0.5 tablespoons) - 5-15g white sugar (about 2-6 teaspoons, choose according to the sweetness of taste) - Honey/syrup 10-20ml (about 2-4 tablespoon, choose according to the sweetness of the taste. If the white sugar exceeds or equals 10g, it is recommended to add only 10ml) - (optional) 2.5g allspice (about 1 teaspoon. Thirteen spices cannot be used) - Grilled salmon: Take 200g boneless salmon steak for one person as an example. The fish should not be cut and needs to be baked in the oven - 10ml light soy sauce (about 2 tablespoons) - 2.5ml cooking wine (about 0.5 tablespoons) - 10-20g brown sugar (about 4-8 teaspoons, choose according to the sweetness of taste) - Italian balsamic vinegar/Zhenjiang balsamic vinegar 2.5-5ml (about 0.5-1 tablespoon, choose according to the acidity of taste) - Nutmeg powder 2.5g (about 1 teaspoon) - thyme powder 1g (about 0.5 teaspoon) - ginger powder 1g (about 0.5 teaspoon) - rosemary powder 1-2g (about 0.5-1 teaspoon) - (optional) white pepper 1g (about 0.5 teaspoon) - (optional) dried chili powder 2.5-10g (about 1-4 teaspoon, choose according to the spiciness of taste)

Case study: After the lean meat is sliced, add a small amount of light soy sauce, starch and oil and mix well. Let it sit for fifteen minutes before adding it to the pan. The meat will be more tender and non-stick to the pan.

items.title: Steam
body: Method: Steamer: The steamer has a multi-layer structure, and the bottom is used to hold water. The heat of the steam generated after the water is boiled is used to heat the food on the upper layer. Add an appropriate amount of water to the bottom of the steamer - place the food in the upper steamer - put the steamer on the fire to heat Iron pot: If there is no steamer, but only an ordinary iron pot (not a pan), you can place a tripod at the bottom of the pot and pour enough water to achieve an effect similar to a steamer. Add enough water to the bottom of the iron pot - put the trivet - place the food on the trivet - turn on the heat and close the lid

Note: * Since the heat source is water vapor, the bottom of the food in the lower steamer may be soaked with water. This can be avoided by placing a steamer cloth under the food. You can also use chopsticks to create a simple stand for food. * You can use smart devices to set a timer to remind you to turn off the fire to prevent forgetting and causing it to dry out. * When using a steamer to make food, you need to pay attention to the remaining water in the bottom area, especially the iron pot, to avoid drying the pot and causing safety issues. * (Optional) When using an iron pot to steam food, you can place a steaming plate on top of the trivet.

Put the ingredients in the steamer after the water is boiled to ensure that the temperature rises in a short time and the ingredients are heated evenly, thus reducing the risk of aging if the steaming time is too long.
Cover steamed eggs and steamed fish with plastic wrap or a plate, and poke holes for ventilation to prevent water vapor from dripping and damaging the surface smoothness of the finished product.

Adjust the time according to the size of the ingredients. Turn off the heat and simmer for a few minutes before opening the lid. Do not open the lid immediately to avoid the temperature difference causing the ingredients to shrink.

Case study: Weekend Xiao He steamed egg custard, stir the egg liquid with warm water and sieve it, cover it with plastic wrap and make small holes. After the water boils, steam it for ten minutes over medium-low heat, then turn off the heat and simmer for two minutes. The egg custard has a smooth surface without honeycombs, a tender texture, and is very delicious after seasoning.

items.title: Use a microwave
body: What is a Microwave Oven: The microwave oven was invented in 1945 by Percy LeBaron Spencer. While working as a radar systems engineer, he came up with the idea and invention after discovering that the chocolate bar in his pocket began to melt as soon as the radar was turned on. How it works: Microwaves create electromagnetic waves with a frequency of 2.45 billion Hz through a magnetron. This frequency causes the molecules of water and oil to vibrate and generate heat.

Process: Microwave ovens work quite well for many cooking tasks. High heat is suitable for: * [Cooking] Cooking vegetables * [Cooking] Softening hard vegetables with high water content (such as potatoes, onions and artichokes) * [Puffing] Popping snacks such as puffs, papadam, popcorn Medium heat is suitable for: * [Cooking] Seafood (e.g. Microwave black cod with onion and ginger) * [Cooking] Softening meat * [Dehydrating] Drying vegetable and fruit peels * [Dehydrating] Making jerky * [Fried] Crispy spice plants * [Fried] Softened leafy vegetables * [Heated] Reheated leftovers Use low heat for: * [Thawed] Thawed food * [Thawed] Melted butter and chocolate

Notes: * Microwave ovens should not be used to heat water, as this may cause it to boil, which may have a certain impact on your personal safety * Never use a microwave oven to heat eggs! Unless it's a raw egg with the shell removed and the yolk needs to be popped. Because heating will cause the gas inside the egg to expand, causing an explosion. * Whatever your purpose, even if you are curious, you should not microwave whole fruits (e.g. grapes, blueberries, cherry tomatoes) as this may cause them to explode * Since microwaves have a wavelength of 12.2 cm, microwaves heat small objects more slowly than larger objects. Therefore, if the ingredients are very small, it is recommended to heat them together. * Microwaves can only penetrate a few centimeters into food, so sometimes the outside may be very hot but the inside may still be cold. The solution is to put the ingredients and a small amount of liquid into a sealed bag, or put it in a bowl and cover it with plastic wrap, so that enough steam is generated in the container to make up for the shortcomings of uneven cooking in microwave ovens. * Tips: When opening the sealed bag, be careful of steam spurting out * Microwaves can only heat objects containing liquid molecules such as water and oil, so neither plastic wrap nor sealed bags will be heated by microwaves. * Metal can reflect microwaves without being heated. Please avoid using containers with gold edges or metal patterns to avoid container rupture caused by uneven heating. Be sure to use porcelain, glass containers or microwave-safe baking pans.
Sprinkle a small amount of water before heating the leftover rice and cover it loosely, leaving a gap for ventilation. Heat it in two steps over medium heat so that it does not taste dry and hard.
Choose defrost mode or low heat when thawing meat, and turn it over every two minutes until the edges become soft to avoid overcooking the outer layer.
When covering with microwave-safe cling film, do not stick food on it and leave ventilation holes; when taking it out, lift it from the edge to prevent steam burns.

Case study: Add eggs and chopped green onions to leftover rice and mix well. Microwave on high for two minutes, stirring once in the middle. The texture will be close to that of fried rice without the need to use a frying pan.

items.title: Use an air fryer
body: What is an air fryer: An air fryer is an electronic cooker that uses air instead of the original hot oil to heat food to cook it, so that the food can achieve a similar deep-fried effect without touching oil. Working method: The air fryer uses the heater above to generate high-temperature hot air, allowing the hot air to circulate and convection around the food, quickly heating the oil in the food itself, taking away the moisture of the food, producing a deep-frying effect, and creating a crispy feeling similar to fried food. Advantages: * Since there is no need to add cooking oil, the intake of cooking oils containing high amounts of fat and calories can be significantly reduced. * The high-speed circulating hot air dehydrates the food, making the surface golden and crispy, making the food crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. * Easy to operate and friendly to newcomers.

Procedure: * Place the air fryer on a stable, flat and level insulated surface. * Take out the frying pan, put the ingredients into the frying basket and slide the frying pan into the appliance. * Modify the preset temperature and turn the knob to adjust the cooking time. * After adjusting the cooking time, the product will start cooking and wait for the cooking to be completed when the timer rings. * Pour all the food in the frying basket into a bowl or plate. Always remove the basket containing the ingredients from the frying pan being used as hot oil or grease may remain on the bottom of the frying pan.

Precautions: * When using an air fryer, you should be careful not to set the temperature too high (try to be within 120°C, preferably no more than 168°C), and the cooking time should not be too long (about 10 minutes) to avoid generating too much harmful ingredient acrylamide. * Reduce the use of air fryers to cook starchy foods, such as potatoes, bread, fried dough sticks, etc., which can reduce acrylamide intake accordingly. Relatively speaking, air fryers are suitable for cooking foods with higher fat or moisture content, such as meat and vegetables. * During use, the air inlet at the top and the air outlet at the back cannot be blocked. If you cover it with your hands, you may be burned by the hot air. * The temperature difference of different brands of fryers can reach ±10℃. It is recommended to reduce the time by 10% for the first time and then adjust gradually.

Cooking suggestions: Common foods: | Food name | Temperature (℃) | Time (minutes) | Method steps | |---------|---------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------| | French fries | 200 | 15-20 | 1. Frozen French fries do not need to be defrosted, spray a small amount of oil on the surface; - 2. Lay the frying basket flat (without overlapping) and shake it every 5 minutes; - 3. Adjust to 210℃ for the last 2 minutes for coloring. | | Chicken wings | 180 | 18-22 | 1. Cut the chicken wings and marinate them with light soy sauce, cooking wine, oyster sauce, and minced garlic for 1 hour; - 2. Lay the frying basket flat and brush the surface with honey water; - 3. Bake for 10 minutes, then turn over and continue grilling. | | Fish | 180-190 | 12-15 | 1. Cut both sides of the fish body and marinate it with ginger slices, green onions, salt and cooking wine for 20 minutes; - 2. Brush the surface of the fish with oil and place tin foil on it to prevent sticking; - 3. Turn over once halfway through. | | Steak | 200 | 8-12 | 1. Bring the steak to room temperature and sprinkle salt, black pepper and olive oil on both sides; - 2. Preheat the air fryer for 5 minutes, put the steak in and grill it according to the thickness (4-6 minutes on each side). | | Beef cubes | 180 | 15-18 | 1. Cut the beef into 2cm cubes and marinate with light soy sauce, starch, and black pepper for 30 minutes; - 2. Lay the frying basket flat and bake for 10 minutes, turning once; - 3. Add onions and colored peppers and grill together. | | Pork chops | 175-185 | 16-20 | 1. Use the back of a knife to pat the pork chops loosely, marinate with soy sauce, garlic powder, and five-spice powder for 40 minutes; - 2. Spray oil on the surface and line it with baking paper; - 3. Turn over halfway and brush with marinade. | | Egg tarts | 170-180 | 12-15 | 1. After defrosting the egg tart crust, pour in the homemade egg liquid (milk + light cream + sugar + egg yolk); - 2. There is no need to preheat the fryer, just bake until the tart crust is golden and the center is slightly charred. | | Cake | 160 | 25-30 | 1. Line a 6-inch mold with greased paper and pour cake batter (7 minutes full); - 2. Bake slowly at low temperature, insert a toothpick and it will be done if there is no sticking; - 3. Invert and cool to prevent collapse. | | Pizza | 180-190 | 8-12 | 1. Frozen pizza does not need to be defrosted, you can sprinkle additional cheese; - 2. Place tin foil on the pizza to prevent leakage, and bake until the cheese becomes charred; - 3. Homemade pizza needs to bake the bottom of the pizza for 5 minutes before toppings. | | Peanuts | 160 | 10-12 | 1. Soak raw peanuts for 5 minutes and drain; - 2. Spray a small amount of oil + salt and mix well; - 3. Spread in a single layer and shake every 3 minutes. | Operation points: 1. Key points for pre-processing - Meat needs to be fully thawed and surface moisture wiped dry (steaks/pork chops are recommended to be brought back to room temperature) - Frozen food (french fries/pizza) can be cooked directly, but shaking/turning frequency needs to be increased 2. Anti-stick skills - Sticky foods such as fish/cakes are recommended to be lined with baking paper or tin foil - Onion slices/lemon slices can be placed at the bottom of the frying basket to enhance the flavor and isolate the juice 3. Color control - increase the temperature in the last 2-3 minutes 10-20℃ can make the surface crispier (applicable to French fries/chicken wings) - Covering the surface of tarts/cakes with tin foil can prevent excessive scorching 4. Doneness detection - Meat: press with chopsticks, if firm, it is fully cooked, soft and elastic, it is medium-cooked - Cake: if a toothpick is inserted into the center and no batter sticks, it means it is done.

Wipe the surface of the ingredients as dry as possible, drain off the excess juice after marinating, and lay them in a single layer without stacking them, so that they can be heated evenly and crispy.
Turn over or cradle once in the middle. Thin ingredients will shorten the time. Thick ingredients will be cooked at low temperature first and then colored at high temperature.
Don’t fill the frying basket too full, leaving space for hot air circulation; clean the frying basket while it’s hot afterward, so that oil stains can be removed more easily.

Case: I made chicken wings for my family in the evening. I dried and marinated the chicken wings and put them in a single layer in the frying basket. I baked them at 200℃ for 12 minutes, flipped them over and baked them for another 8 minutes. When they came out of the pan, the skin was golden and crispy and the inside was cooked.

items.title: Food Safety
body: Poisoning: The following foods are at risk of poisoning: * Unripe green tomatoes * Underripe kidney beans (kidney beans), cowpeas (beans), white beans * Sprouted potatoes (yams), sweet potatoes (sweet potatoes), peanuts * Improper handling/underripe daylilies can cause colchicine poisoning * Raw soy milk * Fungus soaked for too long (not just fungus, all fungi soaked for too long are at risk of poisoning) * Uncooked animal offal * Unknown mushrooms or undercooked mushrooms (There is a proverb: red umbrellas, white stems, lie down together after eating. Generally speaking, the more beautiful the mushrooms, the more dangerous.) * ... (welcome to add) Acidic food stored and cooked in aluminum containers for a long time also has the risk of poisoning, such as * sauerkraut * dried bamboo shoots * tomato paste * lemon juice * braised meat * soy sauce and pickles * ... (welcome to add)

Allergies: The following are common allergic foods (note: allergic reactions are generally lifelong): Adults: * Shrimp, crab, shellfish (eating stale seafood can lead to bacterial growth) * Peanuts * Nuts * Fish Children: * Peanuts * Nuts * Eggs * Milk (mainly intolerance to the A1 protein in milk) * Wheat and soybeans

Salmonella infection: Salmonella is more common in foods of animal origin, including vegetables that may also contain salmonella due to fecal contamination. The following foods pose a risk of salmonella infection: * Undercooked eggs * Undercooked meat * Unpasteurized milk

Aflatoxin: Aflatoxin is often produced by several other molds such as Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus in moldy grains, such as rice, beans, peanuts, etc. It is by far the strongest carcinogen. It only begins to decompose when heated above 280°C, so its structure is not easily destroyed by general heating. The following foods have the risk of causing aflatoxin poisoning: * Rotten peanuts * Rotten rice * Rotten corn Note that the above foods also include their corresponding products, such as rice flour and cornmeal; Peanut seedlings (germinated peanuts) that have been safely cultivated and produced can be considered safe and edible.

3-Nitropropionic acid: 3-nitropropionic acid is produced by Arthrospora cane, a fungus commonly found in sugar cane and coconuts. The main manifestation of poisoning is damage to the central nervous system. Symptoms in the acute phase include vomiting, dizziness, paroxysmal convulsions, lateral gaze, coma, and even death. The sequelae are mainly extrapyramidal damage. The main symptoms include flexion, torsion, spasm, limb rigidity, and reduced tone at rest. There is currently no specific antidote for this toxin. The following foods pose a risk of 3-nitropropionic acid poisoning: * Red sugar cane * Rotten coconut In addition to visual appearance as a criterion, smell is also an important evaluation criterion. Rotten plants often emit a special smell (lees, sourness, etc.). The best thing to do with food that smells rancid is to throw it away.

Parasites: Parasites can enter the body through the air, drinking water, food and direct contact. If the parasite enters the human circulatory system, it can attack white blood cells on the one hand, and can reach the lungs, liver and other organs on the other hand, or block blood vessels or lymphatic channels, causing diseases such as cirrhosis, portal hypertension, elephantiasis and other diseases. If a human is the intermediate host of pork tapeworm, the parasites can even reach the eyeballs, heart and brain, which can be life-threatening. It is best to ensure that the following foods are completely cooked, otherwise they may leave corresponding parasites in the body: * Field snail: Angiostrongylus * Sashimi: Liver fluke * Eel: Gnathostomata * Bullfrog: Sparganoma mansoni parasite * Pork: Pork tapeworm * Beef surface (you can eat it as long as the surface is cooked): Beef tapeworm

Food safety temperature: By heating food at a sufficient temperature and maintaining it for a certain period of time, the risk of survival of bacteria and parasites can be reduced to a certain extent. Various types of food have different temperature requirements. Cooks should use a kitchen thermometer to measure the core temperature of the food. To measure temperature you should use: Kitchen thermometer Measure the core temperature of food The following are industry standard food safety temperatures: | | Whole piece | Minced meat | Whole | |-----------|------------------------------------------------|-------|-------| | Pork | 71°C | 71°C | | | Poultry | 74°C | 74°C | 85°C | Medium-rare: 71°C; medium-rare: 77°C | 71°C | | | Reheat leftovers | 74°C | | | Based on the latest 2011 USDA standards, food safe cooking temperatures have been updated as follows: | 74°C | 74°C | | Beef/Lamb | 63°C (allow to rest for 3 minutes after removing from heat) | 71°C |

Food and drug combination reactions: The combined use of some foods and drugs can lead to serious safety risks. The following are some behaviors that have safety risks: * Cephalosporins and alcohol * (Welcome to add...)

Case: When making cold cucumbers on weekends, I wash the cutting board and knives first, process the raw and cooked ones separately, and refrigerate the cucumbers for no more than two hours. My family did not suffer from abdominal pain or diarrhea after eating.

items.title: Steam (rice)/stew (use rice cooker/pressure cooker/electric pressure cooker)
body: What is a pressure cooker: A pressure cooker is actually an ordinary pot with a lockable semi-sealed lid. The lid has a valve that can be used to control the pressure in the pot. How it works: The way a pressure cooker works is to allow steam to accumulate in the pot and increase the pressure inside the pot. When the pressure in the pot increases, the boiling point of water also increases, which can cause the cooking temperature of water-containing food to exceed 100°C. Advantages: * Since the actual cooking temperature of the pressure cooker is higher, the cooking time can be significantly reduced. * The high temperature inside the pressure cooker promotes browning and caramelization, producing a unique flavor.

Process: * Put the ingredients and water into the inner pot and close the lid to ensure the pot is sealed and heat. * For tougher ingredients, such as tendons, using a pressure cooker can make it easier to cook them and get a better taste. * Pressure cookers usually have a self-locking valve (float valve). During cooking, as the pressure in the pot increases, the self-locking valve will start and lock, isolating the gas inside and outside the pot, and creating conditions for pressurization in the pot. After the self-locking valve is activated, it will also lock the pot lid to prevent forced opening, which plays a safety role. When cooking, you need to make sure that the self-locking valve is not blocked by foreign objects so that the pressure cooker can work normally. * After switching to the heat preservation state, drain the steam from the pot through the exhaust valve before opening the lid. Notes: * The steam is very hot, so do not touch the exhaust valve. * When cooking liquid food, do not manually exhaust the gas and be careful of splashing (you can put the food into a sealed jar or vacuum packaging bag and then cook it in a pressure cooker). * Manual deflation when cooking some dishes (such as soups) may affect the taste and texture of the food. * Make sure the steam has been exhausted before opening the lid. When opening the lid, do not open it all at once, especially do not open the lid in front of others to avoid steam burns. * After cooking is completed, as the air pressure in the pressure cooker decreases to balance with the outside air pressure, the self-locking valve will release. This can be used as a judgment mark to determine whether the pot lid can be opened. * The sealing of the pressure cooker relies on the sealing rubber ring in the lid. For old pressure cookers, you need to check whether the sealing rubber ring is still effective. * Make sure the rubber ring is completely clean, any particles stuck in it may damage the sealed environment. * Many pressure cookers have a safety line. Materials and liquids should not exceed this line. Too many ingredients and liquids may cause water vapor to burst out and block the exhaust valve, or too much water vapor may splash out and be difficult to clean. * For pressure cookers without safety lines, it is best not to let the water level exceed 2/3 of the pot body. * Do not use a pressure cooker to cook foods that are prone to foaming, such as oatmeal or noodles. Foam may clog steam valves and pressure relief tubes. * During the cooking process, when the pressure valve rises and spits out steam or smoke, it means that the inside of the pressure cooker is over-pressurized, and the pressure valve releases the excess pressure to ensure safety. Although the strong aroma of the ejected steam will bring a high sense of pleasure, firstly, the flavor of the food will be lost, and secondly, excessive pressure may cause the groove of some types of pressure cookers to bend. So when you see steam coming out, reduce the firepower. *tips: Opening the cover from the side is a good choice.
The amount of water for steaming rice is adjusted according to the type of rice. Ordinary rice is about 1:12. Brown rice needs more water and is soaked in advance.

When stewing the meat, blanch it in a pot under cold water and skim off the floating foam before adding it to the pot. The color of the soup will be clearer and the fishy smell will be significantly reduced.

After the pressure cooker is on steam, turn to low heat and time it. It is safer to release the pressure naturally after the pressure is over. Make sure the float valve is completely down before opening the lid.

Case: When steaming rice in a rice cooker, I press the rice cup and add water to the corresponding scale. After soaking for 20 minutes, I start the standard program. After tripping, I simmer for 10 minutes. The rice grains are clearly not raw.

items.title: Oil temperature judgment skills and common temperature and unit conversion tables
items.core: * The oil temperature is between 120°C and 140°C: suitable for soft frying [^1] and smooth frying [^2]. Put the chopsticks into the oil pan. There will be basically no bubbles around, no smoke, no noise, and the oil temperature is calm. * Oil temperature is between 150°C-160°C: the optimal cooking temperature. Put the chopsticks into the oil pan, there will be a little oil bubbles and a slight smoke around it, and the oil will be stirred from all sides to the middle. * The oil temperature is between 160°C-180°C: suitable for coloring and frying. Put the chopsticks into the oil pan, a lot of green smoke will rise, and the oil surface will be calmer. * (Note) It is best to buy an oil temperature gun and use the thermometer with caution. The so-called "several percent oil temperature" in online video tutorials refers to 300°C relative to 100% oil temperature. That is, n becomes the oil temperature T_n = 30n [degree Celsius] temperature conversion formula C = 5/9 *(F - 32) or F = 9/5*C + 32
body: Attached is the oil temperature comparison table: made according to the above description. The error is based on non-professional data. | Celsius °C | Common names | Fahrenheit °F | | :----: | :----: | :----: | | -18±4 | Quickly frozen (frozen) | -0.4±4 | | 4±2 | Fresh | 40±4 | | 30±10 | Normal temperature | 86±18 | 194±18 | 120±10 | 40% | 248±18 | 150±10 | 50% | 302±18 | 180±10 | 60% | 356±18 | 210±10 | 70% | 410±18 | | 240±10 | 80% | 464±18 | | 270±10 | 90% | 518±18 | | 300±10 | 100% | 572±18 | * ^1: Soft frying is a deep-frying method in which small pieces, slices or strips of material are battered, put into an oil pan, and fried until they are about 70% cooked * ^2: For stir-frying, select tender animal raw materials and cut them into shapes such as shreds, slices, dices, strips, etc. with egg whites and starch, spread with warm oil, and pour into a colander to drain away the remaining oil.

When there is no oil temperature gun, insert wooden chopsticks to judge: about 30% to 40% no bubbles around, about 50% to 60% fine bubbles, intensive bubbling indicates that the oil temperature is high.
The "percentage of oil temperature" is converted to 30 degrees Celsius, and 60% is about 180 degrees Celsius. Don't interpret it as an oil pan scale.
Fry and fry in batches to avoid a sudden drop in oil temperature; remove the ingredients and put them on a wire rack to drain the oil. Do not stack them directly on the plate to soften.

Case: When frying the short crispy pork, I used an oil temperature gun to measure the oil temperature of about 160°C and put it in the pan. There were only fine bubbles around the chopsticks. I fried it in batches until it was light yellow and took it out. When I re-fried it, it was crispy on the outside and tender on the inside without absorbing too much oil.

items.title: Sugar-colored stir-fry
items.core: Principle: Sugar melts when exposed to high temperature and takes on different properties after being heated for different times. Take frying 200ml of sugar as an example.
body: Stir-frying in water: 1. Take a pot with a curved bottom or a flat bottom that accounts for less than 1/3 of the area. 2. Add 8g of rock sugar, white granulated sugar or soft white sugar to the pot. Rock sugar is better. If you want the sugar color to be more sweet, you can increase it by about 2g. 3. Add 50ml of 70°C hot water to the pot. 4. Place the pot on the stove 5. If you use a gas stove, adjust the firepower from large to small to the minimum so that the flame range does not exceed the water surface. If you use an induction cooker, turn it to the minimum and be ready to turn off the power. 6. Use a spatula to continuously stir the sugar-water mixture. If it is rock sugar, you can use the back or edge of the spatula to gently tap it until it breaks into pieces to accelerate melting. During this process, if the sugar has not yet melted but has begun to change color, you need to continue adding hot water to 50ml. 7. After all the sugar has melted, the sugar-water mixture will be viscous and transparent and white in color, such as the color of mica. At this time, you should continue to stir. 8. Continue to stir the sugar-water mixture, and the color of the sugar-water mixture will gradually turn white. 9. Continue to stir the sugar-water mixture, and the color of the sugar-water mixture will begin to appear light brown. 10. Continue to stir the sugar-water mixture. The color of the sugar-water mixture will be very brown. 11. Continue to stir the sugar-water mixture. The color of the sugar-water mixture will turn brown and dense bubbles will appear. 12. Continue to stir the sugar-water mixture. The color of the sugar-water mixture turns brown and dense bubbles appear. Larger bubbles appear among the dense small bubbles. 13. Add 150ml of 70°C hot water to the pot. At this time, the liquid in the pot turns dark reddish brown, transparent and clear in color, with a light caramel smell. 14. Pour into a bowl to obtain 200ml of sugar color [!Note] Step 13: It is not recommended to use cold water instead of 70°C. Hot water, because low temperature will cause the sugar to solidify and stick to the pan

Recommanded: 1. Fry with water 2. Fry with water 3. Add 10ml of normal temperature cooking oil to the pot 4. Fry with water, change the sugar-water mixture to sugar-oil mixture, finally add 190ml of hot water, and leave the rest a little

Attached is a description of the status of the syrup and its use: |State|Preparation method|Usage (example)| |:--:|:--:|:--:| |Incompletely melted syrup|Water (oil) stir-fry 8|Frost hawthorn||Completely melted syrup|Water (oil) stir-fry 9|Candied haws of water||Caramel|Water (oil) stir-fry 11 and then naturally cooled|Caramel| When using sugar color to cook food with a small unit volume such as braised pork, you can add the ingredients directly before step 13 and stir-fry quickly until there is no obvious liquid accumulation on the bottom of the pot. Add water at this time, so that the color can be colored faster.
Additional content: If you follow the production process of this guide and find problems or processes that can be improved, please file an Issue or Pull request.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot to fry the sugar over low heat. Keep observing the color after the sugar melts. Light amber is suitable for frosting, and jujube is suitable for braising.
As soon as the color is in place, heat the water along the edge of the pot. Do not add cold water to prevent the syrup from splashing and clumping.
As soon as the sugar becomes smoky or bitter, throw it away and make it again. The bitter taste will enter the dish directly and cannot be covered up by seasonings.

Case: Before making braised pork, I used 200 ml of white sugar and a small amount of water to fry the sugar over low heat. When the color turned into maroon, I immediately heated the water and stirred evenly. After pouring out, the sugar was bright and not bitter, and the meat was evenly colored.

items.title: Excipient tips
items.core: * The order of adding the auxiliary ingredients is basically as follows: put the ginger first, then the onions, garlic, chili peppers, then the dry ingredients (star anise/Sichuan peppercorns/Pepper pepper), and then the dry chili peppers. Each of the above steps can remove unnecessary ingredients from the queue depending on the dish being cooked. * Ginger has the highest water content, which means we need more time to stir out the juice. * If you are using scallions (it is best to clap the scallions twice with a kitchen knife), then I recommend that you add the scallions first and then the minced garlic. If you are using chopped scallions, you can put these two ingredients into the pot together. Note: It is more difficult to extract the juice from the green onions. * If you are making stir-fry dishes, then I recommend that you add the dry ingredients before adding the ginger. This can make the oil more flavorful and make the stir-fry dishes more fragrant. Why don’t you do this for stews and stews? It’s because you may need to stir-fry a lot of auxiliary ingredients, so that the auxiliary ingredients stir-fry for too long, causing the dry ingredients to turn black and bitter. * Put the dried chili pepper at the end because the dried chili pepper can easily turn black due to the temperature of the pot. Just stir-fry the dried chili pepper for a few seconds. * Note: No matter what kind of cuisine you like, frying these ingredients over low heat until golden brown will make the whole dish more fragrant, which is something that seasonings cannot give.
body: Timing of adding salt and salt amount control: * Add salt first for quick-fried dishes, salt amount = total weight of ingredients x 0.9%; * Add salt when meat dishes are cooked, salt amount = (total weight of ingredients + 30mL juice) x (1~1.2%); * Add salt at the end of soup dishes, salt amount = initial water amount x 0.8%. * The total amount of salt per day is not recommended to exceed 5g, refer to WHO

Add the ginger, garlic, and chili pepper to the pot according to the degree of frying resistance. Stir out the water vapor from the ginger first, then add the minced garlic to avoid adding it to the pot too early and becoming bitter.
Crack the scallions with a knife before adding them to the pot, so that the aroma comes out more easily; if you chop the scallions, add them to the pot at the same time as the minced garlic.

Dry ingredients are suitable for short-term sautéing. When the pot temperature is high, add dried chili peppers last. Stir-fry for a few seconds and then add the main ingredients when you smell the aroma.

Case study: When frying shredded potatoes, I first put the chopped green onion and shredded ginger into the pot and stir-fry over low heat until fragrant. Then I added minced garlic and dried chili peppers for a few seconds and immediately added the shredded potatoes. The finished product was fragrant and the chili peppers did not turn black.

items.title: Professional terminology for cooking
items.core: Cooking is the same as learning programming. You must first understand the professional terminology, which is like learning basic grammar. Only through the combination of terms can you complete a dish. [Fried (chǎo)], written in ancient times as "煼(chǎo)", is one of the most basic cooking methods at present; that is, cutting food into small pieces, putting it into an iron wok (huò) (pot) that is heated with oil, quickly stirring it until it is cooked, and then adding seasonings for seasoning. [炝(qiàng)] A cooking method in which after the food is cut, it is "burned" or "soaked" in boiling water or hot oil, and then poured into a wok (pot) with dried chili peppers and peppercorn oil and mixed well. [chuī] refers to the method of cooking food by steaming, boiling, etc. It is often named in Chaozhou cuisine. [boil (zhǔ)] One of the simplest cooking methods; a cooking method that uses an appropriate amount of boiling water or soup and seasonings to cook food in a wok (pot). [Fried (jiān)] Heat an iron wok (pot), put a little oil in it, then place the food flatly in the wok, and use slow heat to heat the oil to make the surface of the food golden brown and cooked. [Bào] A cooking method that uses a hot wok (pot) to heat oil and add an appropriate amount of prepared sauce or soup to quickly cook the small pieces of food in the wok and add aroma. [Fried (zhá)] written in ancient times as "煠(zhá)", is one of the most commonly used cooking methods; it refers to a cooking technique in which food is placed in a large amount of hot oil until it is cooked until crispy. [烚(xiá)] is written as "煠" in ancient times. It is a processing method that uses a large amount of boiling water to cook tough meat on the fire until it is soft and cooked. 【Roll(gǔn)】A processing method that uses a large amount of boiling water to bring out the yǔ flavor of food. [汆(cuān)] Northern cooking term, in ancient times it was "Sichuan"; similar to "游(lù)" in Cantonese cuisine, it is a cooking method in which food processed into pellets or flakes is cooked in boiling water, then scooped up into a bowl, and then added to the boiling soup. 【焯(zhuó)】written as "焯(chāo)" in the north; refers to a cooking method in which food is cut into thin slices, cooked quickly in boiling water, and then dipped in sauce (zhàn) before eating. 【炂(dá)】A processing method in which vegetables are boiled with 槧(jiǎn) water or oil and cooked thoroughly over slow fire to make the finished product soft and keep their green color. [Shabu-shabu (shuàn)] Northern cooking term; a cooking method in which thinly sliced ​​food is cooked in spicy soup and then dipped in sauce. [煀(kuò)] was written as "爩(yù)" in ancient times; it refers to the cooking method of putting food directly into a wok (pot) or a clay pot (pot), adding a large amount of ginger, green onion and other spices, covering it, and using a large amount of spices to make it fragrant and mature. [Baked (jú)] A cooking method that uses hot coarse salt to cook food wrapped in tinfoil or jade paper under sealed conditions. [Stew (mèn)] Northern cooking method; refers to a cooking method in which tough food is put into a wok (pot), an appropriate amount of soup is added, the lid is covered, and the food is cooked over a slow fire until soft and cooked. 【爆(wén)】is close to the "burning" of the northern cooking method, so there is a saying of "Southern Wén and Northern Shao"; it refers to a cooking method in which tough food is put into a wok (pot), an appropriate amount of soup is added, and cooked over a slow fire until soft and cooked. [Stew (huì)] A cooking method in which a variety of meats and vegetables are cooked together in an appropriate amount of soup. [Steaming (zhēng)] A cooking method that uses the heat of water vapor to cook food. [Stew (dùn)] Add water or soup to the food, put it into a covered container, cover it, and then use the heat of water vapor to cook it and get the soup. Northern cuisine refers to a cooking method that uses a large amount of soup and slow fire to cook food until it is soft and cooked. [Kòu] After the food is seasoned and pre-processed, it is neatly placed into a bowl and steamed over water. Then the main ingredients are placed on a plate and then poured with a glass of original juice. [Bao (bāo)] is a method of cooking food by putting it in a large amount of water, placing it on the fire and cooking it slowly to make soup.
