[boil(áo)] is a processing method that uses slow fire for a long time to blend the flavor of the meat into the soup and concentrate the soup. [Kào] A processing or cooking method that uses strong-flavored raw materials and fresh soup, and uses slow fire and a long time to impart umami flavor into another boring main ingredient. 【Simmer(wēi)】A method of embedding charcoal ash in ancient works to make them ripe. Today it refers to the processing method of using ginger, green onions and soup to add flavor to food and eliminate the peculiar smell of the food itself. Northern cuisine also refers to the cooking method in which food and soup are placed in a sealed earthen jar and cooked over a slow fire. [焐(wù)] replaces the ancient meaning of "simmer" and refers to the cooking method in which food is marinated, wrapped in lotus leaves, etc., then wrapped in wet mud or noodles, and placed in charcoal fire to mature. [Baking (hōng)] A cooking method in which snacks or food are seasoned or processed and then placed in an oven to become cooked. [Stir-fry (biān)] is the same as 珏(bì). It is written as "whip" or "fire stool" in old times, which is similar to "篆(rǎn)". It refers to the processing method of putting food into a hot wok (pot) and constantly stir-frying it to slightly dry out the water in the food and remove the unpleasant smell; or a cooking method that enriches the umami flavor and eats it. 【Liū】The northern cooking term is similar to the Cantonese "qiàn", which is a cooking method in which sweet and sour juice is thickened with cornstarch to make the fried food smooth and delicious. [Gēng] One of the ancient cooking methods refers to a cooking method in which food cut into cubes is boiled in boiling soup, and then wet corn starch is added to make the soup become a paste. [Zan (zǎn)] has been written as "splash" or "灒(zàn)", etc., and is divided into "Zuanyou" or "Zuanjiu"; the former refers to the technique of pouring boiling hot oil on steamed food to remove the fishy smell and make it smoother; the latter refers to the technique of pouring Shaoxing wine onto the food being cooked to make the food more "huò". [Blanching (tàng)] refers to the processing method of using boiling water to tighten the skin of meat. Common in the north, it refers to a cooking method in which sliced ​​and diced raw materials are cooked in boiling or spicy soup. [Shao (shāo)] In ancient times, "zhì", Cantonese cuisine refers to the cooking method of cooking food on charcoal fire or open fire. Modern northern cuisine refers to a cooking method in which the juice is slightly dried and the food is cooked through slow fire. [Roasted (kǎo)] Northern cuisine is used to replace the old meaning of "roasted", so there is a saying of "roasted in the south and roasted in the north". It refers to a cooking method in which food is cooked over an open fire. [Lǔ]: A cooking method that uses "marine juice" mixed with light soy sauce and spices to make food cooked or delicious. [Jiàng] A cooking method that uses a large amount of sauce or light soy sauce to add flavor or make it ripe. [Jìn] is a cooking method that uses a large amount of boiling water or soup to cook the food within a certain period of time using the heat of the "chrysanthemum heart". Similar to the "氽(tǔn)" cooking method in the north, that is, after the ingredients are cooked, the soup is poured into the noodles (yǎo) and eaten. 【风(fēng)】A processing method in which the pickled food is hung in a ventilated place all year round and allowed to dry naturally in the shade or in the air. 【La(là)】A processing method in which the pickled food is hung in a ventilated place around the twelfth lunar month and allowed to dry naturally in the shade or in the air. [Smoke (yān)] A cooking method in which tea or spices are ignited in a sealed state to imbue food with its fragrant smoke flavor. [Xūn (xūn)] was originally written as "smoked", and can be divided into "dry smoked" and "wet smoked". "Dry smoked" is similar to "smoke"; "wet smoked" is a cooking method in which flowers or Shaoxing wine are used to add fragrance to food. [Zāo]: A cooking method in which food is put into wine grains to add flavor or ripen it. [zuì]: A cooking method that uses a large amount of soju to enhance the flavor or make it ripe. 【甑(zèng)】Ancient "steaming"; a cooking method in which food is chopped into pieces, seasoned, put into a clay bowl (bō), and then cooked using strong steam. [frozen (dòng)], also known as "crystal", refers to a cooking method in which boiled food is added to agar, pig skin, etc., and then boiled into a soup, and then placed in the refrigerator to freeze and solidify before eating. 【Flying Water】Put food into boiling water and pass it through the water until it is half-cooked and then pick it up quickly, which provides a good cutting-edge and basic processing method for subsequent cooking. [Ice-soaking] A cooking method in which the food is cut into shreds and then quickly put into ice water to make the food crispy. This method originated from Japan. 【Stringing】A cooking method in which after the food is starched and fried, it is put into the melted syrup and mixed well so that the food can be pulled out into thin threads when picked up. [Hanging Frost] A cooking method in which after the food is deep-fried, it is put into the boiled syrup and mixed well to disperse or directly sprinkled with powdered sugar. [Salt and pepper] After the food is fried and cooked and dried, it is then stir-fried and mixed with "salt and pepper" prepared in advance with pepper rice and refined salt. [Oil Soaking] A cooking method that uses a large amount of hot oil to quickly cook food. [Oil draining] is also called "oil dragging", "oil draining" and "oil draining"; it refers to a processing method in which processed raw materials are put into boiling oil and quickly dragged through it to provide cutting-edge and basic processing methods for subsequent cooking. [Flame] A cooking method in which fresh seafood is placed in a glass vessel and cooked using the heat generated by igniting a high degree of white wine. 【啫(zé)啫(zé)】A cooking method in which food, ginger, green onion, etc. are put into a clay pot (pot) that is heated to extremely hot temperatures, so that the food makes a "啫啫" sound and emits aroma. [Skewer] The meat is sliced ​​and marinated, then skewered with bamboo skewers and "soaked" in hot oil before eating. Or the cooking method is to cut the meat into slices, skewer it with an iron skewer, cook it on a charcoal fire, and then sprinkle it with zīran and other seasonings. [Teppan] was originally a Western cooking method; that is, after the food is "oiled", together with onion-based spices and sauces, it is placed on an extremely hot iron plate to cook it and make the food fragrant. [Sauna] Also known as "Stone Cooking", etc., this is a cooking method in which the food is oiled and placed on hot stones (mostly Yuhua stones), then the prepared sauce or soup is poured in, and the steam is used to cook the food or release its aroma. [Jian-seal] Also known as "fried and cooked" in the north, it is generally suitable for a large amount of fish. This is a cooking method that marinates the fish with condiments, then slowly frys it in hot oil over a slow fire, and then seals it with gravy (qiàn) to make it more flavorful. [Wo Tie] is a "semi-fried method", which is a cooking method in which the marinated meat is put on the fat with "Wo Tie paste", and "strong wok oil" is used to make the meat crispy on one side and soft on the other. [Tā] is a cooking method in which the pickled food is coated with "egg powder slurry", and the food is fried first and then deep-fried, and then the seasoned soup is added and cooked thoroughly. [Soft-fried] is a "semi-fried method", which is a cooking method in which the marinated meat is mixed with "egg powder slurry", fried first and then deep-fried to make the meat cooked, and then cut into pieces and topped with sauce. [Egg Omelette] The meat is first pre-cooked by using the method of "flying water" or "soaking in oil", then put it into the seasoned egg slurry and mix well, and then fry the bottom of the meat and egg slurry over a slow fire until golden brown. [Gillette] is the transliteration of English CUTLET; a cooking method in which the food is coated with egg paste, coated with bread crumbs, and then deep-fried in hot oil. This method originated from Western cooking. [Crisp frying] After the food is marinated with condiments, it is first coated with wet flour slurry, then patted with dry cornstarch, then fried in hot oil, and then dredged in sauce. [Hot pot] is also known as "shabu-shabu" and "beaten stove" in Guangdong. It is a method of "slicing" or "cutting" fresh meat into thin slices, or meat tarts into balls, balls, stuffings, etc., and delivers them to the guests together with vegetables, etc., and allows the guests to cook them in boiling water or soup. [Steam Pot] A cooking method in which the meat is marinated, together with the medicinal materials, put into a special "gas pot" where the seasoning soup is boiled, and then simmered and eaten. 【Cold Salad】Cooking method of cutting cooked food or fruits and vegetables, adding seasonings and mixing evenly. [Yu Sheng] A cooking method that removes the blood from fresh aquatic products, then cuts them into thin slices, mixes them with shredded ginger, green onion, crispy chips, lemon shreds, etc., and then dips it in light soy sauce and eats it. [Sashimi] is originally a Japanese cooking method. It originally refers to raw meat slices. It is used in Chinese cuisine to refer to the cooking method of removing the scales and purifying the blood of fresh aquatic products or seafood, cutting it into thin slices, dripping lemon juice, and dipping it into spicy Japanese mustard (jiè). [Bamboo tube] In ancient times, it was called "緷(zēng)", which refers to the cooking method of using bamboo tubes as utensils, and then "roasting", "burning", "steaming", and "stewing (dùn)" to cook the food. [Honey juice] refers to a cooking method that turns sugar, honey, maltose, etc. into a thick juice, adds processed raw materials, and uses methods such as "boiling" and "steaming" to make the texture soft and waxy (nuò), the sweetness penetrates, and the sugar juice is moistened. [Blanching (chāo) water], also known as "water out", is a method of placing raw materials in a pot of boiling or cold water for preliminary cooking. [Over-oiling] A method of preliminarily cooking cooking ingredients using oil as the heat transfer medium. Small raw materials passing through warm oil are also called "lubricating oil"; large raw materials passing through warm oil are also called "oil leaking". 【Paste】The process of coating raw materials evenly with a layer of paste before cooking. [Sizing] A process in which starch, eggs, salt, etc. are mixed with raw materials to coat the outer layer of the raw materials with a thin layer of slurry. [Shangjin] A processing method that adds refined salt, water, starch and other auxiliary materials to animal raw materials processed into ant (róng) mud (ní) mince (mò) and stirs them repeatedly to achieve a bright color, tender meat, and a state that does not sink or fall apart when soaked in water. 【Gōu 芡(qiàn)】A process in which a starch solution is added to the pot during the cooking process to make the dish soup have a certain consistency. Also known as "绡", "芡", "勡(lǒng)芡(qiàn)". 【Warm oil】commonly known as 30% to 40%, the temperature is generally 70℃~100℃. [Hot oil] is commonly known as 50% to 60% oil, and the temperature is generally 110℃~170℃. 【Wangyou】commonly known as 70% to 80%, the temperature is generally 180℃~220℃. [Sliding pan] Heat a pan, pour a little oil on it, slide it all over, and then pour out the oil. [Soy pot], also known as "frying pot", refers to a method of putting ginger, green onions, minced peppers or other fragrant seasonings into hot base oil, stir-frying them in the pot until they are fragrant, and then adding the ingredients in a timely manner. [High soup], also known as "clear soup", "upper soup" and "top soup", refers to a soup made from pork bones, chicken bones, duck racks, minced meat heads and other raw materials, and then mixed into a thin paste with unsalted chicken or meat mince to make it as clear as water, rich and fresh in taste. [Milk Soup] Also known as "white soup", it is a milky white soup made by simmering raw materials with water.
body: When you see "blanch water", prepare boiling water and ice water first. After blanching the vegetables, they can be kept crisp and green by passing them through ice water. After blanching the meat, rinse off the foam.
The "lubricant" is suitable for shredded pork and fish fillets. Control the oil temperature to be warm, quickly spread it out until it changes color, take it out, and then season it.
Before "thickening", stir the starch water evenly, pour a small amount along the edge of the pot, and turn it while pouring. The soup will stop with a spoon.

Case study: To make a dish of shredded pork with green pepper, I first sauté the shredded pork with oil, then sauté the ginger and garlic in a hot pan, add the green pepper and stir-fry quickly, then add the sauce and mix well. The dish is made with smooth and tender shredded pork and crispy green pepper.
